author: skyyplayz
body:
## Root cause

Three Paperclip agent worktrees were committed to the repo as gitlink objects (mode `160000`) under `.claude/worktrees/`:

- `.claude/worktrees/agent-a367b280a95e585c5`
- `.claude/worktrees/agent-a55d02d6a477e2ede`
- `.claude/worktrees/agent-a5a59f56ed27867aa`

When `actions/checkout@v4` runs `git submodule status`, it sees these gitlink objects as unregistered submodules (no `.gitmodules` file exists). This triggers an error:

```
fatal: no submodule mapping found in .gitmodules for path '.claude/worktrees/agent-a367b280a95e585c5'
Bad Submodules found, removing existing files
```

Git then forces a full repo recreation (`git clean -ffdx` removes all node_modules/caches), then `actions/setup-node@v4` fails because the runner's workspace is now in a corrupted/unexpected state. This cascades into shards 2, 3, and 4 all failing at "Set up Node.js" — never reaching actual test execution.

Shard 1 happened to run on a runner that had a different cached state (or wasn't affected), which is why it passed while 2/3/4 failed.

## Fix

- `git rm --cached .claude/worktrees/agent-*` — removes the 3 committed gitlinks from the index
- Add `.claude/` to `.gitignore` — prevents recurrence when future agent worktrees are created inside the repo root

## Why CI will be green

- **build-linux**: no app code changed; only `.gitignore` and removal of gitlink index entries
- **build-macos**: on-demand only, non-blocking
- **ci (E2E shards)**: the gitlink submodule false-positive is gone; `git submodule status` will be clean; `actions/checkout@v4` will not trigger repo recreation; caches restore normally; Node.js setup succeeds; E2E tests run as expected

## Tests

No test changes — this is a pure CI infrastructure fix. The fix is verified by the root-cause analysis of run `28483407047`.

Fixes [SKY-4730](/SKY/issues/SKY-4730).

author: aaronsb
body:
## Summary

agent-ways 1.0.0's installer still **cloned into `~/.claude`**, producing the pre-1.0 in-place shape — so a brand-new 1.0 user landed in exactly the topology 1.0 replaced, then had to migrate off it. This reworks `install.sh` to the native 1.0 path, wiring the machinery ADR-144/145 already anticipated (fresh = *materialize the manifest into an empty tree* = `ways reconcile`).

**New flow:** stage app → `$XDG_DATA_HOME/agent-ways`, `make setup`, link binaries onto PATH, `ways reconcile` the projection into `~/.claude` (which also seeds `settings.json` and preserves Claude Code's own files). No new logic — `ways reconcile` already does projection + settings merge.

## Behaviour

| State | Action |
|---|---|
| fresh (empty or CC-only `~/.claude`) | stage → build → reconcile |
| already installed (app dir is our repo) | pull + rebuild + reconcile |
| legacy pre-1.0 in-place clone at `~/.claude` | point to gated `ways migrate` |
| app dir occupied by non-agent-ways | stop (don't clobber) |

Native projection made the old **four-option conflict menu disappear** — an existing `~/.claude` with CC files is no longer a problem to resolve, it's the normal case we project into.

## Validation

Sandbox `HOME`/`XDG` run of the reworked installer:
- ✅ app staged to `$XDG_DATA/agent-ways`
- ✅ `~/.claude` has **no `.git`** (not the in-place shape)
- ✅ `skills`/`agents`/`commands`/`hooks/ways` are symlinks into the app dir
- ✅ `settings.json` seeded via the three-way merge (hooks + 6 ways perms, backup written)

(The sandbox couldn't fetch/build the binary — `gh` auth is broken under an overridden `HOME` — so the reconcile step was validated with a supplied binary. The installer correctly *skips* reconcile and warns when no binary is present, rather than half-installing.)

## Follow-ups (not this PR)

- Binary acquisition for **unauthenticated** fresh installs (`download-ways.sh` uses `gh release view`).
- The `ways` make target leaves a **dangling `bin/ways` symlink** when the build fails (same class as #210).
- Makefile `help` text + the remaining doc/way sweep (`.claude/todo-1.0-path-doc-audit.md`).

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n` clean; sandbox projection verified (no `.git`, symlinked trees, seeded settings)
- [ ] Real fresh install on a clean machine (cube / sandbox with gh auth) to exercise binary fetch

- `docs/PROGRESSION_MODEL.md`

  - Viktig: den erstatter ikke eksisterende `quiz_history`, `knowledge_universe`, `trivia_universe`, `hg_learning_log_v1`, courses/pensum, badges/merits eller profile update-hooks.

- `docs/PLACE_STANDARD.md`

  - Binder stedstandard til eksisterende dataregler, PlaceCard-rundinger, quiz, people, Wonderkammer/leksikon, ruter, Nearby og Spotmeeting.

- `README/README.md`
  - oppdaterer hoved-README med lenker til de tre nye dokumentene.
  - presiserer at de nye dokumentene skal leses sammen med eksisterende kontrakter, ikke overstyre dem.

## Viktig korrigering etter gjennomgang av eksisterende docs

Før dokumentene ble ferdigstilt, ble relevante eksisterende dokumenter lest og innarbeidet:

- `docs/APP_STRUCTURE_INDEX.md`
- `docs/DATA_PRODUCTION_CONTRACT.md`

author: sardark942
body:
Improves the vendor-bio AI assistant on three fronts + fixes a real polish-mode bug found while reading the wiring.

## 1. Better prompts (`src/lib/ai/prompts.ts`)

- **Cliché blocklist** — 14 explicit words: "passionate", "dedicated", "experienced", "professional", "the best", "top-tier", "world-class", "capturing moments", "beautiful memories", "unforgettable", "one-of-a-kind", "tailored to you", "we love what we do", "attention to detail".
- **Structure guidance:** What → Who → one distinctive detail. The third one is what makes bios not sound identical.
- **Anti-example + positive example** teaching what specific-and-warm looks like vs generic-marketplace-copywriting.
- **Cultural context restored** — acknowledges Baazar serves many wedding traditions (Desi/South Asian, Persian, Nigerian, West African, East Asian, Latin, etc.) and tells the AI NOT to assume any one tradition unless the vendor's business name / category / subcategory signals it. Restores specificity lost when brand copy was renamed to "cultural wedding marketplace" in PR #79.
- **Polish prompt tightened** — cut adverbs, cut passive voice, preserve specific facts, never invent. Edit, not rewrite.

## 2. Pipe subcategories through

Cart vendors get bios that name what they actually serve (dessert vs beverage vs appetizer) instead of generic "we sell food" lines. Wired end-to-end: `BioAssistCard` → route zod schema → user-prompt functions.

## 3. Fix broken polish mode 🐛

While reading the wiring: `BioAssistCard` was sending `{ mode, currentBio, businessName, category }` but the API's zod schema only reads `draft` (field names got out of sync). Zod strips unknown keys → route received `draft = undefined` → polish check always false → **every 'Polish with AI' click ran the DRAFT prompt** and generated a fresh bio, ignoring the vendor's existing text.

Card now sends `draft: currentBio`. Polish mode fires as intended.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green (typecheck + lint + unit + build)
- [ ] Test contract preserved (`You write short, warm vendor bios` + `polish vendor bios` substrings)
- [ ] Manual smoke: cart vendor draft names actual cart types + no cliché words
- [ ] Manual smoke: existing bio → Polish → AI edits it rather than replacing wholesale (previously broken)

author: samuelbharti
body:
## Genome viewer (igv.js)

Adds the **`igv`** component: an embeddable interactive genome browser backed by [igv.js](https://github.com/igvteam/igv.js).

**Library:** `igv` **3.8.3** (added via `pnpm --filter @bioviz/components add igv`; no new `allowBuilds:` entry required). The bundle is ~1.5 MB — expected and acceptable for a full genome browser.

### Config contract (config-driven, not columnar)
igv.js streams and tiles remote indexed files (BAM/CRAM, bigWig, VCF, BED, ...) itself, so there is **no binary transport** — data flows entirely through the browser config as URLs. The `data` channel is unused (`setData` is a no-op).

Options (camelCase keys, identical across JS / R / Python):

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `config` | A full igv.js browser config (`{ genome\|reference, locus, tracks: [...] }`). When present it is passed through as-is and the convenience fields are ignored. |
| `genome` | Genome id (default `"hg38"`), used when `config` is absent. |
| `locus` | Initial locus string / gene symbol. |
| `tracks` | Array of igv.js track configs, used when `config` is absent. |

The pure `assembleConfig(options)` helper builds the config from convenience fields (or passes `config` through), omitting empty values so igv.js applies its own defaults. It lives in `igv-config.ts` (free of the igv import) so it is unit-testable headless.

### Async lifecycle
- `createIgv(el, {options})` returns a `BiovizInstance` **synchronously**, then kicks off `igv.createBrowser(el, config)` (which returns `Promise<Browser>`) asynchronously.
- `setOptions` with a new `locus` calls `browser.search(locus)`; a locus requested before the browser resolves is **buffered** and replayed once the promise settles. New entries in `tracks` are additively loaded via `browser.loadTrack`.
- `resize()` nudges igv.js via `igv.visibilityChange()` (igv tracks its own container size); it is a no-op until the browser is ready.
- `exportSVG()` returns `browser.toSVG()` once live, else `null`.
- `destroy()` calls `igv.removeBrowser(browser)` and clears the element; a `destroyed` guard tears down a browser whose `createBrowser` promise resolves after destroy (no leak).

Note: `igv`'s `main` field is a UMD bundle without a `default` export, so the runtime value is imported from `igv/dist/igv.esm.js` (with a local `igv-esm.d.ts` remapping types to the package root); esbuild then bundles a proper default export.

### Wrappers
- **R:** `igv(genome = "hg38", locus = NULL, tracks = list(), config = NULL, ...)` + Shiny bindings `igvOutput()` / `renderIgv()`. Config is assembled into the options list.
- **Python:** `IGV(genome="hg38", locus=None, tracks=None, config=None, ...)`.
- **Dev demo:** `dev/main.ts` `igv` entry — hg38 at `chr8:127,736,588-127,739,371` with a public ENCODE bigWig track.

### Shared-file edits (appended, sorted)
`packages/components/src/lib/index.ts`, `packages/components/dev/main.ts`, `python/src/bioviz/__init__.py`. Everything else is new files. Generated `man/igv.Rd`, `man/igv-shiny.Rd` and `NAMESPACE` are committed.

### Verification (all pass)
- `pnpm install && pnpm dist` — builds + syncs (igv umd/anywidget bundles ~1.5 MB).
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" typecheck` — clean.
- `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" test` — 9 passed (5 igv `assembleConfig` cases + 4 volcano).
- `roxygen2::roxygenise("r/bioviz")` + `devtools::test("r/bioviz")` — PASS 22.
- `pytest -q` (python `.venv`) — 9 passed (4 new igv).

body:

## Problem
On the active workout screen, every exercise section rendered its own full set-input card. With several exercises added, multiple "Log Set" buttons and weight/reps fields stacked on screen — crowded, and the extra inputs were "not always wanted".

## Change
Only one exercise's set-input is expanded at a time.

- **Move to the next exercise → finishes the last:** adding an exercise expands it and collapses the previously expanded one.
- **Collapsed exercises** show a compact accent-soft **Add Set** button; tapping it expands that exercise (collapsing any other).
- **Close button:** the expanded card gains a small collapse control (top-right) that hides the input and dismisses the keyboard — "finish log set" via a close button.

Behaviour applies to standalone and superset exercise sections. Logged-set chips and the "Last: …" summary remain visible when collapsed, so nothing is hidden except the entry fields.

## Tests
- New widget tests: newly added exercise is the only one expanded; tapping **Add Set** moves expansion (never stacks two inputs); tapping collapse leaves all exercises collapsed.
- Full suite: 890 tests pass. `dart analyze` clean; formatted.

author: lionsr
body:
## Summary

This PR routes explicit large-N HDF5 `schedule` metadata through the existing multi-frequency schedule parser before the bond-dimension summarizer prints an evidence row.

Valid output is unchanged. Missing schedule metadata still displays as `unknown` for legacy files. The behavioral change is that an explicit malformed schedule value, such as `reverse`, now raises an `ArgumentError` instead of being treated as an unrecognized non-deterministic schedule with `n/a` period and detuning-coverage fields.

## Motivation

The multi-frequency schedule is part of the physical protocol: it determines which detuning is applied at each completed cycle. The allowed values already have a single source of truth in `src/multi_frequency_schedules.jl` (`round_robin`, `descending`, and `random`). The large-N summarizer should use that same vocabulary when reading HDF5 metadata.

Closes #612 and contributes to the large-N evidence hygiene tracked in #146.

## Validation

- `julia --project=. --startup-file=no test/test_multi_frequency.jl`
- `julia --project=. --startup-file=no test/test_largeN_bond_summary_script.jl`
- `git diff --check`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Validation-only change in a reporting script plus stricter parser errors; no simulation or auth paths affected.
> 
> **Overview**
> Large-N bond-dimension summaries now treat explicit HDF5 **`schedule`** metadata as multi-frequency protocol names by routing values through **`parse_multi_frequency_schedule`** (same vocabulary as **`src/multi_frequency_schedules.jl`**: `round_robin`, `descending`, `random`).
> 
> **Unchanged:** missing schedule still shows **`unknown`** for legacy files; valid schedules still print as before.
> 
> **Changed:** malformed explicit values (e.g. **`reverse`**) or wrong types (e.g. numeric **`7`**) raise **`ArgumentError`** instead of being summarized as an unrecognized schedule with **`n/a`** period/coverage fields. The parser’s fallback method now rejects non-Symbol/non-string inputs with a clear error listing allowed schedules.

author: krasforge
body:
## What

Pushes the v1.5 external-state policy inward per `docs/architecture/orthogonal-persistence-v2.md` section 6. In-flight DMA buffers and non-drainable IPC/network endpoints cannot be replayed across a power cut, so they are severed on restore with a defined error and the owner re-establishes them.

Closes #146.

## Why an endpoint layer

Not every non-persistable resource is a file descriptor. An in-flight DMA mapping or an IPC/network endpoint is its own kernel object. v1.5 severed the fd-flags layer (#128); v2 adds an endpoint layer that severs those resources directly, plus the reconnection contract the design calls for.

## What is added

New `extstate_endpoint_t` (kind, flags, owner pid, generation) and its ops:

- **persistable**: thin wrapper over the kind classification (DMA / device / socket / pipe do not survive; a file-backed mapping would).
- **sever / sever_all**: restore-time transition. Severs open non-persistable endpoints, idempotent, so a process's DMA mappings and IPC endpoints are reported severed and their next use returns a clean `EXTSTATE_SEVERED`.
- **status / needs_reconnect**: what the owner observes, mirroring the socket reconnect path of #128.
- **reconnect** (the reconnection contract): after the owner re-establishes the resource out of band it calls `reconnect`, which clears the severed state, marks it reconnected + open, and bumps a generation counter so stale references elsewhere can detect the endpoint was rebuilt. A re-sever on a later checkpoint clears the reconnected flag; a double reconnect is a safe no-op.

This lands in the dependency-free policy core, so it stays host-testable and builds unchanged in the freestanding kernel.

## Testing

The existing extstate unit test gains a DMA/IPC endpoint section and a reconnection-contract section: a checkpoint taken with an in-flight DMA mapping restores with the mapping severed (the acceptance criterion), then reconnects cleanly and can be re-severed by a later checkpoint. All checks pass. The module compiles clean freestanding and the end-to-end persistence demo still passes.

No new build wiring, since the module and its CI test invocation are already in place.

Depends on #118/#128 (external-state policy) and #143 (re-attach framework, merged).

author: rennf93
body:
Stacks on #36 (B3.1). Closes out the B3 precision arc. Retarget to master once #36 merges.

## Result (harness, expanded 56-sample benign corpus)
- **fp_rate: 0.125 -> 0.000** — every benign category now clean, including the pre-existing `SELECT…FROM`-in-prose (0.67) and the 4 FP vectors Phase B introduced.
- **detection_rate: 0.8568 (held exactly)** — zero recall loss; the ratchet floor was the guardrail.

## How
- **`SELECT…FROM` corroboration scoring:** its weight drops to 0.5 (via B3.1's override map); two new 0.5-weight signals (`SELECT *`, a `WHERE <op>` clause) push real SQLi back over the 1.0 threshold. `SELECT * FROM users` and `… WHERE id=1` still flag; "select items from the catalog" no longer does.
- **Surgical tightening:** ORDER BY requires a terminator; DDL requires the `;` separator; ERB requires dangerous content (not `@user.name`); NoSQL split into always-dangerous operators (`$where`/`$regex`/`$type`/`$exists`/…) vs comparison operators gated on injection-shaped values (`""`/`null`/`{`/`[`), so `{"$gt": 5}` is clean while `{"$ne":null}`/`{"$where":…}` still flag.
- **Expanded benign corpus** (+40 realistic samples: keyword-bearing prose, legit Mongo/JSON, template docs, code comments, URL params) — the FP measurement instrument.

## Verification
358 tests pass (full detection + sync-mirror + attack-sim ratchet). 13 new FP-reduction unit tests pin each fix in both directions (attack flagged, benign near-miss clean). ruff/format/vulture clean; async/sync byte-identical.

## Note
One over-reach caught mid-work by the ratchet: value-gating `$type` dropped the `{"$type":"string"}` seed (recall 0.92->0.68); fixed by moving diagnostic operators to the always-dangerous group. Recall restored to 0.8568 exactly. No API/route changes.

author: paulalbert1
body:
Visual polish for the People search evidence rows (under the existing `SEARCH_EVIDENCE_REASON_COUNTS` flag, #1366 — staging-on / prod-off). **Presentational only; no new flag.**

### What changed
Two commits:

1. **Per-row polish** (`c3928023`, prior): brighter/distinct "Also matched" dots, category-colored lesser labels, dotted underline scoped to the expanded-MeSH-concept flavors, lighter primary lead + count, subtitle reword, dashed-divider dropped.

2. **Collapse hybrid** (this PR's new work): the "Also matched" group now collapses by default to **one summary line** — a colored dot + category label per secondary, **no counts and no entities** — with a far-right chevron that expands it to the full lesser rows.

### Why no counts on the summary
The secondary counts mix denominators (a "4 of 98 publications" concept vs a "9 of 29 grants" funding tag), so an un-denominated count line inverts real strength. The collapsed line is category-only; the card's one honest count stays the primary's single-denominator fraction.

### Behavior
- Fires only for **≥2 secondaries**; a lone secondary still renders bare under the divider (unchanged).
- Inline labels cap at **4** with a `+N` tail so the line can't wrap.
- The umbrella chevron is far-right (`ml-auto`) to read as distinct from the primary's content-width rep-papers chevron.
- Funding's demoted row is included in the summary even though it's rendered separately on the card.

### Tests
- Full vitest suite: **6380 passed**. The one failure (`edit-page.test.tsx`) is a pre-existing Radix Avatar / `FakeImage` mock mismatch in the shared `node_modules` — unrelated to this diff (that test imports none of these files).
- Added: collapsed-by-default (summary shown, entities/counts/disclosures hidden) + expand-reveals-full-rows. Updated the existing demote-Funding test to expand the umbrella first.

### Rollout note
Deploying this branch to staging rolls the image #1366 owns — coordinate timing before `gh workflow run deploy.yml --ref ui/evidence-rows-polish -f env=staging`. No flag deploy needed.

Review only — do not merge.

author: diaquas
body:
## Why

The REQ:IQ listener's singleton guard was a **check-then-write** on the pid file:

```php
if (file_exists($pidFile)) { ...exit if /proc/$old exists... }
file_put_contents($pidFile, getmypid());
```

That has a race window. Two starts firing close together both pass the "is it running?" check (neither has written its pid yet) and then **both run**. The plugin now has several start paths that can fire nearly simultaneously during setup — enable, install hook, the once-a-minute watchdog cron, the new key-save auto-enable, and the REQ:IQ page self-heal — so the race became reachable.

**Duplicate listeners are corrosive.** Each one:
- POSTs its own `seconds_played` every beat, so the cloud's `now_playing_started_at` is overwritten with slightly different values → the viewer's now-playing countdown **jumps around**;
- acts on the same request directive → the requested song is **double-inserted**, and inserts racing against each other cause **stray playlist jumps**;
- drains and executes the one-shot transport command → commands run **twice**.

## What

Replace the pid-file check with an **exclusive, non-blocking `flock`** held for the process lifetime. `flock` is atomic at the OS level, so a second instance can never slip through no matter how many start paths race — it just fails the lock and exits. The pid file is still written (the plugin UI reads it) and cleaned up on exit; the lock file is intentionally never unlinked (the lock is by open fd, not by path).

Bumps the plugin to **1.2.2**.

## Operator note

This prevents *future* duplicates. A box that already has duplicate listeners running (from 1.2.0/1.2.1) needs them cleared once — stop them all and let one restart (e.g. `pkill -f reqiq_listener.php`, or toggle REQ:IQ off/on on the plugin page, or reboot FPP).

author: valardragon
body:
## Motivation

Semantic block verification near the chain tip can queue proof/signature batch work and then wait for the global `MAX_BATCH_LATENCY` before the underlying crypto batch starts. Lowering that latency globally would also affect mempool behavior, so this PR adds a targeted block-verification flush instead.

## Solution

- Add `Batch::flush()` to queue an explicit flush command on the existing batch worker.
- Add `Fallback::primary()` so consensus code can flush the primary batched service without changing fallback verification behavior.
- Register each semantic block verification batch in `zebra-consensus::primitives`, keyed by the existing per-block shared `known_outpoint_hashes` `Arc`.
- Mark each block transaction once its async checks have had an initial poll, then flush initialized Ed25519, Sapling, and Halo2 batch services when all transactions in the block have reached that boundary.
- Keep block safety unchanged: the block verifier still awaits all transaction verifier futures before calculating block totals and committing the block.

### Tests

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p tower-batch-control --test ed25519 batch_flushes_on_explicit_flush`
- `cargo test -p zebra-consensus primitives::tests`
- `cargo test -p tower-batch-control --test ed25519`
- `cargo check -p zebra-consensus -p tower-batch-control -p tower-fallback --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy -p zebra-consensus -p tower-batch-control -p tower-fallback --all-targets -- -D warnings`

### Specifications & References

None.

### Follow-up Work

- Monitor whether future transaction verifier changes start using additional shared batch services, such as RedJubjub or RedPallas, and add them to the targeted flush helper if needed.

### AI Disclosure

- [ ] No AI tools were used in this PR
- [x] AI tools were used: OpenAI Codex for implementation, tests, validation, and PR description.

### PR Checklist

- [x] The PR title follows [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format: `type(scope): description`
- [x] The PR follows the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

author: stoltemberg
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `errno.EINVAL` (22) to `_PEER_GONE_ERRNOS` in `tui_gateway/transport.py`. On Windows, detached stdout raises `OSError(22, 'Invalid argument')` instead of POSIX `EPIPE`. Without `EINVAL` in the set, this was re-raised as a fatal error causing WebSocket 1011 crash loops with 28+ reconnections in 10 minutes.

## Related Issue

Fixes #55119

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tui_gateway/transport.py`: Add `errno.EINVAL` to `_PEER_GONE_ERRNOS` frozenset with comment explaining the Windows detached-stdout case
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_transport.py`: NEW — 10 tests covering:
  - EINVAL, EPIPE, ECONNRESET, EBADF, ESHUTDOWN presence in _PEER_GONE_ERRNOS
  - frozenset immutability
  - StdioTransport.write() behavior with EINVAL, EPIPE, ENOSPC, and success cases

## How to Test

1. Run `python -m pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_transport.py -v` — all 10 tests should pass
2. On Windows: launch TUI gateway, detach stdout (e.g. close terminal) — should see clean disconnect instead of WebSocket 1011 crash loop
3. On POSIX: no behavioral change (EINVAL was already not raised for pipe scenarios)

## Summary

Closes issue #10's acceptance criteria on top of the checkout/payment flow already shipped in PR #6.

- **Order status page.** New `/cafe/[slug]/order/[orderId]` customer page + scoped `GET /api/orders/[orderId]` endpoint. Shows live fulfillment status (new/making/ready/completed/**cancelled** — newly wired up; the DB already allowed it, the UI never used it) and payment status (pending/paid/failed/refunded). Demo mode updates live via the existing `demoStore` event bus (same mechanism the staff board already uses); production mode polls every 10s with a manual refresh button, consistent with the polling approach already documented as the interim step before full Supabase Realtime in `docs/KNOWN_GAPS.md`.
- **Loyalty opt-in in checkout.** New, clearly separated "Loyalty (optional)" card between order review and tip. Never blocks guest checkout. Demo mode: type a phone, order confirms, a loyalty stamp is awarded. Production mode: shows "signed in" if the customer already has a session, otherwise an inline phone → OTP → verify flow (same `signInWithOtp`/`verifyOtp` pattern as the existing rewards page) so *this* order can be credited — loyalty crediting is enforced server-side by `apply_paid_order`'s existing `auth_user_id is not null` gate, which requires verification to happen before payment.
- **Real payment confirmation, not fake data.** Found and fixed: the confirmation screen hardcoded `"Paid · Visa ••42"` even in **production mode**. Square's actual card brand/last4 now flows from the payment response through `/api/orders` to the confirmation screen, falling back to no card text if unavailable. Demo mode keeps its clearly-fake test-card text (`4242 4242 4242 4242`).
- **"Track your order"** link added to the confirmation screen, pointing at the new status page.
- **Clearer payment/validation error state.** The `paymentError` display went from a line of small red text to a bordered alert banner (same pattern as the table-error banner from #9), covering Square-not-configured, tokenize failures, and any server validation error from `/api/orders`.

## Acceptance criteria mapping (issue #10)

- [x] Checkout clearly separates order review, optional loyalty, tip, and payment — new Loyalty card added; order review/tip/payment cards already existed.
- [x] Phone loyalty opt-in/check-in is optional and does not block guest checkout — new.
- [x] Payment failure, missing Square configuration, and server validation errors have clear customer-facing states — elevated to an alert banner. **"Canceled payment"**: Square's embedded Web Payments card field has no mid-flow cancel/redirect concept; the existing "Back to menu" button already lets a customer back out before paying, which is the practical equivalent.
- [x] Confirmation includes order number/name, table/pickup context, item snapshot, subtotal/tip/tax/total, and payment status — already shipped; this PR fixes the payment status detail (real card brand/last4) instead of hardcoded text.
- [x] Order status page showing new/in-progress/ready/completed/cancelled/failed/refunded — new (`making` = in-progress).
- [x] Demo mode presents the whole story without credentials, clearly demo-only — unchanged demo conventions throughout.
- [x] Production mode uses server-created orders/Square/Supabase state, never fakes payment success — new (this PR removes the one place it was faking it).
- [x] BEM convention followed — reuses `eyebrow`, `status-dot` (+ new `--cancelled` modifier), `card--parchment`; new one-off states use plain Tailwind per `docs/BEM_STANDARDS.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test -- --run`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` — added coverage for the demo loyalty opt-in flow and the order-status page (9 passed, up from 7; same 4 pre-existing `fixme` skips)

## Known gaps for later issues

- No owner-facing UI yet to see/manage `accepting_orders` (see PR #18) — natural fit for the admin setup hub (#12).
- Order-status page uses polling, not Supabase Realtime, in production — matches the existing documented gap for the staff board in `docs/KNOWN_GAPS.md`.
- "Canceled payment" has no dedicated UI state beyond the existing back-out button, since Square's card element doesn't have a cancel/redirect flow to react to.

author: mrkhachaturov
body:
## Summary

Two related changes to the astrai18n image and the repo's local/CI tooling.

### 1. Docker file-secrets for astrai18n
The upstream image launches Java directly and reads sensitive settings only as
plaintext env values — it has no file-secret convention. This adds a thin
entrypoint wrapper that resolves any `<VAR>_FILE` variable from the file it
points at (a Docker/Swarm secret in `/run/secrets`) into the environment before
handing off to the stock launcher.

- `file-secrets.sh` — sourceable `expand_file_secrets` (any `<VAR>_FILE` → read file → export `<VAR>`, trailing newline stripped).
- `entrypoint.sh` — runs the expansion, then `exec /app/cmd.sh "$@"` (keeps `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` and the upstream OTEL logic intact).
- `Dockerfile` — copies both `--chmod=555` and overrides the entrypoint.
- One mechanism covers every secret — the external datasource password (`SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD_FILE`), provider API keys, JWT/S3 secrets — decoupled from the app's property-key schema.

### 2. `just` → `mise`
- Replaces `justfile` + `.just/` with `mise.toml` + file tasks under `.mise/tasks/` (`setup`, `local-build`, `remote-build`, `generate-app-labels`, `test`).
- Toolchain (`jq`, `yq`, `container-structure-test`) pinned in `[tools]`; `setup` fetches the linux `goss` + `dgoss` into `.bin/` (goss must be linux — dgoss injects it into the container under test).
- CI `label-sync` switches from Homebrew + `just` to `jdx/mise-action` + `mise run`.

### Test-harness fixes
- `tests.yaml` goss `timeout` set to integer milliseconds (the previous `300s` duration string is rejected by goss); added a command test proving the `_FILE` expansion resolves.
- Raised the app-tests goss `--retry-timeout` to `300s` — this image boots an embedded PostgreSQL + migrations and reports healthy at ~64s, past the old 60s window.

## Verification
- `mise run local-build astrai18n` — build + goss: **12/12 checks pass**, including the `_FILE` expansion test; app healthy at ~64s.
- `mise run test` — **69/69** task-layout / label-generation self-tests pass.
- `shellcheck` clean on all new task and entrypoint scripts.

author: inodb
body:
## What

Two related additions for `msk_spectrum_tme_2022`, both about the study's **CD45 FACS-sorted** single-cell data:

1. **Caveat in the cell-type profile descriptions** — the relative + absolute cell-type fraction profiles gain a `Caveat:` note. These fractions come from CD45-sorted scRNA-seq, so a sample's composition reflects its sort gate (some samples are immune-only or non-immune-only) rather than whole-tumor cellularity. The frontend renders `Caveat:` as a ⚠ per-track warning (cBioPortal/cbioportal-frontend#5637).

2. **New `CD45 Sort Fraction` generic-assay track** (`SINGLE_CELL_GATING`, categorical) — records which CD45 fraction(s) were actually sequenced per sample (`CD45-positive (immune)` / `CD45-negative (non-immune)` / `CD45-positive and negative` / `Unknown`), derived from the paper's Supplementary Table 2 (aliquot IDs encode `CD45P`/`CD45N`) and matched to sample barcodes via the MSK-IMPACT + Bulk-WGS crosswalks. Keeps all single-cell data under generic assay, and explains the one-sided compositions the caveat warns about.

## Files

- `meta_relative_fraction.txt`, `meta_absolute_counts.txt` — `Caveat:` appended to `profile_description`
- `meta_cell_gating.txt` — new categorical generic-assay profile (in this PR)
- `data_cell_gating.txt` — the sort-fraction values (**LFS — pending push**)

author: geekgonecrazy
body:
## Problem

`atomic agent enable` installs recording hooks guarded with:

```sh
test -d .atomic && atomic agent hooks <agent> <verb> || true
```

An agent **sandbox** working tree (`atomic sandbox create`) has no `.atomic/` directory of its own — it carries only a `.atomic-sandbox` pointer file to the canonical graph. So inside a sandbox the guard is always false, the recorder never runs, and **every turn's provenance is silently dropped**.

## Fix

Widen the guard to fire when either marker is present:

```sh
test -d .atomic || test -f .atomic-sandbox && atomic agent hooks <agent> <verb> || true
```

POSIX `&&`/`||` are equal-precedence and left-associative, so this parses as `(((test -d .atomic || test -f .atomic-sandbox) && CMD) || true)`:

| State | Recorder runs? |
|---|---|
| neither marker | no |
| `.atomic-sandbox` pointer only (sandbox) | **yes** |
| `.atomic/` dir only (canonical checkout) | yes |
| recorder itself fails | turn not blocked (`|| true`, exit 0) |

`atomic agent hooks` already resolves the sandbox pointer via `Repository::open` and records into the canonical graph, so nothing else needs to change on the runtime side.

## Details

- Centralized the guard in `hooks::guarded_hook_command` so **claude-code**, **gemini-cli**, and **codex** share one definition (previously duplicated as literals / `format!` calls in each adapter). The sandbox-pointer filename comes from `atomic_repository::SANDBOX_POINTER`.
- Hook detection (`is_installed`, `is_atomic_hook`, uninstall) is substring-based on the `atomic agent hooks <agent>` prefix, so already-installed **legacy** hooks are still recognized for status/uninstall/`--force` reinstall.
- Updated the manifest doc example and the `is_atomic_hook` tests to cover the new format.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p atomic-agent hooks::` — 414 passed
- `cargo test -p atomic-cli agent` — 59 passed
- Verified guard precedence for all four states in a real shell.

## 📺 Overview

Closes #501

### What does this PR do?
* **Type of change:** [x] Bug fix
* **Component(s) affected:** `calcore/llm.py` (`query_pass_decision`), `/api/session/{sid}/pass-decision` endpoint in `server.py`

---

## 🛠️ Technical Context & Implementation

* **The Problem:** `query_pass_decision()` aggregated client-supplied measurement fields (`delta_e`, `effective_gamma`, `cct`) and called `round()`/arithmetic on them *before* entering its `try`/`except` block. A non-numeric value (e.g. `delta_e: "bad"`) raised an uncaught `TypeError`, which propagated through `post_pass_decision` in `server.py` as an HTTP 500 instead of degrading gracefully, violating the project convention that `query_*` functions never raise.
* **The Solution:** Added a `_safe_float()` helper that coerces `delta_e`, `effective_gamma`, and `cct` to `float`, returning `None` when a value isn't numeric. Measurements whose `delta_e` doesn't coerce are skipped (same as the existing "missing `delta_e`" path). Also added a check so that if no measurement has a usable `delta_e`, the function returns `None` immediately rather than making a pointless LLM call with empty data.
* **Impact on existing workflows/APIs:** None for well-formed requests. Malformed/corrupted measurement payloads now cause `/api/session/{sid}/pass-decision` to return its existing graceful fallback (`{"action": "accept", "reason": "LLM unavailable", ...}`, HTTP 200) instead of a 500.

## What

`vibium fill` on an `input[type=range]` failed with `editable check failed — input type range not editable`, even though a range holds a settable value. (With auto-wait now the default, it also blocked for the full timeout before failing, rather than failing fast.)

The editable actionability check (`clicker/internal/api/actionability.go`) allowed only a whitelist of text-like input types (`text`, `password`, `email`, `number`, `search`, `tel`, `url`). `range` wasn't in it.

author: mikedougherty
body:
The last active finding from the 2026-06-26 review. Blunts brute-force against the login/callback flow and the admin bearer token (compounds #7's constant-time compare). Relates to #141 (finding #10).

## Summary

New `RateLimitMiddleware` does fixed-window per-IP counting in Redis, keyed by path scope:

| Scope | Budget |
|-------|--------|
| `/api/v1/auth/` | 20 requests / 60s |
| `/api/v1/admin/` | 60 requests / 60s |

Over the budget → `429` with a `Retry-After` header. Non-auth/admin paths are never touched (no Redis call). Gated by `settings.rate_limit_enabled` (default on) as a kill switch.

Two deliberate design choices:
- **Client IP from `X-Forwarded-For`** (first hop). Behind nginx-gateway-fabric every request's socket peer is the gateway, so `request.client.host` would lump all clients into one bucket. Falls back to the socket peer for direct/local requests.
- **Fails open.** If Redis is unavailable the request passes through rather than being blocked — a Redis blip must not lock everyone out of authentication. Availability wins over the hardening here.

<details>
<summary>How to Review</summary>

One commit (20c8c26):
- `middleware/rate_limit.py` (new) — `RateLimitMiddleware`, `RateLimitRule`, `DEFAULT_RULES`, `client_ip()`.
- `config.py` — `rate_limit_enabled` flag.
- `app.py` — import + conditional `add_middleware` (added after session so it sits outermost and rejects early).
- `tests/test_rate_limit.py` (new) — coverage below.

The budgets are generous on purpose: a person logging in or an agent driving the admin API won't hit them, but credential brute-force becomes impractical.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Test Plan</summary>

- [x] Under the limit passes, then 429 with `Retry-After` over it
- [x] Non-matching paths are never limited (no counter created)
- [x] Per-IP isolation: distinct `X-Forwarded-For` clients have independent budgets
- [x] Fails open when Redis errors (requests pass through)
- [x] `client_ip()` prefers the first XFF hop, falls back to the socket peer
- [x] Full suite: 1632 pass (+6); ruff + ruff format + mypy strict clean
</details>

<details>
<summary>Impact</summary>

- Only `/api/v1/auth/*` and `/api/v1/admin/*` are rate-limited; all other routes are unaffected.
- Legitimate use (human login, agent/CLI admin calls) stays well under the budgets.
- A Redis outage degrades to "no rate limiting" rather than "no auth".
- With this merged, the security review is closed: 10 of 11 findings fixed, #3 accepted-risk.
</details>

body:
The app's whole value is **monitor → identify → fix**, but tapping "Relieve the live cause" on a memory finding ran `sirsi guard` — which is literally the **monitor** (aliased to `sirsi monitor`). It opened a read-only dashboard, not a remediation. Every memory finding dead-ended.

## Fix
- **Route memory findings to real actions**, not the monitor: RAM Pressure / Memory Processes / Swap(critical) → `sirsi relieve --memory`; Thread Leaks → `sirsi relieve` (renice).
- **New `sirsi relieve --memory`** — the honest memory lever:
  1. **Identifies** the top memory consumer (the half the app skipped — e.g. "Python (12.0 GB)").
  2. **Flushes inactive caches** with `purge` — the safe, non-destructive macOS memory lever (renice frees CPU, not RAM; auto-killing user apps isn't safe to automate).
  3. Preview → **admin auth via the macOS native dialog** (your password goes to the OS, never to sirsi) → **before/after free-memory + pressure proof**.
  4. Honest guidance to quit the named hog to free more.

**Verified live** (preview): names the top consumer + free + pressure + a real "Flush caches now" action. `go test -race ./internal/guard` green.

Part of a larger "every finding maps to a real macOS lever" effort (catalog + ADR to follow). This is the memory exemplar of the pattern.

Refs: PANTHEON_RULES.md A1, A10

author: krasforge
body:
Closes #38.

Turns the frozen ABI spec (#37) into a practical starting point: an outside developer can build, load, and share a plugin using only this SDK and the documentation, with no Tessera kernel sources.

## What's in `sdk/`
Self-contained; depends on no Tessera kernel header.

- **`tessera.h`** - the single header you include. Wraps the ABI and adds `TESSERA_ABI_VERSION`, `TESSERA_PLUGIN_EXPORT`, `TESSERA_DEFINE_ABI_VERSION`, and the host parameter-queue layout + reader.
- **`plugin_abi.h`** - bundled copy of the frozen ABI header (kept identical to `include/plugin_abi.h` by `make verify-sdk-abi-sync`).
- **`libtessera.a`** (from `lib/`) - `tessera_sinf` (fast, range-reduced sine, <0.1% error), `tessera_clampf`, `tessera_param_queue_read` (lock-free queue drain). No libc, no allocation.
- **`tessera.ld`** - link script placing code/rodata/data in **separate R-X / R / R-W segments**, so an SDK-built plugin is W^X-safe and audits clean under the #35 sandbox. (The kernel's own `plugin.ld` emits a single RWE segment; the SDK improves on that.)
- **`examples/sine_plugin/`** - a complete, commented sine plugin using only the SDK, with a standalone `Makefile`.
- **`Makefile`** (builds `libtessera.a`), **`Makefile.template`** (copy-paste cross-compile makefile), **`README.md`**.

## Acceptance criteria (issue #38)
- `cd sdk/examples/sine_plugin && make` produces a loadable `sine_plugin.elf` with no additional dependencies - verified (built with `CROSS_COMPILE=aarch64-linux-gnu-`; the default triple is `aarch64-none-elf-`). Output: AArch64 `ET_EXEC`, all five ABI symbols, zero disallowed imports.
- The resulting ELF loads and produces audio under Tessera - `test-arm-sdk-qemu` loads it, audits it clean (`wx=0`, nothing outside its regions), gets non-silent stereo audio from `process_block`, and confirms a 440->880 Hz change delivered through the host parameter queue changes the output.
- The SDK depends on no Tessera kernel internal header (only the bundled public ABI header).

## Verification
- `make test-sdk` - host unit tests: `tessera_sinf` vs libm `sinf` (peak error 0.001 < 0.002), `tessera_clampf`, and `tessera_param_queue_read` against the exact host wire format.
- `make test-arm-sdk-qemu` - the full build-from-SDK + load + audio + param-change acceptance, `SDK: PASS`.
- `make verify-sdk-abi-sync` - guards the bundled header against drift.
- New `sdk-tests` CI job runs all three.

## What & why

Follow-up polish on the marketing site:

### favicon.ico
The site had no `/favicon.ico` (the classic browser/OS icon). Added a multi-resolution `.ico` (16/32/48) of the coffin mark, generated by the repo's own `gen:icons` script via a small **pure-node ICO packer** (no new deps), and linked it in the head.

### Dark-only + Dark Reader fix
Removed all light-mode machinery:

body:
## What

Takes test coverage from **36% → 95%** (whole codebase, including the PySide6 desktop GUI), gates CI at **70%**, and surfaces coverage on GitHub via a PR comment + README badge.

## Tests added (~215 new tests)

Headless Qt via `pytest-qt` (offscreen platform):
- **desktop engine/paths/updater/bridge** — real logic tests, incl. a full offline council `run()` (TestModel).
- **desktop GUI** — dialogs, pages, panels, and `main_window` constructed + exercised headlessly.
- **quorum_core gaps** — catalog, provider `build_model`, validation, events, migrate, agents_service.
- `desktop/tests/conftest.py`: offscreen platform, temp SQLite in test-model mode, seeded-agents `db` fixture.

Per-area coverage lands at 95–100%; **total 95.38%**.

## Tooling

- Dev deps `pytest-cov`, `pytest-qt`; `[tool.coverage]` config (`source`, `omit`, `fail_under = 70`, `relative_files`); `testpaths += desktop/tests`.
- `make test-cov` — tests with coverage (terminal + `htmlcov/`), enforces the 70% gate.
- `ci.yml` `pytest` job installs Qt runtime libs (offscreen PySide6 on the Linux runner).

## Coverage visibility (GitHub-native)

- `coverage.yml`: runs coverage, posts/updates a **PR comment** and publishes a **README badge** via `py-cov-action/python-coverage-comment-action` (no external service — uses the built-in token), then enforces the **70% minimum**.
- README badge added (renders once the action runs on `main` post-merge and creates its data branch).

## Bug fix (found by the dialog tests)

`AgentEditDialog._do_save` passed `name` both positionally **and** via `**self._fields()` to `engine.create_agent`, so UI agent-creation always errored (`multiple values for 'name'`, swallowed by the `except`). Fixed by popping `name` from the field kwargs.

## Verified locally

258 passed · coverage 95.38% (gate 70% reached) · `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean · `mypy` clean.

> Note: the desktop GUI tests run offscreen; CI installs the required Qt libs on Ubuntu for both the `pytest` and `coverage` jobs.

author: mgzwarrior
body:
Closes #735

## What

The favorite-sets panel (`FavoriteSetsPanel`) took up a lot of vertical space in Swipe. Two changes shrink its footprint:

- **Collapsed by default.** The panel now starts as a one-line header — a disclosure button (`aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`) that summarizes what's inside (`3 pinned · 5 suggested`) with a chevron. Clicking it expands to reveal the pinned chips and suggestions; clicking again collapses.
- **Cap suggestions to five.** `MAX_SUGGESTIONS` dropped from 6 to 5 so the expanded list stays short.

## Why

Swipe is the low-friction way in for a collector, and the personalization panel was eating room above the card. A collapsed strip keeps the surface available without dominating the view; the summary means you still know it's there and what it holds before expanding.

## Notes

- Accessible disclosure: the toggle lives inside the `<h3>` (heading keeps its semantics), carries `aria-expanded` and points at the body via `aria-controls`. The body unmounts when collapsed, so it genuinely reclaims the space.
- No data-model or API changes — pure presentation. The panel still hides entirely when there's nothing pinned and nothing to suggest.

## How to verify

- `make check` green; `cd web && npm run build` green; full web suite (605 tests) green.
- Updated/added `FavoriteSetsPanel.test.tsx` coverage: collapsed-by-default (summary shown, chips not rendered until expanded), expand reveals the sets, and suggestions cap at five. Existing pin/unpin/suggest tests expand first.
- In the app (Swipe, signed in with pins or suggestions): the panel is a single row that expands on click and shows at most five suggestions.

author: ooiuuii
body:
Closes #98357

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Slack operators could accidentally put a Slack user token in the bot-token slot and still see Slack startup/probe succeed without any warning that `auth.test` returned a human `user_id` but no `bot_id`.

Because Slack mention and self-author handling uses the authenticated identity, silently accepting that ambiguous response makes misconfiguration hard to diagnose. It was also possible for `openclaw channels capabilities --channel slack` to look healthy because the Slack probe formatter only showed bot/team lines.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a shared Slack `auth.test` identity warning for successful responses that include `user_id` but omit `bot_id`. The warning is surfaced in provider startup logs and account probe/capabilities output, with the probed Slack account id carried into the diagnostic so named accounts point to `channels.slack.accounts.<id>.botToken`.

The change intentionally does not alter token precedence, Slack client setup, or startup failure behavior, and it does not log token values.

## User Impact

Slack users now get a clear diagnostic when a bot-token field appears to contain a user token (`xoxp-...`) instead of a bot token (`xoxb-...`). Correctly configured bot tokens continue through the existing startup and probe paths without extra warnings.

Named Slack accounts now get account-specific guidance instead of being told to edit the default account.

## Evidence

- Before/source proof: on current main, a successful Slack `auth.test` response with `user_id` and no `bot_id` is accepted by provider startup and `probeSlack()` without any warning, and the Slack capabilities formatter has no path to print a probe warning.
- After-fix Slack WebClient probe proof, using a temporary redacted Slack `auth.test`-compatible endpoint and a redacted `xoxp-...` token-shaped value. This exercises the PR branch's Slack WebClient probe path, not only the formatter:

```text
SLACK_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<mock-port>/api/ node --import tsx <probeSlack accountId=work>

REQUESTS: POST /api/auth.test
RESULT:
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": 200,
  "bot": {
    "id": "UWORK",
    "name": "human-installer"
  },
  "team": {
    "id": "TREDACTED",
    "name": "Redacted Workspace"
  },
  "warning": "slack auth.test returned user_id=UWORK without bot_id for account \"work\"; channels.slack.accounts.work.botToken may contain a Slack user token (xoxp-...) instead of a bot token (xoxb-...). Slack mentions of that user can be mistaken for bot mentions until the token is replaced."
}
```

- After-fix capabilities-display proof, using the Slack plugin status adapter on the same probed account result. This verifies the warning reaches the user-visible capabilities/probe lines:

```text
SLACK_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<mock-port>/api/ node --import tsx <slackPlugin.status.probeAccount + formatCapabilitiesProbe>

REQUESTS: POST /api/auth.test
Warning: slack auth.test returned user_id=UWORK without bot_id for account "work"; channels.slack.accounts.work.botToken may contain a Slack user token (xoxp-...) instead of a bot token (xoxb-...). Slack mentions of that user can be mistaken for bot mentions until the token is replaced.
Bot: @human-installer
Team: Redacted Workspace (TREDACTED)
```

- Live Slack API proof (July 1, 2026): created a disposable Slack app named `OpenClaw Proof 98358` in the test workspace `pep-ucd-AY2019`, installed it with bot scope `chat:write` and user scope `users:read`, then invoked Slack's real `https://slack.com/api/auth.test` through this PR branch's `probeSlack()` path. Token values, user ids, and team details were redacted from output.

```text
node --import tsx <live-proof-harness importing extensions/slack/src/probe.ts>

{
  "label": "user-token-in-bot-slot",
  "ok": true,
  "status": 200,
  "team": { "idPrefix": "TQ", "name": "<redacted>" },
  "bot": { "idPrefix": "UQ", "name": "<redacted>" },
  "warning": "slack auth.test returned user_id=<redacted> without bot_id for account \"live-work\"; channels.slack.accounts.live-work.botToken may contain a Slack user token (xoxp-...) instead of a bot token (xoxb-...). Slack mentions of that user can be mistaken for bot mentions until the token is replaced."
}
{
  "label": "bot-token-control",
  "ok": true,
  "status": 200,
  "team": { "idPrefix": "TQ", "name": "<redacted>" },
  "bot": { "idPrefix": "U0", "name": "<redacted>" },
  "warning": null
}
```

- Live capabilities-display proof using the same real Slack user token in the bot-token slot and this PR branch's `slackPlugin.status.probeAccount + formatCapabilitiesProbe` path:

```text
warn Warning: slack auth.test returned user_id=<redacted> without bot_id for account "live-work"; channels.slack.accounts.live-work.botToken may contain a Slack user token (xoxp-...) instead of a bot token (xoxb-...). Slack mentions of that user can be mistaken for bot mentions until the token is replaced.
info Bot: @<redacted>
info Team: <redacted> (TQ...)
```
- After-fix focused tests:

body:
Stage 5 delivers a single standardized eval suite shared by the offline runner and the pipeline scorer, a CLI entry point, and warm-endpoint reuse for TimesFM serving. All five items are validated offline (218 passing) and 5.4/5.5 additionally validated live on `hybrid-vertex`.

## Items

| # | Item | Commit |
|---|------|--------|
| 5.1 | Eval suite in `metrics.py` — guarded sMAPE, pinball/quantile loss over `QUANTILES`, per-series breakdown, `evaluate()` aggregator | `5d71aa8` |
| 5.2 | Unify: wire `evaluate()` into `runner.py` + `score_and_track_step`; shared `rank_backends` for the comparison Markdown | `7244b3c` |
| 5.3 | `scripts/run_experiment.py` CLI (argparse over `run_experiment`); extract AutoML overrides | `518a1b9` |
| 5.4 | Warm endpoints + fingerprint reuse + teardown guard | `a2f5e1f` |
| 5.5 | Live validation + `docs/notes/` writeup | `1d0fb7d` |

## 5.4 — warm-endpoint reuse (highlights)

- **Fingerprint** = `sha256(image_digest + serving_env)[:16]` — a warm deployment is discoverable + reuse-compatible only when its serving contract matches (digest pins the baked checkpoint).
- **Submit-time lookup + compile-time DAG branch** (matches the recorded "branch at compile time, the YAML shows exactly what executes" convention) — not a runtime `dsl.If`. Reuse path emits `endpoint-predict-by-name` and omits the whole serving lifecycle.
- **Two teardown guards:** primary — no teardown task emitted on a reuse run; secondary — `teardown_serving_step` skips any endpoint/model labelled `keep=true`. The `keep` label is stamped whenever `keep_deployed`, independent of reuse mode.
- Digest resolution shells `gcloud` behind an injected runner (4.7 precedent); all seams unit-test offline.

## 5.5 — live validation (`--disable-automl`, hybrid-vertex)

- **Warm deploy** → endpoint labelled `fingerprint` + `keep=true`, no teardown node.
- **Reuse** → submit-time lookup found the warm endpoint, reuse branch predicted against it with **identical** metrics (reuse correctness).
- **Teardown guard** probed live → skipped the `keep=true` endpoint and model; both survived. Then explicit cleanup (0 endpoints / 0 models remain).
- Unified richer suite flows through the pipeline live (sMAPE + quantile loss populated).
- Gotcha documented: a schema change requires a runtime-image rebuild before a live run (a component rejected the new `reuse_endpoint` field under `extra=forbid`).

Full writeup: `docs/notes/stage-5-warm-endpoint-reuse-live-run.md`.

## Verification

- Offline gate green: `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `ty check` + `pytest` (**218 passed**).
- 5.4 code-quality review (reviews-as-gates): APPROVE-WITH-NITS; the MEDIUM finding + empty-digest fail-loud fixed before merge.

author: xclsv-bot
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Ideate error you hit — `⚠ Unexpected token 'A', "An error o"... is not valid JSON` — on a longer "refine" turn.

## Root cause
`/api/ideate` could overrun the serverless **function timeout** on a longer turn (`claude-opus-4-8` at **medium** effort + **8000** max_tokens). Vercel then returns a non-JSON platform error page ("An error o…"), and the client crashed calling `res.json()` on it. Confirmed against prod logs: only `200`s + method-`405`s, **no 5xx** — the signature of a timeout (the function is killed before it can log), not a code exception.

## Fix (two layers)
1. **Cut Ideate latency**: effort **medium → low** and max_tokens **8000 → 4096** — keeps concept quality but finishes well under the limit. Bumped `maxDuration` **60 → 300** on `ideate` + `review` + `revise` for headroom (Vercel caps it to your plan max).
2. **Make the clients timeout-resilient**: new `src/lib/http.ts` `fetchJson()` reads the body defensively and **never throws on a non-JSON/timeout response** — it returns a friendly `{ error }` ("That took too long and timed out — try again") instead of the cryptic parse error. Wired into **Ideate** (send) and the **Script panel** (Review / Revise), the timeout-prone AI calls.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run build` — green

## Note
If a call still occasionally times out, it likely means the Vercel plan caps function duration below what a heavy generation needs — tell me and I'll dial effort down further or split the work. But low-effort Ideate should be comfortably fast now.

Five edge functions had `peninsulaequine.lovable.app` hardcoded as the site URL, so every transactional email linked users to the Lovable preview app rather than production. | Function | Change |
|---|---|

author: colonelkernie
body:
## Summary
Several refinements to the booking calendar in `BookingFlow.jsx`:

- **Minimum one-night stays** — a date can't be selected as a check-in if its following day is booked (no valid checkout). The rule applies only while selecting the check-in, so the day before a booked block remains selectable as a checkout-only date.
- **No overlapping ranges** — while selecting the checkout, dates at or beyond the nearest booked dates on either side of the check-in are disabled, so a range can never span an existing booking.
- **Duration semantics** — nights are counted as midnight crossings; check-in is stored at 3pm and checkout at 11am to reflect the real stay window.
- **Default month** — the calendar opens on the month of the first available check-in date.
- **Styling** — booked dates are shown in grey instead of red, and date cells have square (non-rounded) corners.

## Testing
- `npm run build` passes.

Removes all server-side timeout enforcement — a feature that was marked P1 in CLAUDE.md but never built beyond the state machine + service method.

- **GameMove.java**: `isTimeout` column + `TIMEOUT` enum value dropped

Low. `handleTimeout` has zero callers. The frontend `turnTimerSeconds` field was optional and never consumed beyond the type definition. No coordinated deploy needed — new backend can safely omit the field while old frontend is still running.

author: germsrosolino
body:
# Establish Initial Repository Architecture

## Summary

This PR establishes the initial structure of the Open Evidence Library.

Rather than immediately focusing on content, this change lays the foundation for a version-controlled, evidence-based knowledge repository intended to support researchers, educators, journalists, software projects, and advocacy organizations.

The initial emphasis is on creating an architecture that can scale as the library grows.

---

## What Changed

### Repository Documentation

- Added project README
- Added CC BY 4.0 license
- Added initial `.gitignore`

### Repository Governance

- Configured branch protection rules
- Enabled pull request workflow
- Created initial project issue

### Initial Architecture

Created an initial domain-oriented directory structure including:

- Animal Agriculture
- Environment
- Legislation
- Nutrition

Each domain currently contains placeholders for:

- Claims
- Sources
- Topics

### Templates

Added reusable templates for:

- Claim
- Source
- Topic
- Article Brief

These templates are intentionally lightweight and are expected to evolve as real-world usage informs future improvements.

---

## Architectural Decisions

Several architectural decisions were made during this initial implementation.

### Domain-first organization

Rather than organizing by artifact type (e.g. `claims/`, `sources/`), the repository is organized by subject domain.

This keeps related evidence together and should scale more naturally as the repository grows.

### Separation of Claims and Sources

Claims and supporting sources are intentionally stored separately.

A single source may support multiple claims, and individual claims may be supported by multiple independent sources.

This separation also aligns with future plans for structured evidence reuse.

### Public-first philosophy

The repository is intended to function as an openly accessible evidence library.

Research should be transparent, version-controlled, and freely reusable under the CC BY 4.0 license.

---

## Follow-up Work

Future work includes:

- Import the first primary source
- Validate repository templates using real content
- Establish research standards
- Develop naming conventions and claim identifiers
- Expand repository documentation

author: no77312
body:
## 现象

每日盈亏日报里所有人当日涨跌都是 `US$0（0.00%）`。

## 根因

日报的当日涨跌 = Σ 数量 ×(今日价 − 昨日价),前提是价格真的刷新了。查定时任务日志:

```
"updatedCount": 0
"failed": [VOO, MSFT, 0700, BTC, AAPL, NVDA, TSLA, ... 50+ 个全部"未找到可用的 T-1 收盘价"]
```

**Alpha Vantage 免费版限制为每分钟 5 次 / 每天 25 次**,而账号里有 50+ 个不同标的,额度远远不够 → 刷新全部失败 → 价格不动 → 相邻两天快照价格相同 → 当日涨跌恒为 0。日报逻辑没错,是上游行情源限流了。

## 改法

## 概要

Phase 1（ユーザー所有 Vercel への公開）の続き。生成 MVP が **ユーザーの Vercel など別オリジン**に配信されても、ビルダーの **BaaS（データ / 認証 / アップロード / フィードバック）** を利用できるようにする。

> **base はあえて `feat/vercel-oauth-phase1`**（#35）にしています。Phase 1 が main にマージされたら、本PRの base を main に付け替えてください（stacked PR）。

## 背景（なぜ必要か）

これまで公開 HTML は **相対パス** `/api/run/<id>/...` で BaaS を呼んでいた。ビルダー自身がホストする `/run` では同一オリジンなので動くが、**ユーザーの `*.vercel.app` に配信すると相対パスはそのドメインを指してしまい**、BaaS に届かない。加えて公開エンドポイントに CORS が無かった。

## 変更点

- **SDK / ウィジェットの絶対URL対応**: `buildRuntimeSdk` / `buildFeedbackWidget` に `apiOrigin` を追加。指定時は `/api/run/*` を**ビルダーの絶対URL**に向ける。未指定は従来どおり相対パス（`/run` 同一オリジン）。
- **注入ロジックの共有化**: `injectRuntimeSdk(html, projectId, apiOrigin?)` を `mvp-runtime.ts` に集約。`/run` route（相対）と publish（絶対）で共用し、`/run` の重複コードを削除。
- **publish で絶対URL注入**: publish route が `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`（無ければリクエストホスト）からビルダーオリジンを解決し、Vercel 公開 HTML に絶対URLの SDK+ウィジェットを注入。
- **CORS**: `src/proxy.ts`（Next.js 16 で middleware から改称）に `/api/run/:path*` を追加。`OPTIONS` プリフライト応答 + `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`。認可は Bearer / 匿名 ownerKey で **Cookie 非依存**のため wildcard で安全。既存の `/studio` 保護はそのまま。

## セキュリティ

- `/api/run/*` は Cookie を使わない（資格情報付きでない）ため ACAO `*` で安全。既存のサニタイズ / 実在チェック / サイズ制限は不変。
- 別オリジンからの呼び出しでも projectId スコープは維持。

body:
## Summary

- STDLIB-COMP-FN-040 (`minOf(a: Float, vararg other: Float)`) was already implemented and merged in #4354. This PR marks it done in TODO.md.
- While verifying that work end-to-end, found that `minOf`/`maxOf` for `Float`/`Double` — the 2-arg, 3-arg, and vararg overloads alike — lowered to a plain `<`/`>` comparison. That diverges from `kotlinc` in two cases:
  - **NaN operands**: ordered comparison (`<`/`>`) is always `false` for NaN, so the *non-NaN* argument silently won instead of NaN propagating (e.g. `minOf(Float.NaN, 1.0f)` returned `1.0` instead of `NaN`).
  - **Signed zero**: `-0.0 == 0.0` under IEEE 754, so argument order determined the result instead of following `Math.min`/`Math.max`'s fixed rule (e.g. `minOf(-0.0f, 0.0f)` returned `0.0` instead of `-0.0`).
  - Verified both the mismatch and the fix directly against `kotlinc`.
- Added `kk_min_float`/`kk_max_float`/`kk_min_double`/`kk_max_double` runtime helpers that replicate Java's `Math.min`/`Math.max` semantics, and routed the Float/Double lowering paths in `CallLowerer+StdlibComparisons.swift` through them instead of the raw comparison. `Int`/`Long`/unsigned paths are untouched since they have no NaN/signed-zero distinction.

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build` succeeds
- [x] Manual `kswiftc` output compared directly against `kotlinc` for NaN/-0.0 cases across 2-arg, 3-arg, and vararg `minOf`/`maxOf`, Float and Double — all match
- [x] Full `CompilerBackendTests.CodegenBackendIntegrationTests` suite (921 tests) passes with no regressions
- [x] New edge-case tests added and passing: `testCodegenCompilesMinOfFloatNaNAndSignedZero`, `testCodegenCompilesMinOfFloatNaNMultiArg`, `testCodegenCompilesMinOfDoubleNaNAndSignedZero`, `testCodegenCompilesMaxOfFloatNaNAndSignedZero`, `testCodegenCompilesMaxOfDoubleNaNAndSignedZero`
- [x] `CompilerCoreTests.ComparisonSyntheticTopLevelTests` (36 tests, Sema layer) passes unchanged — this PR only touches KIR lowering + runtime, not Sema

author: renatomen
body:
## What & why

Standardizes how UI-change visuals (GIFs / static images) are captured, stored, and referenced across PRs and release notes — and makes generating them a **default, automated pipeline step**. Previously this was ad-hoc, and the PR path relied on `ce-demo-reel`'s **catbox** default (an external host with link-rot risk, no provenance). Release notes render in two places (the GitHub release page and the in-app "What's New" view), so a referenced image must be reachable and immutable for the life of every install.

This PR moves visuals **into the repo** under an enforced convention, and adds a judgment-driven skill that generates them automatically with your existing `ce-demo-reel` workflow.

## What's included

- **Convention** — `docs/conventions/visual-assets.md`: assets in `docs/media/`, feature-named, referenced only by **pinned `raw.githubusercontent` markdown image URLs** (PR → branch/SHA, release → tag); permanence rules; the demo-director staging checklist; fixtures-only privacy guarantee. Linked from `AGENTS.md`.
- **Shared module** — `scripts/visualAssets.mjs` (path/URL construction + validation) + `scripts/repoInfo.mjs` (single-sourced owner/repo slug).
- **Build-time validator** — `scripts/releaseFiles.mjs` rejects relative/unpinned/foreign image URLs and missing committed assets, so a bad reference fails the build/CI instead of silently shipping a broken image.
- **`scripts/addVisualAsset.mjs`** — the deterministic bridge that lands any produced artifact (a ce-demo-reel GIF, a recording, a screenshot) into `docs/media/` with the convention name + prints the pinned markdown. Source-agnostic, unit-tested.
- **`/tng-demo` skill** — the **default** visual step for PRs and releases: judges whether a demo is warranted (docs/refactor → none), reads the user-facing text and plans visuals per section (one combined or several short), generates each via **ce-demo-reel against fixtures** with house staging (maximized, panels closed), lands them, and inserts pinned references.
- **`/tng-release`** — drafts notes and delegates its visual step to `/tng-demo`; draft-only, unchanged.

## Key decisions

- **ce-demo-reel is the demo engine.** The repo owns the convention, the validator, a thin landing step, and a judgment skill — not a competing capturer. (An earlier WDIO static-capture helper was built and then **removed** as redundant; see the plan's Revision section.)
- **Markdown `![]()` only, never raw HTML** — the release-notes generator rejects raw HTML and fails the build; GIFs work as markdown images.
- **Feature-named shared pool** — one committed file serves the PR and every release that mentions the feature; releases re-pin to the tag (a no-force-move rule backs permanence).
- **`tng-` command prefix** — project-local commands (`/tng-release`, `/tng-demo`) are prefixed to distinguish them from external plugin commands, matching the existing `tngantt_` / `tng-` code namespace.

## Privacy

Demos are **fixtures-only and cannot leak private data.** Generation runs against committed `test/vaults/*` fixtures (reusing existing e2e scenarios where they fit), never a real vault — privacy by construction, enforced in the convention and the skill.

## Testing

- **934 unit tests pass**; lint 0 errors; typecheck 0 errors.
- New coverage for the asset module, the release-notes image validator, and the `addVisualAsset` landing script (incl. regressions for review-found bugs: branch-ref parsing, bracketed alt text).
- Release toolchain exercised directly (generators exit 0, no drift); `addVisualAsset` CLI smoke-tested end-to-end.

## Post-deploy monitoring & validation

No plugin runtime (`src/`) code changed — this is build-tooling, CI validation, docs, and agent commands, so there is **no end-user runtime impact**. Validation signal: CI `build` stays green (the image validator runs at Vite `buildStart`); the per-PR e2e suite is unaffected. No rollback plan needed beyond reverting the branch.

## Notes

Follows the revised plan at `docs/plans/2026-07-01-001-feat-release-visual-assets-plan.md` (see its "Revision" section for the corrected capture model). Deferred follow-ups (relocating the aged-out beta.3 asset; converging the runtime `releaseNoteLinks.ts` slug) are recorded there.

author: vfilby
body:
## Problem

Editing a single exercise in a plan regenerated the entire plan's `sourceMarkdown` from the parsed model, which hardcoded every header to `##`. A `## Warmup` section with `### Band Side Step` children collapsed into two sibling `##` headers — breaking the section nesting and producing a parse error the user then had to hand-repair before they could save again. Supersets lost their `###`/`####` nesting the same way. It also discarded anything the model doesn't round-trip (blank-line layout, comments, unknown `@metadata`).

## Fix

Persist an exercise edit by splicing **only that exercise's block** back into the original `sourceMarkdown` at its original header level(s), then re-parse the spliced text — instead of regenerating the document. Editing an exercise is now equivalent to replacing that one section of the source with the user's edited version; everything else is preserved verbatim.

- `MarkdownParser` records a source span (start/end line, header level, child header level) per exercise/group, keyed by `orderIndex`, returned on `LMWFParseResult`.
- New `LMWFSourceEditor` locates the edited block via those spans, renders the replacement at the source's own levels (superset children keep their real, possibly non-adjacent level), splices, and validates the result re-parses before committing.
- `WorkoutDetailView` routes exercise-edit saves through the splice; falls back to a plain model update when the plan has no stored markdown.
- Retire the flattening `regenerateMarkdown()`.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`LMWFSourceEditorTests`, 7): the reported `## Warmup`/`### Band Side Step` case, non-standard workout header level, superset level-skips, superset rename, splice isolation, span accuracy, and the legacy fallback.
- **E2E** (`edit-plan-preserves-structure.yaml`): drives the real import → edit → save → reopen-markdown path and asserts no parse error + valid parse. Passed locally (~46s).
- Full unit suite green (911, 0 failures).

## Notes

- Spec-first: `spec/screens/workout-detail.md` updated to describe the splice behavior.
- To make the edit button targetable in e2e, its accessibility id is now name-based (`edit-plan-exercise-<name>`, matching the existing `youtube-link-<name>`), and the parse-error banner gained `edit-plan-markdown-error`.
- The session-side encoder (`SessionLMWFEncoder`) is out of scope — it's a separate sync/export flow and is already nesting-aware.

## Summary

The `go-replace_kopia` hooks for OADP 1.3 and 1.4 were incorrectly replacing `github.com/kopia/kopia` with `github.com/migtools/kopia` at a branch ref. OADP 1.3 and 1.4 do not use an OADP-maintained kopia fork in go.mod — they depend on `github.com/project-velero/kopia` at specific upstream tags.

The `migtools/kopia` fork has diverged from the `project-velero/kopia` tags (renamed struct fields, changed types), causing `go vet` failures during the `go-mod-tidy-and-commit.sh` hook. This was breaking auto-rebase CI for velero, oadp-operator, and oadp-cli on both 1.3 and 1.4.

The hooks now pin to `project-velero/kopia` at the correct SSOT tag (`v0.13.0-velero.1` for 1.3, `v0.17.0-velero.1` for 1.4), matching what the repos actually use.

Note: `migtools/kopia` branches for 1.3/1.4 still exist and are consumed by must-gather's kopia submodule — those hooks are unaffected.

author: ugexe
body:
A pod block before a class parses into the following `is repr('CStruct')` trait's circumfix as a leading Doc::Block statement, so the circumfix holds two statements: the doc block and the repr value. `handle-is-repr` took the first statement of the circumfix, which was then the doc block, and reported `is repr(...) trait value must be known at compile time`.

`handle-is-repr` consumes the circumfix and drops it, so the doc block trapped inside it never reached `$=pod` either, unlike a pod block before any other class.

This reads the repr value from the circumfix's code-statements, which exclude doc blocks, and hands any doc block back to the pending collection so it attaches to the following declaration and reaches `$=pod` as it does elsewhere.

author: ippoo-z-up
body:
🛡️ Sentinel has improved the security posture of the application by addressing two high-priority vulnerabilities:

### 1. Secure Administrative Credential Storage
Administrative accounts stored in the KV database (via `/admin/roles`) previously used a simple, unsalted SHA-256 hash of `password:username`. This made them vulnerable to rainbow table attacks and GPU-accelerated brute-force.
- **Fix:** Transitioned new role creation to use **PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256** with **100,000 iterations** and a **16-byte random salt**.
- **Compatibility:** The login logic now supports a fallback mechanism that checks both the new salted PBKDF2 format and the legacy SHA-256 format, ensuring existing admins are not locked out.

### 2. Prevention of Sensitive Data Leakage in Logs
The `logWebhookEvent` function was persisting raw HTTP headers from payment providers (like Kkiapay and Fedapay) to the KV audit ring. This included secrets like `x-kkiapay-secret` and `x-fedapay-signature`.
- **Fix:** Implemented a centralized `SENSITIVE_HEADERS` redaction list. The logging pipeline now automatically replaces sensitive header values with `[REDACTED]` before storage.

### 3. Sentinel Journaling
Initialized the `.jules/sentinel.md` journal to document these critical security learnings and prevent future regressions.

✅ **Verification:** Changes were verified for syntax and bundling using `esbuild` and the full application was built successfully using `pnpm build`.

author: chl-wxp
body:
### Purpose

  This PR adds MetadataProvider SPI support for the Flink starter, so Flink jobs can resolve datasource connection options from the metadata center by using `metadata_datasource_id`.

  Before this change, Flink jobs with configs such as:

  ```hocon
  source {
    Jdbc {
      metadata_datasource_id = "test_catalog"
      query = "select * from source"
    }
  }
  ```

  could fail during connector option validation because required JDBC options like url and driver were not resolved before FactoryUtil created the source.

  ### Changes

  - Load metadata center configuration from seatunnel.yaml in the Flink starter.
  - Resolve datasource configs through MetadataProviderManager before applying legacy Metalake config handling.
  - Keep compatibility with existing Metalake placeholder replacement logic.
  - Update JDBC e2e coverage for MetadataProvider SPI on Flink.
  - Ensure the Flink e2e job process has SEATUNNEL_HOME so it can locate config/seatunnel.yaml.
  - Keep Metalake legacy env behavior using METALAKE_ENABLED, METALAKE_TYPE, and METALAKE_URL.

  ### Why

  The MetadataProvider SPI expects metadata settings from:

  ```yaml
  seatunnel:
    engine:
      metadata:
        enabled: true
        kind: gravitino
        gravitino:
          uri: http://gravitino:8090
          metalake: test_metalake
  ```

  Flink starter needs this config before connector validation, otherwise datasource options are not merged into the job config.

author: u3kkasha
body:
### Problem
The automated update bot (`r-ryntm` / `nixpkgs-update`) was failing to update `antigravity-cli` because it checks if the old version string followed by a double quote exists in the package's Nix file (e.g. searching for `"1.0.12\""`). However, in `antigravity-cli`'s `package.nix`, the version attribute was defined dynamically:
```nix
wholeVersion = "1.0.12-6156052174077952";
version = builtins.head (lib.splitString "-" wholeVersion);
```
Since `1.0.12` is followed by a hyphen (`-`) rather than a double quote (`"`), the bot's check failed. Furthermore, the custom `update.sh` script required a full Nix evaluation of Nixpkgs, which fails inside sparse checkouts.

### Solution
1. **Refactored Variable Structure**: Declared `version` and `buildId` as separate variables in `package.nix`, defining `wholeVersion` dynamically via interpolation:
   ```nix
   version = "1.0.12";
   buildId = "6156052174077952";
   wholeVersion = "${version}-${buildId}";
   ```
   This exposes the version string as a simple literal `"1.0.12"` so that the bot can find and replace it.
2. **Rewrote `update.sh`**: Modified the script to parse the version locally using grep, construct the URLs, and update the fields using a Python string-replacement snippet instead of calling `update-source-version` and `nix-instantiate` on the root of Nixpkgs. This makes it completely self-contained and compatible with sparse checkouts.

author: aroxarth
body:
## Resumen

Agrega una **ventana de historial** de la conversación: un botón **📜 Historial** que
abre, en una ventana aparte, todas las preguntas con su respuesta (inglés) y su
traducción (español). Nace de una necesidad real de uso: a veces uno olvida qué le
preguntaron, y aunque la IA ya lo tiene en memoria, no había forma de repasarlo.

## ✨ Mejora aplicada

- **Botón 📜 Historial** entre *Escuchar* y *Nueva conversación*. Al hacer clic, abre una
  ventana movible con la lista numerada de intercambios:
  - ❓ la pregunta detectada
  - 🗣️ la respuesta en inglés (lo que uno dice)
  - 👁️ la traducción en español (para entender)
- **Registro independiente de la memoria de la IA.** La memoria interna se recorta a
  `MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGES` para controlar el costo en tokens; el historial visible **no se
  recorta**, así se pueden repasar TODAS las preguntas de la conversación aunque sean
  muchas.
- **Se actualiza en vivo** si la ventana queda abierta mientras entran preguntas nuevas.
- **Se borra con "Nueva conversación"**, ya que el historial está atado a la conversación
  actual.

## 🔧 Detalles técnicos

- El `CopilotWorker` emite una señal `exchange_recorded(question, answer, translation)`
  cuando termina una respuesta (después de traducir).
- El `Overlay` mantiene `history_log` (lista de intercambios) y lo renderiza como HTML en
  un `QTextEdit` de solo lectura dentro de un `QDialog`.
- El texto se escapa con `html.escape`, de modo que preguntas o respuestas con `<`, `>` o
  `&` no rompen el renderizado.

## ✅ Cómo se probó

- Generación del HTML verificada con caracteres especiales (`<thread> & process`) y saltos
  de línea: se escapa y formatea correctamente.
- Caso vacío manejado (mensaje "Todavía no hay preguntas...").
- Compila e importa sin errores; validado en la app: el botón abre la ventana y "Nueva
  conversación" la vacía.

## 📝 Notas

- La ventana es independiente del overlay principal (se puede mover y cerrar sin afectar
  la escucha).
- No se agregan dependencias nuevas: usa solo PySide6 y la stdlib (`html`).
