author: theboycoder
body:
## Bug
On `https://stellarlight.xyz/leaderboard`, every project row shows `—` for Stars / Issues / Repos / Last commit, and the ranking is wrong (no-signal projects float to the top).

## Root cause
`/api/leaderboard` was migrated to read GitHub stats from the enriched **`repos`** collection — its own comment says *"The legacy `signals` cache this endpoint used is no longer populated, so every project read back as zeros."* But the **`/leaderboard` page** was never migrated: it still queries the dead `signals` collection directly, so every row reads back blank, and with all `lastActivityAt` null the activity sort collapses.

Diagnosis (live): the uncached API returns 50/50 projects with real stats (Keybase 9,219★, etc.); the page returns 0/50 with the identical query — because the page's `signals` source is empty. Page renders fast (0.65s), so it's not an M0 timeout — it's the wrong (dead) data source.

The Electric Capital block (`<EcosystemDevStats/>`, static JSON) was unaffected and already renders.

## Fix
The page now consumes `/api/leaderboard` (the single source of truth — reads `repos`, applies sort/range/category/limit server-side) instead of re-querying Payload's dead `signals`. This also deletes the duplicated query logic that let the two drift apart in the first place (−122/+50).

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck` clean.
- Will verify live post-deploy: `/leaderboard` rows show real stars/issues/repos, sorted by activity.

body:
## Summary
- Adds device-specific BKCs for NVIDIA's official `nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4` ModelOpt checkpoint targeting RTX PRO 6000 and 1x GB10 / DGX Spark.
- Uses the NVIDIA model-card launch shape: `--quantization modelopt`, 262K context, FP8 KV cache, and `--reasoning-parser qwen3`.
- Keeps the existing community `sakamakismile` Qwen3.6 BKCs unchanged and adds exact-model lookup/device-selection tests.

## Research notes
- The requested `nvidia/Qwen3.5-27B-NVFP4` / `NVPF4` name does not exist as an NVIDIA-owned HF repo. NVIDIA's current public 27B NVFP4 release is `nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4` (released 2026-06-26; updated 2026-06-30).
- NVIDIA's model card recommends `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`; the GB10 entry uses Yokai's existing NGC Spark image and notes that it may need an aarch64 nightly image if NGC lags ModelOpt NVFP4 runtime support.
- `hf-mem`: weights 21,921,428,072 bytes; 262K FP8 KV cache 28,588,376,064 bytes; 262K BF16 KV cache 57,176,752,128 bytes.

## Validation
- `/usr/local/go/bin/go test ./internal/bkc`

author: tupe12334
body:
## Why

`app/opengraph-image.tsx` and `app/twitter-image.tsx` were the only two route files under `app/` with no test file — every other route (`layout.tsx`, `page.tsx`, `not-found.tsx`, `robots.ts`, `sitemap.ts`) and component (`ExternalLink.tsx`) has one. A regression here (e.g. accidentally dropping `export const dynamic = "force-static"`, which breaks `next build` under `output: "export"`, or `twitter-image.tsx` drifting into a hand-copy instead of re-exporting `opengraph-image`) would only surface at build time instead of failing fast in `npm test`.

I checked the ~100 open PRs on this repo first (many cover SEO/a11y/JSON-LD/CSS-token work, including one that restyles this same card, #261) — none add test coverage for these two files, so this doesn't duplicate anything in the backlog.

## What

- `app/opengraph-image.test.tsx` — asserts the `force-static` export, the `1200x630` OG dimensions, the `image/png` content type, and the alt text.
- `app/twitter-image.test.tsx` — asserts it genuinely re-exports (identity, not a copy of) `opengraph-image`'s `size`/`contentType`/`alt`/default renderer, so the two cards can never silently diverge.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased] / Added`, matching this repo's existing convention.

Note: I verified that fully rendering the `ImageResponse` (SVG → PNG via `resvg-wasm`) does not work under the `jsdom`/vitest setup used here (`Unsupported input` error from the wasm decoder), so these tests target the route's static config/exports instead — the same level of coverage `robots.test.ts` and `sitemap.test.ts` already use for their routes.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm test` — all passing (8 files / 21 tests, including the 2 new files)
- [x] `npm run build` — static export succeeds, `/opengraph-image` and `/twitter-image` still prerender

This pull request was opened by the Daemon + Landing auto-improve & auto-merge lint/docs PRs routine of moadim.

author: shawzg
body:
Fixes CVEs in the base/generic images, primarily through **component version bumps** and **reworking how `jq` is installed**. Version bumped `2.3.7` → `2.3.8`.

## Changes

### `base/Dockerfile`

**Version upgrades (CVE fixes):**

| Component | Old | New |
|-----------|-----|-----|
| Go (git-lfs build) | 1.26.2 | 1.26.4 |
| docker buildx | v0.34.0 | v0.35.0 |
| docker compose | v5.1.3 | v5.2.0 |
| helm | v4.2.0 | v4.2.2 |
| kubectl | v1.36.1 | v1.36.2 |

**Structural rework:**

- Added a global `apt-get upgrade` to pull the latest patched distro package versions.
- `jq` now installed as a static binary (1.8.1) in the base image at `/usr/local/bin`, avoiding the vulnerable distro `jq`/`libjq1`/`libonig5` packages (e.g. CVE-2026-43895/43896/44777/41256/41257).
- Modernized APT keys: HashiCorp and Azure repos now use the `signed-by` keyring approach, dropping the deprecated `apt-key add` / `apt-add-repository`.
- Merged RUN layers and consistent `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` cleanup to shrink the image.
- Fixed typo: `azure-cl.list` → `azure-cli.list`.

### `generic/Dockerfile`

- Go SDK `1.26.3` → `1.26.4` (with updated hash).
- Removed the local `jq` install block — now inherits the static `jq` from the base image, removing duplication.

### `claude_code/install-claude.sh`

- Dropped `jq` from the apt install list (`ca-certificates curl jq` → `ca-certificates curl`), since `jq` now comes from the base image.

### `VERSION`

- Bumped `2.3.7` → `2.3.8`.

## Net effect

Consolidated `jq` into a single hardened static binary in the base image, bumped all tooling to CVE-patched versions, and modernized/slimmed the Dockerfile layers.

author: jjackson
body:
## Product Description

Opening the **Audit Program Report** used to land on a dead-end: "No rollup yet — click Refresh data", and clicking it still showed "0 opportunities · 0 weeks". A report should just load. Now the PAR **loads itself on open** — it pulls the watched creator's audit runs into the week × opportunity grid automatically. The action button reads **"Load report"** (empty) / **"Update"** (to pull newer runs) instead of the confusing "Refresh data", and if you haven't set a reporting window it simply shows **all** of the creator's runs.

## Technical Summary

- **Render:** a mount `useEffect` auto-runs the `audit_par_rollup` job once when the report is live and empty; button label is context-aware; empty-state copy reflects loading / no-runs instead of "click Refresh".
- **Handler (`audit_par_rollup`):** builds the compute state from the workflow **definition config** (`watched_source` + optional window) overlaid by run state, so the rollup works straight from config with nothing pre-seeded into run state (previously it errored `missing_window` because run state was empty).
- **Rollup (`compute_audit_par_rollup`):** the report window is now **optional** — with no window, every one of the watched creator's runs is included; only a missing watched creator (`creator_definition_id`) errors (`missing_source`).

## Safety Assurance

### Safety story
Render + handler + rollup for one template; no models/migrations. Strictly more usable — it removes a manual step and a broken empty state, and broadens the rollup to include all runs when unwindowed. Completed (frozen) reports are unaffected (auto-run skips them). Render transpile-verified.

### Automated test coverage
`test_audit_par.py`: renamed missing-window→`missing_source`; added a test that with no window every creator run is included; existing per-opp/per-week + scoping tests still pass (6 total).

### QA Plan
Open a fresh PAR run → it auto-loads and shows the creator's runs (or "no runs yet" if none), no manual Refresh needed; "Update" re-pulls.

### Labels & Review
- [ ] The set of people pinged as reviewers is appropriate for the level of risk of the change

author: lochinan
body:
## Problem

The AuraBuff reminder icon labels were hardcoded English: spell-based labels used the hardcoded English spell name, and non-spell consumable labels (Flask, Food, HS, Whistle, Rune, Felguard, Inky, Augment Rune, Main/Off Hand) were plain English literals. So the reminders stayed English regardless of client locale.

## Change

Localize the labels in both the live reminders (`EllesmereUIAuraBuffReminders.lua`) and the options preview (`EUI_AuraBuffReminders_Options.lua`):

- **Spell names**: resolve buff / aura / poison / rite / imbue names from their spell ID in the client's locale via a new `_G._EABR_SpellName` helper (English fallback), so labels use the game's localized spell name.
- **Consumables**: wrap the non-spell labels in `EllesmereUI.L()` — Flask, Food, HS, Whistle, Rune, Felguard, plus the `ShortLabel`-derived Augment Rune / Inky Black Potion / Main Hand / Off Hand.

Labels are display-only (selection keys live in `itemKey` / `dismissKey`), so logic is unaffected; `L()` falls back to English for unkeyed strings.

## Testing
`/reload` with zhTW active — reminder icon labels (spells + consumables) render localized; click-to-buff/dismiss still works; no Lua errors.

## Note
Depends on the matching zhTW keys (added in the separate zhTW PR) to display in Traditional Chinese; until merged, unkeyed strings fall back to English.

author: valyord
body:
## Context

The current `app/page.tsx` is a "coming soon" placeholder and `app/layout.tsx` has no shared chrome. This task wires up the persistent **Header** and **Footer** used on every page, and builds the **Hero search section** — the above-the-fold area of the Home page (`/`). Everything below the fold (QuickCards, FeaturedCarousel, BrowseByCity, etc.) is out of scope and will follow in a separate task.

Spec references:
- `docs/en/00-PRODUCT-SPEC.md` §8 (design system / tokens) and §9 (Header/Footer anatomy)
- `docs/en/pages/01-home.md` §2 (layout tokens), §3.1 (Header), §3.2 (Hero + search), §5 (component tree), §6 (responsive), §7 (a11y), §8 (SEO/meta)

Stack: **Next.js 15 App Router · TypeScript · Tailwind CSS · shadcn/ui · next-intl**. i18n locale routing (`/hy`, `/ru`, `/en`) is **not** required in this task — use the default `/` route with English microcopy. No Supabase calls yet; all data is static/hardcoded.

---

## What to build

### 1 — `<Header />` — `components/layout/Header.tsx` (Client Component)

Sticky (`sticky top-0 z-50`). On the hero: transparent/translucent; after scroll past 64 px: `bg-white shadow-sm` with a CSS transition (`transition-colors duration-200`).

**Left:** Logo text or SVG placeholder → `href="/"`.

**Center (≥1024px):** Nav links — **Buy · Sell · Rent · Mortgage · Find an Agent · News & Guides**. Each opens a **mega-menu dropdown** on hover/focus. Mega-menu content per §9 of the product spec (static links, no data fetch). Below 1024 px the center nav collapses into a hamburger drawer.

**Right (desktop):**
- ♡ Favorites icon → `/favorites`
- 🔔 Notifications icon → `/notifications`
- 🌐 Language switcher chip `HY / RU / EN` (toggle UI only, no routing change required)
- 💱 Currency switcher chip `AMD / USD / EUR / RUB` (toggle UI only)
- **[Post a property]** — primary button → `/sell/new`
- 👤 **[Sign in]** ghost button → `/auth/login`

**Mobile (<1024px):** hamburger icon opens a slide-in drawer with the nav links + utility actions stacked vertically.

### 2 — `<Footer />` — `components/layout/Footer.tsx` (Server Component)

Five columns (≥768px) / single accordion stack (mobile):
1. **Company** — About us, Careers, Contact, Press
2. **Buyer / Seller** — Buy, Sell, Rent, Mortgage
3. **Resources** — Guides, Blog, FAQ, Help center
4. **Legal** — Terms, Privacy, Cookie policy
5. **Contact** — social icons (placeholder hrefs), language/currency toggles

Bottom bar: `© 2026 Real Estate Platform. All rights reserved.`

### 3 — Wire chrome into `app/layout.tsx`

Import `<Header />` and `<Footer />` into the root layout so they appear on every page.

### 4 — `<HeroSearch />` — `components/home/HeroSearch.tsx` (Client Component)

Full-bleed hero, `h-[440px] md:h-[520px]`, background: `next/image` with `priority` + `fill` + `object-cover` (use a placeholder `/public/hero.jpg` — any real photo of Yerevan, or a gradient fallback). Overlay: `absolute inset-0 bg-black/40`.

**H1** — `"Find your home in Armenia"` — `text-2xl md:text-4xl font-bold text-white leading-tight`.
**Subtitle** — `"10,000+ verified listings in one place"` — `text-base md:text-lg text-white/80 mt-3`.

**Search card** (`bg-white rounded-xl shadow-lg p-2 max-w-2xl mx-auto mt-8`):

- **Tabs row** — `[Buy] [Rent] [Sell] [Estimate]`; active: `bg-primary text-white rounded-md px-4 h-10 font-medium`; inactive: `text-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-100 rounded-md px-4 h-10`. Tab state lives in local React state.
- **Input row** (hidden when "Sell" tab is active):
  - Text input — `h-12 flex-1 px-4 text-base outline-none` — placeholder changes per tab:
    - Buy / Rent → `"City, district, address…"`
    - Estimate → `"Enter address for an estimate"`
  - **[🔍 Search]** button — `bg-primary text-white h-12 px-6 rounded-lg font-medium hover:bg-primary/90` — navigates on click:
    - Buy → `/search?deal=sale&q={input}`
    - Rent → `/search?deal=rent&q={input}`
    - Estimate → `/home-value?address={input}`
    - Empty input → navigates without `q` param (browse all)
  - Pressing **Enter** in the input submits the same way.
- **"Sell" tab active** — hide the input; show a single full-width **[Post a property →]** button → `/sell/new`.
- On mobile (`<768px`) the input and button stack `flex-col gap-2`.

*Autocomplete dropdown is **out of scope** for this task — the input is plain `<input>`, no suggestions.*

### 5 — `app/page.tsx` — Home page shell

Replace the placeholder with:
```tsx
import HeroSearch from '@/components/home/HeroSearch'

export default function HomePage() {
  return (
    <main>
      <HeroSearch />
      {/* below-the-fold sections — next task */}
    </main>
  )
}
```

### 6 — Design tokens

Ensure Tailwind config has `primary` mapped (e.g. `#2563EB` blue or a green chosen for the brand — pick one and commit it). shadcn/ui `Button`, `Tabs`, and `Sheet` (for mobile drawer) components should be installed if not already present.

### 7 — SEO / meta (`app/layout.tsx`)

```tsx
export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: 'Real Estate Platform — Buy, Sell & Rent in Armenia',
  description: 'Find 10,000+ verified property listings in Armenia. Buy, sell or rent apartments, houses and land.',
}
```

Add `lang="hy"` default on `<html>` (will be dynamic when i18n is wired up).

---

## Out of scope (next tasks)

- Autocomplete / geo suggestions on the search input
- QuickCards, FeaturedCarousel, BrowseByCity, PropertyTypeShortcuts, CTA banner, Tools, StatsStrip, LatestBlog, RecentlyViewed sections
- i18n / locale routing
- Supabase auth integration (header shows static Sign in button)
- Mega-menu data from API

Acceptance criteria:
### Functional

- [ ] Navigating to `/` renders the Header at the top, HeroSearch in the viewport, and Footer at the bottom — no "coming soon" placeholder.
- [ ] Header is transparent over the hero; scrolling ≥64 px transitions it to `bg-white shadow-sm`.
- [ ] On desktop (≥1024px) all six nav links are visible; hovering/focusing one opens its mega-menu dropdown with the correct static links.
- [ ] On mobile (<1024px) the nav links are hidden; tapping the hamburger icon opens a full-height slide-in drawer with all links.
- [ ] Header right side shows: ♡, 🔔, Language switcher (HY/RU/EN), Currency switcher (AMD/USD/EUR/RUB), [Post a property], [Sign in].
- [ ] Clicking **Buy** tab → input placeholder is "City, district, address…"; clicking [Search] with `q=Yerevan` navigates to `/search?deal=sale&q=Yerevan`.
- [ ] Clicking **Rent** tab → [Search] navigates to `/search?deal=rent&q=...`.
- [ ] Clicking **Estimate** tab → input placeholder is "Enter address for an estimate"; [Search] navigates to `/home-value?address=...`.
- [ ] Clicking **Sell** tab → input row disappears; a [Post a property →] button appears; clicking it navigates to `/sell/new`.
- [ ] Pressing **Enter** inside the search input performs the same navigation as clicking [Search].
- [ ] [Search] with empty input navigates to the tab destination without a `q` param (no empty `?q=` in URL).
- [ ] Footer renders five columns on ≥768px; stacks to an accordion on mobile. All links are crawlable `<a href>` elements.

### Visual / responsive

- [ ] Hero height is `440px` on mobile and `520px` on md+.
- [ ] H1 is `text-2xl` on mobile, `text-4xl` on md+; white; readable over the overlay.
- [ ] Search card input and button sit side-by-side on md+; stack vertically on mobile.
- [ ] Active tab has `bg-primary text-white`; inactive tabs have ghost style.
- [ ] [Post a property] in the header is styled as the primary button (matches `bg-primary text-white`).

### Code quality

- [ ] `<Header />` is a Client Component (`'use client'`) — it needs scroll + hover state; `<Footer />` and `<HomePage />` are Server Components.
- [ ] No `any` types; no `@ts-ignore` without comment; no `console.log`.
- [ ] `next/image` used for the hero background with `priority`, `fill`, and `object-cover`; `alt=""` (decorative).
- [ ] Heading hierarchy: one `<h1>` in the hero, footer/nav titles use `<h2>`/`<h3>`

author: matthewlew
body:
💡 What: 
- Added a global `:focus-visible` outline for interactive elements.
- Updated programmatic keyboard focus calls to use `{ preventScroll: true }` to avoid interrupting smooth scroll animations.
- Intercepted the 'Escape' key within focused inputs and textareas to blur them, allowing users to escape the input context and return to global shortcut navigation.

🎯 Why: 
Custom keyboard-navigable lists often suffer from glitches where native focus jumps interrupt intended smooth scrolling behavior, and custom CSS resets often strip default focus indicators, making the app difficult for keyboard users to navigate.

📸 Before/After: 
Before: Navigating filter pills with the keyboard provided no visual feedback, and pressing `Escape` while typing did not blur the input.
After: Filter pills (and all interactive elements) receive a clear focus outline, and pressing `Escape` successfully blurs inputs to restore shortcut navigation.

♿ Accessibility: 
Ensures all interactive elements have visible focus indicators and that focus management smoothly integrates with programmatic scrolling.

개인 자산 포트폴리오 **리밸런싱**을 지원하는 Flutter 크로스플랫폼 앱(iPhone 우선)을 `asset_rebalancing/` 하위에 추가합니다. 오프라인 우선·로컬 저장·로그인 불필요. 기존 사다리 게임 파일은 그대로 보존했습니다.

## 주요 변경
- **데이터 모델**: `Asset` / `History` / `Snapshot` / `RebalanceResult` + enum(카테고리·이력유형·모드)

  - 추가금 매수만(No-Sell): 부족분 비율 배분, 매도 없음

- **붙여넣기 파서** (`services/parser_service.dart`): 마크다운 표 / CSV / JSON 3형식 자동 인식, `₩·원·,·%` 제거, 실패 줄 안내

body:
## What
Migrate the **ttnn-ops dataset** (backing the model-traced / lead-models sweeps) from Neon (Postgres) to the org **Snowflake** warehouse, and adopt Data Central's managed **SELF_SERVE** model. Both read/reconstruct and write/ingest run on Snowflake; the Neon backend is fully removed from the loader.

## Access model (managed SELF_SERVE)
The shared `SELF_SERVE` role (granted to `PUBLIC`) was the root cause of "everyone can read/write" and is deprecated. Data lives in `SELF_SERVE.TTNN_OPS_V6`, provisioned via Data Central with two per-project roles:
- **`SELF_SERVE_OWNER_TTNN_OPS_V6`** — write (ingest/DDL)
- **`SELF_SERVE_READER_TTNN_OPS_V6`** — read-only (CI reconstruct, sharing)

Read-only is now enforceable (verified: reader role reads, writes denied).

## Changes
- **`tests/sweep_framework/load_ttnn_ops_data_v2.py`** — Snowflake-only DB layer: keypair/SSO auth (default role = reader; owner to write), `SEQUENCE`-based ids, `get_or_create`/`MERGE` upserts, **batched** bulk config `INSERT` + link `MERGE` (full 27k-config load ~7 min vs ~38 h row-by-row), Snowflake-dialect reconstruct (one bulk source-fetch per op). `psycopg2`/Neon removed.
- **`model_tracer/create_ttnn_ops_schema_v6_snowflake.sql`** — reproducible Snowflake DDL (`SERIAL`→`NUMBER`+sequences, `JSONB`→`VARCHAR` exact round-trip, `int[]`→`ARRAY`, non-enforced PK/UNIQUE/FK); `CREATE OR REPLACE` tables inside the pre-provisioned schema (run as owner).
- **`.github/workflows/ttnn-run-sweeps.yaml`** — reconstruct job reads Snowflake with the **reader** role; only secret is `SWEEPS_SNOWFLAKE_KEY`; deps swap `psycopg2`→`snowflake-connector-python`/`cryptography`. The separate results-write step (`push_sweep_results.py`, `TTNN_OPS_DATABASE_URL`) is unchanged — not Neon, out of scope.
- **`tests/sweep_framework/test_load_ttnn_ops_data_v2_functional.py`** — the old mocked-`psycopg2` DB tests are replaced with a gated Snowflake integration test (real load→reconstruct round-trip against a pre-provisioned scratch schema via `TTNN_OPS_TEST_SCHEMA`; skips otherwise). 52 unit tests unchanged.
- **`model_tracer/GUIDE.md` + `README.md`** — rewritten for Snowflake: connection/env, prerequisites, a **Snowflake Reference** cheat-sheet (provision schema, create tables, load, reconstruct, grant read/write), and write examples using the owner role.

## Validation
- Reconstruct output **byte-identical to Neon** across `reconstruct-op`, `reconstruct-trace`, full `reconstruct-manifest` (18,154 configs).
- Data faithfully re-migrated into the new owner-role schema: **27,139 configs, all 10 tables match**.
- Functional tests: 52 passed, 3 skipped (integration gated) / 0 failed.

## Before merge
- Set repo secret **`SWEEPS_SNOWFLAKE_KEY`** (service-account private key PEM). The service account (`SVC_TTOPS_SWEEPS`) holds the reader role for CI reads (and owner for ingest).

author: pradeep0153
body:
Closes #3932.

### Description
This PR drastically reduces friction for returning students by instantly routing them exactly back to where they left off the previous day, right from the main dashboard.

### Changes Made
- Engineered a complex new backend query to identify the user's most recently interacted `CourseSession`. The API now tracks and returns the specific `course_id`, `lecture_id`, and exact `video_timestamp` (in seconds) of their last active session across all enrolled courses.
- Designed and built a massive, visually striking "Hero" widget that spans the top of the student dashboard.
- The widget dynamically loads the high-resolution cover image of the user's most recent course, overlays the title of the specific lecture they were watching, and features a highly prominent "Resume Lecture X" Call-to-Action button.
- Clicking the button bypasses the standard course landing page and syllabus entirely, deep-linking the user directly into the video player, automatically seeking to the precise second they stopped watching yesterday.

### Impact
- **Frictionless Re-engagement:** Previously, a student logging in to study had to manually locate the correct course tile in their grid, click it, wait for the syllabus to load, try to remember which section they were in, click the specific lecture, and manually scrub the video to find their place. This cumbersome multi-step process killed momentum. By providing a one-click "Resume" shortcut at the very top of the page, we eliminate all navigational friction, making it effortlessly easy for students to dive straight back into deep learning the moment they log in.

author: barriehadfield
body:
Fixes two data-correctness defects in the email→`comms_log` write path that spec-341 shipped. No mail is sent or re-sent — data change only. Spec: `mindset-prod/memex-building-itself/specs/spec-442`.

## Defects
1. **Auth emails mis-typed `transactional`.** The magic-link and password-reset templates carried no `commsType`, so `recordEmailComm` defaulted them. (Verification email already set `email_verification` per spec-12.)
2. **`sent_at` never populated.** `recordComm` inserted `status='sent'` with `sent_at` NULL on every email.

## Fix
- **Templates** (`templates.ts`): stamp `commsType` `'magic_link'` / `'password_reset'` at the two auth builders so the type travels with the message.
- **Write path** (`comms-log.ts`): `recordComm` stamps `sent_at` (defaults to `now()`) for any resolved `status='sent'` row lacking one — holds for **every** caller. `recordEmailComm` forwards an optional `sentAt`.
- **Send time** (`sender.ts`): `PostmarkEmailSender` reads `SubmittedAt` from the Postmark response and threads it as the real send time (fallback `now()`).
- **Migration `0120`** (+ revert): re-types existing auth emails by subject; backfills `sent_at = created_at` for historical `sent`/NULL rows (documented approximation — no `comms_event` delivery time exists for them); adds CHECK `comms_log_sent_requires_sent_at` (`status <> 'sent' OR sent_at IS NOT NULL`) as **NOT VALID → VALIDATE** after the backfill. Mirrored in `schema.ts`.

`comms_log` stays user-keyed, RLS-excluded, and outside `mutate()` (spec-6 — unchanged; no `memex_id`, per dec-5).

## Testing
- 3 new tagged test files (type mapping, `sent_at` stamping + `SubmittedAt` threading, CHECK rejection, `0120` type-remap over seeded rows) — **ac-1…ac-9 all verified**.
- Updated 3 pre-existing fixtures that seeded invalid `sent`/NULL rows.
- **Full server suite green** (5137 passed; a first run's 7 failures were confirmed flaky parallel-DB teardown races — pass in isolation, clean on re-run). `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Notes for reviewers
- The task's "wire up Postmark delivery-webhook ingestion into `comms_event`" follow-up is **already built** (spec-12 t-2, `routes/postmark-webhook.ts`); the empty table reflects no delivery webhooks received in-env, not missing code. Once those flow, real delivery data replaces the `created_at` approximation.
- The `sent_at=created_at` backfill's positive path can't be unit-tested after the fact (the new CHECK forbids creating the precondition); its end-state is guaranteed by the CHECK (ac-7). The type-remap half is tested directly.

author: joeborrello
body:
## JOE-33 — Daily map future match-ups

On the daily map, when a knockout day's fixtures aren't yet decided, a slot used to render as a bare placeholder (`W74`, `1E`) with a `?` flag. This surfaces the **teams that may end up playing** there instead.

### How it works
- **`predict.slot_candidates`** — reuses the existing projected-bracket Monte-Carlo aggregate (same cache as the Predictions page / bracket) to tally, per knockout slot and side, the top few teams by how often the sims land them there, with their marginal probability. No extra simulation cost once the aggregate is warm.
- **`/api/matches`** — attaches `team{1,2}_candidates` (`team` + flag `code` + `p`) to every **undecided** knockout side only. Decided sides keep their real team and get no list; the group stage is untouched.
- **Daily map (`map.js` / `style.css`)** — renders a "may play" cluster:
  - **Pin:** the favourite's flag, dimmed, with a `?` corner (full odds in the tooltip).
  - **Side panel & popup:** flag + name + odds chips, e.g. *Winner Grp E → 🇩🇪 Germany 42% or 🇭🇷 Croatia 18%*.

Raw slot placeholders are humanized (`W74` → "Winner match 74", `1E` → "Winner Grp E", `3A/B/C/D` → "3rd place …").

### Tests
- New `tests/test_daily_map_future_matchups.py` covers the engine (shape, validity, `top` limit, open-field coverage), the API plumbing (candidates attached only to undecided knockout sides; none on the group stage), and the client wiring (map.js / CSS).

author: tchiayan92
body:
## Summary

Adds an **LLM (Human MOS) label-export path** to Autotrain, the counterpart to the
existing TTS export. After a `task_type=llm` run finishes, the gateway generates
one assistant response per eval row on the run's VM using the finetuned model,
then creates a Label-platform **`human_mos`** project seeded with those
conversations for human MOS scoring.

Both commits are here:
- `feat(autotrain): Automoted Human MOS generation` — the feature
- `fix(autotrain): label export` — the `_ssh_put_bytes` fix (see below)

## What's new

**Gateway**
- `gateway/gateway/training/llm/llm_label_export.py` (new) — ships to the run's VM,
  downloads the LoRA checkpoint, merges it into the base Gemma-4 model, generates
  a response per eval row, and emits a parsed `@@LABEL {"items":[…]}` manifest.
- `training_api.py`:
  - `_create_llm_label_project_for_run` — orchestrates the VM generation, then
    creates the `human_mos` project, sets MOS axes, and batch-imports the
    conversations as tasks; round-trips a `kind=label` Dataset.
  - `_fetch_eval_rows_from_catalog` — pulls eval rows (JSONL) from a catalog dataset.
  - `_run_llm_label_export_ssh` — ships the `llm/` dir + streams the export log.
  - Wires the LLM branch into the post-run and retry-export dispatch, plus the
    `llm_label_*` config fields and `LabelExportRequest` LLM overrides.

**Web**
- `label-export-tab.tsx` — `isLlm` branch: eval dataset / responses / max-new-tokens /
  MOS-axes knobs replace the TTS controls; branched submit payload.
- `training-form.tsx` — LLM label-export config on the New Training form.
- `training-detail.tsx` — `canLabelExport` now includes `llm` runs; project card
  shows "N conversations" for `human_mos` (vs "N clips" for TTS).
- `gateway.ts` / `types.ts` — LLM override fields + `project_type` on `LabelProjectCard`.

## Why the TTS/LLM export scripts differ (by design)

TTS synthesizes binary WAV clips and uploads each to **S3** from the VM (a Label
task only carries a filename). LLM outputs are plain text small enough to ride back
in the `@@LABEL` manifest, so there's no per-item S3 upload — the gateway
batch-imports all conversations in one `POST /api/projects/{pid}/tasks`.

## Bug fix included: "Argument list too long"

`_ssh_put` base64-encodes the config into a single argv arg; with ~100 eval rows
embedded it blew past `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (~128 KB) → `/bin/bash: Argument list too long`.
Switched the label-config write to `_ssh_put_bytes` (stdin streaming, no argv limit).

## Testing

- `python -m py_compile gateway/gateway/training_api.py` — clean
- `tsc --noEmit` (web) — clean, exit 0
- Rebased cleanly onto latest `main` (`added region`); conflicts in the
  `label_*` config-key list and the export payload resolved keep-both.

body:
## Summary
- All 13 open [code scanning alerts](https://github.com/joszz/GarageStack/security/code-scanning) are the same root cause: `libexpat` in the `garagestack-frontend` image is stuck on `2.8.1-r0` (fix is `2.8.2-r0`).
- The Dockerfile already runs `apk upgrade --no-cache`, but `docker-publish.yml` builds with a persistent GHA layer cache, so that RUN layer was reused from before the fix was published upstream and never actually re-executed, even on the weekly scheduled rebuild meant to catch new OS patches. Confirmed by pulling the published image: it had `libexpat-2.8.1-r0` even though Alpine 3.23's repo already serves `2.8.2-r0`.
- Adds an `OS_PATCH_DATE` build-arg (refreshed daily in CI) referenced inside the `apk upgrade` RUN commands in `frontend/Dockerfile`, so that layer's cache key changes and it actually re-runs.

## Test plan
- [x] Built `frontend/Dockerfile` locally with the new build-arg and confirmed the resulting image reports `libexpat-2.8.2-r0` installed (was `2.8.1-r0` before the change).

body: ## Problem After PR #53, sync-landing failed with: ``` error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: scripts/merge-main-into-landing.mjs Merge with strategy ort failed. Unhandled merge conflict(s): (none) ``` PR #53 checked out `main`'s merge script onto the `landing` worktree before running `git merge`, leaving uncommitted changes that blocked the merge. ## Fix Write the script to `/tmp` and run it from there — the landing worktree stays clean. ```bash git show origin/main:scripts/merge-main-into-landing.mjs > /tmp/merge-main-into-landing.mjs node /tmp/merge-main-into-landing.mjs ``` Verified locally: merge completes successfully with this approach.

author: lifelonglazylearner
body:
Closes the v0.8.1 roadmap item ([`docs/agentskills-review.md`](https://github.com/LifelongLazyLearner/qu-ai-wei/blob/main/docs/agentskills-review.md) \"已知盲区\"): `check-version-sync.sh` only checked version *strings*, not flat-build content, so editing `SKILL.md`/`references/` without re-running `build-flat.sh` would silently ship a stale `.cursorrules`/`WARP.md`. This was the engineering reviewer's recurring concern across all three review rounds of v0.8.1.

## What's new

**`tests/check-flat-sync.sh`** — flat-build determinism guard:
1. Copies `SKILL.md` + `references/*.md` + `scripts/build-flat.sh` into a temp dir
2. Runs `build-flat.sh` there (it resolves `DIR` via `BASH_SOURCE`, so regeneration writes inside the temp dir — the working tree is never touched)
3. Diffs the temp-generated `.cursorrules`/`WARP.md` against the committed ones byte-for-byte (`cmp`)
4. On drift: fails + prints the diff + the fix command (`bash scripts/build-flat.sh && git add .cursorrules WARP.md`)

**Future-proofing:** the `references/*.md` glob auto-copies any new reference file; `build-flat.sh`'s own `[ -f ] || exit 1` existence guard makes any missing temp source fail loudly rather than silently false-pass.

## Design choice
Temp-dir regeneration (not in-place) because a *check* script should have no side effects — in-place would mutate the working tree and conflict with pre-commit staging / dirty CI checkouts. The `BASH_SOURCE`-based `DIR` resolution in `build-flat.sh:13` was evidently designed to support exactly this pattern.

No rule change, no behavior change. Flat files differ only in the version banner (0.8.1 → 0.8.2).

## Verification
All gates pass:
```
build-flat.sh, check-version-sync.sh, check-flat-sync.sh,
check-snapshot-smoke.sh, check-runs.sh tests/after, check-triggers.sh
```

## Review process
AGENTS.md public-face commit gate — three reviewer verdicts (final round):
- **[CEO: APPROVE]** — version bump consistent with precedent (v0.6.5 was also a test-coverage-only release)
- **[中文 authentic: APPROVE]**
- **[Engineering: APPROVE]** — verified BASH_SOURCE isolation, copy completeness, no false-pass risk, temp-dir design sound

author: zarand3r
body:
Follow-up to a critical review of the merged P1 foundation. Two contract bugs in `slate_enums`, both **masked because the unit test asserted my inference rather than the consumer's actual contract**.

## 🔴 Bug 1 — reflection names were missing their prefixes (crash)

`SlateLayout.cc:83/88/91` formats sym names as `get(access).substr(strlen("slate_"))` and `get(shard).substr(strlen("shard_"))`. My names lacked the 6-char prefixes, so `"read_only".substr(6)` → `"nly"` and `"sync".substr(6)` (4 chars) → **`std::out_of_range` throw**. Now registers `"shard_*"` / `"slate_*"`; the test asserts the post-`substr` result matches the consumer.

## 🔴 Bug 2 — permission model forbade control from creating `cyclic`/`static`

The control instance is built with `deny(rwc, c_nonsync)` (`FtRuntime.cc:156`, `slate_control_sync_only`) yet `BasicControl` creates `reset_counters` / `autosequence_begin`/`end` in **`shard_cyclic`** through that handle. My model treated every non-sync shard as nonsync-class → control creation of cyclic rejected. Fix: three-way classification — `sync*` needs `c_sync`, `nonsync*` needs `c_nonsync`, `static`/`cyclic` need only the general create bit (now load-bearing). P3's boundary is preserved (runtime can't create sync; control can't create nonsync).

## Notes recorded (not fixed here)
- `slate_id::is_valid` relies on layout indices ≥ 1 — **must be enforced in `SlatePathMap`** (not yet built); top latent risk.
- `slate_id`: `offset > kOffsetMax` is a dead defensive check (`slate_offset_t` is `UINT32`). Harmless.
- `SymbolTable::add(size_t, uint)` narrows for `StateMachine` callers — fine for realistic counts; revisit when StateMachine compiles.

## Verification
g++ `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` — **12/12** on the full integrated tree; Bazel green; valgrind clean; `docs/implementation.md` corrected.

author: zackees
body:
## Summary

Newer LPC845-BRK / LPCXpresso boards ship with NXP's LPC-Link2 CMSIS-DAP firmware pre-flashed on the on-board debug probe. That firmware presents the LPC845's USART0 as a VCOM alongside the CMSIS-DAP HID interface at VID:PID **1FC9:0132** (NXP's own VID), not the community-pool **16C0:0483** used by the older LPCXpresso VCOM firmware. `ci/util/port_utils.py` only knew about the latter, so `bash autoresearch lpc845brk` failed at port detection on any board with the newer firmware.

Change the map from single-VID:PID to tuple-of-VID:PIDs so an env accepts any of several firmware variants. All five LPC8xx canary envs now accept both fingerprints; the first port matching any listed pair wins.

## Backwards compat

- Renamed to `ENVIRONMENT_TO_VCOM_VID_PIDS` (plural).
- Kept `ENVIRONMENT_TO_VCOM_VID_PID` as a shim derived from the first entry per env — deprecated, slated for removal once no in-repo callers remain.
- Error message now lists BOTH accepted fingerprints when neither is found.

## Tests

`TestAutoDetectUploadPort` — 5/5 pass:

- New: `test_lpc845brk_lpcxpresso_vcom_fingerprint_matches`
- New: `test_lpc845brk_lpc_link2_cmsis_dap_fingerprint_matches`
- New: `test_lpc845brk_neither_fingerprint_matches_reports_both`
- Fixed a stale pre-existing assertion in `test_expected_environment_probe_failure_falls_back_to_descriptor` after #3446 dropped the explicit `timeout=3.0` override.

Ruff clean.

## Refs

- Unblocks the on-silicon `bash autoresearch --pwm-dma-cl` port detection for #3468's SCT+DMA channels-API validation harness.
- Adjacent to the #3300 / #3450 LPC restoration meta.

* **Bug Fixes**

  * Error messages now show all accepted fingerprints when no match is found, making setup issues easier to diagnose.

author: malachuk-josh
body:
## Summary

Debugging why the news brief still didn't generate after the API key + credits were added: the endpoint returns `found:false` for real, findable topics, which means the **web-search tool call is erroring** (likely web search isn't enabled on the account) — and the old code swallowed that as "not found," so the reader always showed the open-original fallback.

### Fix (`api/desk.js`, `src/App.jsx`)
- `fetchArticleBrief` now tries the **grounded web-search brief** first; if that errors or returns empty, it **falls back to a plain-Claude interpretive brief** from the headline (no live search). So a valid key always yields a readable brief.
- The fallback is clearly flagged in the UI: **"AI context brief · interpretation, not the original — verify at the source"** (vs. "grounded via web search" when search works).
- Adds a diagnostic `_err` field so the actual web-search error is visible on the production endpoint (I'll remove it once we've confirmed the cause).

### Next
Once deployed I'll re-hit the endpoint to read `_err` and confirm whether it's the web-search tool being disabled on the account (fixable in the Anthropic Console) or something else — either way the brief now works via the fallback.

### Testing
- `node --check api/desk.js` and `npm run build` pass.

… tokens

Rebuilds the login page from a functional-but-plain form into a hero surface comparable to Clerk/Auth0/Linear-style auth screens, and adds the reusable design-token layer other pages will draw on in later phases.

Design system additions (tailwind.config.ts / index.css):
- New shadow scale: shadow-elevated / elevated-lg (layered ambient shadows) and shadow-glow-brand-lg (large soft brand glow) alongside the existing card/glow tokens.
- New radius scale: card-lg (20px) / card-xl (28px) for hero surfaces.
- New `bg-aurora` gradient + `animate-aurora` keyframe — a slow-drifting multi-stop radial mesh, GPU-accelerated (transform/opacity only).
- New `animate-float` / `float-slow`, `animate-glow-pulse`, `animate- drift` (particle rise with per-instance horizontal sway via a `--drift-x` CSS custom property), and `animate-shake` (error feedback).
- New `.glass-panel` component class: heavier blur (28px + saturate), premium border/shadow treatment distinct from the existing `.glass- card` used elsewhere — reserved for hero surfaces (login, future splash/empty-state heroes), not the general card system.

New reusable components:
- AuroraBackground — full-bleed animated gradient mesh backdrop.
- ParticleField — ambient floating-particle layer, pure CSS animation (no per-frame JS), configurable particle count.

Login page rebuild (src/features/Login.tsx):
- Card grown from max-w-sm (384px) to max-w-[440px] with substantially more internal padding, sitting on the new .glass-panel treatment with a soft ambient glow blob and shadow-glow-brand-lg.
- Full-bleed AuroraBackground + ParticleField behind both the illustration and form panels (previously the radial glow was confined to one corner).
- Costorah logo now appears prominently in the card header on all breakpoints (previously desktop only showed it on the left panel, not within the form itself); left-panel mark gets a soft pulsing glow.

0600 temp .env, sets ENV_FILE_PATH so the child can locate it, and securely
deletes it on exit — independent of the clean|merge population mode. This

guard, user-supplied vars, and deprecating the legacy flags follow next.

author: usae4544-art
body:
🚨 **Severity:** MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability:** The application used `window.open(url, "_blank")` to open image downloads and full-size versions without specifying the `'noopener,noreferrer'` features. 
🎯 **Impact:** This omission exposes the application to Reverse Tabnabbing, a vulnerability where an opened third-party site could maliciously redirect the parent page using the `window.opener.location` API, potentially leading to phishing attacks if an attacker intercepts the destination URL or if the domain is taken over.
🔧 **Fix:** Added `"noopener,noreferrer"` as the third argument to the `window.open` calls in `index.html`. This ensures the newly opened tab runs in a separate process without a reference to the parent window and restricts referrer information.
✅ **Verification:** Started a local server and ran a Playwright test script (`verify_links.py`) that mocked `window.open` on the page and verified the correct arguments were passed when the 'Download HD' and 'Full Size' buttons were clicked. The automated tests passed successfully. The learning was also logged in `.jules/sentinel.md`.

author: avrabe
body:
Fixes #242.

## Bug
`dce-functions` removes/renumbers functions, but the `name` and `.debug_*` custom sections were passed through **byte-identical** over the changed index space. Surviving functions get **misattributed** names and dangling indices — silent debug-info corruption that Z3 and `wasm-tools validate` don't catch. Repro (from the issue):

```
before: name-section = {0:alpha, 1:dead, 2:gamma}
dce removes $dead (idx 1) -> survivors renumber
BUG:    func[1] (real gamma) labeled 'dead' + dangling entry at idx 2
```

## Fix
In `eliminate_dead_functions`, after the existing function-index remap:
- **`name`**: remap the function-names (id 1), local-names (id 2) and label-names (id 3) subsections through the same old→new remap — drop dead entries, renumber survivors, keep sorted. Module name (id 0) and non-function-indexed subsections (types/tables/memories/globals/elems/data) are preserved verbatim. If the section won't parse, it's **dropped** rather than risk misattribution.
- **`.debug_*`**: dropped — DWARF line tables reference code offsets that optimization changed and cannot be safely remapped.

Hand-rolled LEB/name-section codec (not wasm-encoder's `NameSection`) so it emits exactly the raw subsection payload loom stores, and a malformed section degrades to a drop instead of panicking.

## Verification
- Repro now yields `(export "gamma" (func $gamma))` — correct, no dangling index; module validates.
- Unit tests: remap (drop-dead + renumber + preserved subsections) and malformed-input→drop.

## Scope / follow-up
Covers the function-renumber path (the reported repro). Dropping `.debug_*` on body-changing transforms that **don't** renumber functions is a small follow-up in the CLI output path.

## CI note
The `WASM Build` check will be red until #243 (cranelift-isle 0.132 MSRV pin) merges — that's the pre-existing floating-deps failure, unrelated to this change.

author: sorryhyun
body:
## What

Adds `docs/proposal/reward_weighted_artist_lora.md` — a design-only proposal
(no code) for training an artist LoRA to learn the **style manifold** rather than
memorize the training images.

## The idea

Standard FM-to-image LoRA training has memorization as its global optimum on few
images — nothing in the loss rewards a *new* in-style sample. Swap the implicit
CFG reward (`log p(c|x)`) for an **explicit frozen verifier** and the adapter
becomes a policy `πθ(x|c) ∝ π_ref · exp(verifier/λ)` — the caption-dropout
unconditional is already `π_ref`.

Estimator is **reward-weighted regression (RAFT/ReST)**, deliberately not
policy-gradient or GAN:

- **Gradient never flows through the rollouts** — the reward only selects/weights
  the targets; the backward pass is bit-identical to the direct FM loss (safe +
  cheap). No head on the DiT.
- **Grow phase reuses the 4-step turbo student** (<1 s @ 1024²) stacked with the
  in-progress artist LoRA.
- **Why 28-step deployment stays healthy:** FM training is sampler-agnostic — we
  train on the turbo *output* `x0`, not its trajectory/step-count, so no few-step
  property transfers. What *does* transfer (turbo's collapsed/CFG=4 output
  distribution) is handled with a full-step candidate mix, accumulate-don't-replace
  real-image anchoring, a novelty term, and validation at the deployment config.

## Structure

Phase-gated with a **Phase-0 verifier-falsification gate** (if a frozen
feature-space judge can't separate held-out same-artist from the training set /
generic negatives, the program stops before any training). Matches the house
proposal style (premise sources, metric-trap priors, falsifiable gates, cost
accounting).

## Scope

Proposal doc only — no implementation, no bench, no config changes. Planned
`scripts/rwr/` and `bench/rwr/verifier_probe.py` are described, not added.

author: sebrbo
body:
## Summary

This PR clarifies and tightens the Combined mode Go/No-Go behavior around two explicit modes:

- `Stimulus color = Go/No-Go`
- `Background color = Go/No-Go`

The Go/No-Go color mapping is now fixed and consistent in both modes:

- Green (`#00aa00`) = Go
- Orange (`#ff8800`) = No-Go

## Before

Combined mode forced arrow stimuli and the option labeled `Use only arrows with random colors` pulled from the selected color list. That made the Go/No-Go rule ambiguous because the stimulus could use unrelated random colors. The background cue option also still operated inside an arrow-only Combined mode.

## After

Combined mode now builds its displayed content from the existing selected arrows, numbers, and letters. It no longer uses random selected colors for Go/No-Go.

- In stimulus-color mode, the displayed arrow, letter, or number is green for Go or orange for No-Go, with a neutral background.
- In background-color mode, the background is green for Go or orange for No-Go, while the displayed arrow, letter, or number stays neutral and readable.
- The existing ids for the two Combined mode checkboxes are preserved.
- The existing No-Go streak guard is preserved.
- Other modes, timings, cycles, sounds, countdown, fullscreen behavior, local storage, PWA files, service worker, and manifest were not modified.

The previous custom Go/No-Go color inputs were removed from the Combined UI because user-configurable cue colors conflicted with the requested fixed clinical convention: green = Go, orange = No-Go.

## Files changed

- `index.html`: updates Combined mode labels, helper text, and removes ambiguous/random-color wording and cue color pickers.
- `js/app.js`: changes Combined stimulus generation to support arrows, letters, and numbers in both Go/No-Go modes with fixed green/orange cue colors.
- `README.md`: updates EN/FR feature descriptions for the clarified Combined mode behavior.

## Validation

Automated/local checks run:

- `node --check js/app.js`
- `git diff --check`
- Local browser check on `http://localhost:4173`: Combined UI labels visible after enabling Combined mode, no console errors.
- Node DOM-simulation check using the real `js/app.js` generation functions for all six requested Combined scenarios.

Manual test scenarios documented for review:

1. Combined mode + Stimulus color = Go/No-Go + arrows: green arrow = Go, orange arrow = No-Go, no other stimulus colors.
2. Combined mode + Stimulus color = Go/No-Go + letters: green letter = Go, orange letter = No-Go, no other stimulus colors.
3. Combined mode + Stimulus color = Go/No-Go + numbers: green number = Go, orange number = No-Go, no other stimulus colors.
4. Combined mode + Background color = Go/No-Go + arrows: green background = Go, orange background = No-Go, arrow remains readable.
5. Combined mode + Background color = Go/No-Go + letters: green background = Go, orange background = No-Go, letter remains readable.
6. Combined mode + Background color = Go/No-Go + numbers: green background = Go, orange background = No-Go, number remains readable.
7. Other PhysioReact modes should continue to behave as before; this PR only changes Combined Go/No-Go handling.

author: com-junkawasaki
body:
## Phase 2.4 — CLJC system schedule (defsystem declare + dispatch)

Implements Phase 2.4 of the clj-wgsl migration (ADR-2607010930). Brings ECS
iteration into CLJ as a **data-first system schedule**.

### Core invariant
CLJ authors the system SCHEDULE as EDN — `{:system ident :order n :query
#{component-keys} :events #{…}}` — and `run-schedule` threads the ECS world
through each system in `:order`, handing each fn only the entities matching
its `:query` (via `kami.ecs/query`). The Rust host executes the archetypal
query (hecs) and hands bulk component buffers to WGSL compute. **CLJ does NOT
iterate per-entity on the hot path** (wasmi has no JIT — a per-entity CLJ
loop is unsafe); it declares + dispatches.

### The runner is coarse-grained by design (wasmi-safety)
`run-schedule` is a per-system reduce, NEVER a per-entity loop. It hands the
whole queried entity seq to each system fn once. Per-entity work is the fn's
job — expected to be O(1) in CLJ or a bulk dispatch to WGSL/native, not a
per-entity CLJ loop. Documented in the ns docstring.

### Changes (additive — `sim.cljc` untouched)
- New `kami.schedule` namespace (`src/kami/schedule.cljc`):
  - `schedule` — build + sort specs by `:order` (plain data)
  - `run-schedule` — pure reduce: thread `world`, hand each fn its queried ents
  - `defschedule` — optional CLJ macro to define (and optionally register) a schedule
  - `specs-by-system` — index by `:system` ident (tests/lint)
- New tests (`test/kami/schedule_test.cljc`, 7): a system receives ONLY
  entities matching its query; world is threaded in `:order`; the runner
  invokes each fn exactly once (not once per entity); nil-return is identity;
  empty query matches all; spec indexing.

### Test results
`clojure -M:test` in `kami-engine-sdk-clj/` — **53 tests, 184 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors.**
(Baseline was 46/167; +7 tests, +17 assertions.)

### Portability
Pure data, portable `.cljc`, no IO/GPU/atom. Matches surrounding ns style
(`fsm.cljc`, `sim.cljc`). Does not modify `sim.cljc`'s existing `defsystem`/`step`.

body:
The synthetic GGUF test builders and the native Q8_0 dense-manifest fixture no longer satisfied the stricter conversion invariants: the builders omitted now-required dense tensors (tripping the F3 shape/inventory checks), and the Q8_0 fixture used tensors whose element counts were not 32-block multiples (violating F6).

## Test fixtures
- **Repaired three synthetic builders** (`build_synth_gguf_arch_ext`, `build_synth_gguf_q4_0_per_expert`, `build_synth_gguf_mixed_per_expert`) to emit the full required dense set — `token_embd`, `output_norm`, `output`, `attn_q/k/v/output`, `ffn_norm`, `ffn_gate_inp` — using logically-correct shapes (GQA `synth_qkv_dims`, gate `[num_experts, d_model]`) rather than arbitrary squares.
- **Rebuilt the Q8_0 fixture** (`from_dir_loads_native_q8_dense_manifest_without_alias_files`) on a dedicated `d_model=32` config so every Q8_0 tensor is a whole-block multiple, keeping the F6 block-size check intact.

## Conversion inventory (`gguf_loader.rs`)
- Arch-aware required-tensor resolution via `resolve_conversion_profile`: QK-Norm (`attn_q_norm`/`attn_k_norm`, head-dim validated) required when `uses_qk_norm()`; routed MoE gate required with `[num_experts, d_model]` shape validation.
- Explicit `Unsupported` error for fused-QKV (Phi) and MLA (DeepSeek-V2/V3) families instead of silently demanding nonexistent separate Q/K/V tensors.

## Tied output head
- Manifest `tied_to` entries are validated in `dense_tensor.rs` (empty file, zero byte_len, existing target) and resolved in `model.rs::try_load_dense_weight`, reconstructing the LM head from the token embedding.

author: serhiy-storchaka
body:
When `idle.py` is run as a script, its directory (`.../idlelib`) is placed on `sys.path[0]`.  `ModifiedInterpreter.transfer_path()` then sends the whole GUI `sys.path` to the user subprocess (replacing its `sys.path`), so user code could import idlelib submodules as top-level modules, e.g. `import help` silently imports `idlelib.help`.  A subissue of #69674.

`transfer_path()` now removes the idlelib directory from the transferred path.  Only that entry is removed, so `import idlelib.run` and the other idlelib modules the subprocess needs still resolve via the `Lib` parent directory; as Terry noted in the issue, `idlelib.run` runs fine without idlelib on the path.

The removal is factored into a module-level `fix_user_path()` with a non-GUI unit test.

body:
## What

Surfaces the manual post-install steps an add-on needs — CLI commands bougie can't run for the user (`module:enable`, config generation, asset rebuilds) — both in the bougie **starter manifest** and as an **on-screen setup panel**. Built out for Loki Checkout (Hyvä).

## Changes

**Add-on `notes` mechanism**
- Add-ons gain an optional `notes:` list (`definitions/addons/loki-checkout-hyva.yaml` documents its 5 steps: `module:enable`, `hyva:config:generate`, Tailwind rebuild, Alpine.js 3 / Hyvä 1.4+ requirement, don't-run-both-checkouts).
- `Definitions::addonNotes()` accessor; `StarterController::manifest()` emits them into the manifest's `notes` **only when the add-on's package actually lands in `require`** — so users never see steps for something they didn't install.

**Loki Checkout detection**
- `Configurator::requiresLokiCheckoutHyva()` matches `loki-checkout/magento2-hyva` (deliberately **not** the Luma build — different steps).
- `DefinitionsSerializer` flags add-ons with `lokiHyva` so the client reveals the panel optimistically; `ConfiguratorController` passes `usesLokiCheckout` through.

**Dock UI refactor**
- Hyvä setup moves from a dock *tab* → an inline card stacked above the `composer.json` output; a matching **Loki Checkout** card sits beside it. Both toggle via the `hidden` attribute from `usesHyva` / `usesLokiCheckout` (client-optimistic, confirmed by `/api/build`).
- require/replace chips + Save/Copy footer pinned to the top; dock scrolls. Drops the stale `· build canvas` appbar tagline + Docs link.

## Tests
- `HyvaRequirementTest`: `requiresLokiCheckoutHyva` (Hyvä true / Luma false / empty false).
- `StarterTest`: notes appear in the manifest only when Loki's package is selected.
- `BuildEndpointTest`: render assertions updated `build canvas` → `window.MAKER` / `mageos-maker`.

## Note

author: shenshan123
body:
## Summary

Closes an honesty regression in ASAP7 signoff and scaffolds the authoritative Calibre path.

The trigger was a request to reach a *clean* ASAP7 DRC/LVS. Investigation showed there is **no clean open-source ASAP7 deck** (the community KLayout `asap7.lydrc` carries an irreducible false-violation floor; the authoritative decks are Calibre-only). But checking *how the store recorded that truth* surfaced a live **fabricated-clean** bug: six asap7 A/B arms recorded `drc=clean, violations=0` (and `lvs=clean` on a deckless platform) while the real `asap7.lydrc` run found **25 violations**.

## What's in this PR

### 1. `fix(skill)` — DRC extractor freshness guard (the fabricated-clean bug) — `d417f69`
`extract_drc.py` lacked the mtime freshness guard its LVS sibling already had (`b710905`), so a fresh `drc_run.log` over a **stale** local `6_drc_count.rpt=0` / `6_drc.lyrdb` was read as a clean.
- `extract_drc.py`: `artifacts_stale()` → status `stale` (never a fabricated clean) when artifacts predate the run.
- `run_drc.sh`: purge stale `6_drc.{lyrdb,log}` / count **before** `make drc` → honest `no_count`→`stuck` if the fresh copy is skipped.
- `extract_lvs.py`: symmetric guard (stale KLayout lvsdb vs fresh `lvs_run.log` → `stale`, downgrades clean only).
- Both new statuses are outside the `{clean,clean_beol,skipped}` whitelist that `fix_signoff` and `ingest_run.is_clean` enforce — fail-closed everywhere.
- **Verified end-to-end:** injected a stale seed → purged → honest `fail(119)` on master_dma; store reconciled (asap7 `drc_clean=0`, honesty gates 5/5, `foreign_key_check=0` after cleaning 15 orphaned `config_lineage` rows).

### 2. `feat(skill)` — Calibre DRC signoff scaffold (deck-ready, guarded) — `3e82361`
The authoritative asap7 signoff is the official (encrypted) Calibre deck. This machine has Calibre 2025.1 + a license but **not** the deck (gated ASU download).
- `run_calibre_drc.sh` (restage GDS → standard SVRF runset → `calibre -drc -hier -turbo`; **guarded** → `skipped` when deck/tool absent; detects version/license load-fail → `incompatible`).
- `extract_calibre_drc.py` (parses the Calibre results DB into the `extract_drc` schema, `engine:calibre`; ships the freshness guard **from day one** — the lesson applied preemptively).
- `references/calibre-signoff.md` (obtain / **2017.4-vs-2025.1 version risk** / runbook / loop-integration). LVS/RCX scaffolds are follow-ups (LVS needs the asap7 `make cdl` fix first).

### 3. `docs` — failure-patterns + `/r2g-debug` command — `9f5e687`, `f29780e`
- `failure-patterns.md`: the DRC-leg recurrence + Calibre resolution pointer.
- `/r2g-debug` command corrected: asap7 KLayout DRC is **not clean-able** (so "DRC clean" was the wrong goal that spawned the bug); new bug-hunt lead for the fabricated-clean alarm with a direct invariant query; Calibre as the authoritative path.

## Tests
`866 → 875` green (+9: DRC guard, LVS guard, Calibre extractor). No regressions.

## Notes
- `knowledge.sqlite` is intentionally **not** in this PR (it holds the whole campaign's session data + the 15-row `config_lineage` cleanup — to be committed deliberately).
- Open follow-ups: a 6th honesty gate (no-LVS-deck ⇒ `lvs∈{skipped,NULL}`); Calibre LVS/RCX once the deck is installed and smoke-passes.

# Полное обнуление detekt-baseline (757 → 0)

Сводит серию правок, доводящих `detekt-baseline.xml` всех модулей до **0 записей** — весь код проходит detekt без исключений в baseline.

## Как достигнут ноль (без изменения вида/поведения)
- **Волна 1 — калибровка + механика:** `MatchingDeclarationName` отключён (осознанная компоновка `*Navigation.kt`=Route+extensions и компонент+enum); `NestedIf` выпрямлен; `TooGenericExceptionCaught` (safeRequest — граница ошибок) и `TooManyFunctions` (BaseScreenModel — MVI-контракт) под `@Suppress` с обоснованием; `TopLevelPropertyNaming`/`ForbiddenComment` — механика.
- **LongMethod (26)** — **чистое извлечение** под-Composable: связный блок → `private @Composable fun` на том же месте с теми же параметрами. Проверено симметрией всех `dp`/`sp`/`Color`/числовых литералов в диффе (composition tree идентичен).
- **LongParameterList (12)** — data-классы параметров/колбэков (с перегенерацией baseline, чтобы не породить новый LongMethod), либо `@Suppress` для компонентов дизайн-системы (параметры = публичный API, минимальный API-контракт).
- **Длинные строки (14)** — комментарии-разделители укорочены, `desc`-строки перенесены конкатенацией (байт-идентично), код-строки переформатированы.
- **Плеер (#22)** — логика скраббинга/seek/SaveProgress **не тронута**: только группировка параметров + переформат; сложные функции под `@Suppress` с ссылкой на #22.

## Проверка
- `./gradlew detekt` — **зелёный при пустом baseline** (0 находок).
- `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` — собирается.
- **Before/after на `Television_1080p`** для Главной, Деталей, Библиотеки, Профиля — **экраны идентичны** (декомпозиция вид не меняет).
- Симметрия литералов подтверждена по всем затронутым файлам.

Closes #18, #19, #20, #21, #36 (структурный долг доведён до нуля во всех модулях).

author: niagawan-mave
body:
Adds **silent background auto-update on Windows** via `electron-updater`, on top of the v1.16.0 Option-A download prompt.

## How it works
- `src/main/autoUpdate.js` — **Windows packaged builds only** (`app.isPackaged && win32`). `autoDownload` + `autoInstallOnAppQuit`: new versions download in the background and install when the app quits. Re-checks every 6h. Emits `update:ready` when a build is downloaded.
- `main.js` wires it and adds `ipcMain 'update:restart'` → `quitAndInstall`.
- preload/store expose `onUpdateReady` / `restartToUpdate`.
- Renderer shows a **"Restart now"** banner when an update is downloaded (bilingual).
- `package.json` adds the `electron-updater` dependency.

**macOS** intentionally stays on the Option-A "Download" prompt — Squirrel.Mac refuses unsigned updates and the app uses ad-hoc signing. Silent macOS updates need an Apple Developer ID cert (future step).

## Testing
- ✅ `node --check` all main files · `npm run build:renderer` · headless Electron smoke (`renderer loaded OK`) · i18n key coverage
- ⚠️ The live update flow (download → install-on-quit) needs an on-device Windows check with a newer release present — can't be exercised headless.

author: jnowat
body:
## Summary

A self-review of WP-50 through WP-55 surfaced several real issues. This PR fixes them in priority order, adds regression coverage for the highest-severity one, and expands ROADMAP.md's honesty about what remains incomplete or risky.

**Highest severity — WP-55 genomic fingerprint data corruption:**
- `update_strain_status` persisted whatever `genomic_fingerprint` value it was sent unconditionally, and `StrainManager.svelte`'s status form pre-filled itself from the current (possibly `"[RESTRICTED]"`-masked) value. Any status update by a role with this field hidden — not only a genomic-confirmation one — would silently overwrite the real fingerprint with the placeholder string, permanently destroying it short of a backup restore.
- Fixed with a hard backend guard (`db::permissions::reject_if_restricted_marker`), a `COALESCE`-based SQL fix so omitting the field preserves the existing value, and a frontend fix so the form never loads the marker into an editable field. Extracted the logic into a testable `db::queries::apply_strain_status_update` and added regression tests for exactly the reported scenario.

**Structural — N+1 query fix:** new `db::permissions::FieldPermissionSet` loads a role's full permission set once (`HashMap`) instead of once per row; wired into all four masked-field read call sites.

**WP-52 — Scheduler mutex poisoning:** the background scheduler silently died forever on mutex poisoning with no logging. Now logs and recovers via `PoisonError::into_inner`.

**WP-53 — iOS camera permission:** added `Info.ios.plist` with `NSCameraUsageDescription`, wired into `tauri.conf.json`.

**Masking robustness:** new defense-in-depth backstop drops any notification candidate containing the restricted-field marker before it can reach a desktop popup, email, or the audit log.

**SMTP credential security:** `create_backup` now redacts `smtp_config.password` in the backup file it produces (live DB still stores it in plaintext — disclosed limitation).

**WP-54 — Sensor source validation:** added `validate_source`, plus documentation of the trust gap (`source` is a caller-supplied label, not a verified fact, since no hardware transport exists).

**Documentation:** ROADMAP.md's WP-50/WP-51 sections now disclose concretely that the PostgreSQL connector has never been executed against a live server, and LAN sync conflict resolution has no frontend UI at all.

Full detail in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --lib --no-default-features` — 387/387 passing
- [x] `cargo test --lib` (default `tauri-commands` feature) — 419/419 passing
- [x] `cargo clippy --no-default-features --lib -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `npm run check` — 0 errors, 85 pre-existing a11y warnings (unchanged)
- [x] `cargo check`/`cargo clippy --features postgres` — clean
- [x] 26 new regression tests, including the exact reported scenario: read a masked field → perform a status update → verify the real value is preserved

## Known limitations after this pass
- SMTP password is still stored in plaintext in the live database (only backups are now protected) — full OS-keychain integration was assessed and deliberately deferred rather than shipped unverified in this sandboxed environment.
- PostgreSQL backend and LAN sync remain foundational/unverified — neither is usable by a real lab today.
- iOS remains unverified end-to-end; the Info.plist fix is believed correct per Tauri's config schema but unexercised against a real Xcode build.
- Sensor `source` validation rejects nonsense values but cannot verify a claimed source is true.

author: vbonnet
body:
Completes the ADR-002 mutual-unblock audit (ce-20p9). Fixes 1 & 2 landed in #779; this PR is fixes 3–6.

## What & why
The supervisor skills never invoked the mutual-unblock path ADR-002 requires. A supervisor or worker frozen on a permission prompt still lists as `active` (and its heartbeat can look fresh), and it **cannot receive `agm send msg`** — so the mesh had no working way to clear a blocked peer.

**Fix 3 (Important)** — `orchestrator.md` Step 5b: run `agm scan --cross-check` each tick. It reads tmux ground truth for peer supervisors, auto-approves RBAC-safe prompts, and reports the rest for `agm send approve`.

**Fix 4 (Important)** — `orchestrator.md` Level 2: a `PERMISSION_PROMPT` worker was sent a defer *message* that can never arrive. Replaced with `agm send approve worker-<id> --reason "<defer guidance>"`, which clears the prompt and delivers the guidance in one shot.

**Fix 5 (Recommended)** — `protocol.md` new "Permission Model & Mutual Unblock" section: supervisors spawn with an `--role` RBAC profile (pre-approving `agm send *`, `agm scan *`, `tmux send-keys *`, …) in `--mode=auto`, so a supervisor on a prompt is a mesh incident; peers clear it with `agm send approve`.

**Fix 6 (Optional)** — new `agm admin install-supervisor-unblock-schedule`: a LaunchAgent running `agm scan --loop --cross-check` that auto-approves stuck supervisors **independent of any supervisor being alive**. This closes the residual deadlock (the SRE scenario that filed the bead: whole trio stuck at once). `agm watch-stalled` does not cover it — its permission recovery only *alerts* the orchestrator, landing on a dead session.

## Verification
- `go test ./cmd/vroom-dispatch/...` — pass (3 new guard tests: cross-check, blocked-worker approve, permission-model doc).
- `go test ./cmd/agm/` (agm module) — pass, incl. 2 new render tests for the watchdog plist.
- `go vet` + `gofmt` clean on changed packages.

Note: `agm send approve` **errors** ("could not find Yes option") when no prompt is visible — it is not a clean no-op. The skills now tell callers to ignore its exit when approving speculatively.

body:
## Cycle-3 integration (Agent D coordinator) — rendering (G) + texturing (H)

Integrates two new feature islands onto main from `feature/g-rendering` (a single linear branch carrying both).

### Included
- **Agent G — Realistic Rendering** (`/rendering`, `shared/render_schema.json` v1.0): PBR + procedural HDR-IBL + ACESFilmic tone mapping + N8AO + emissive bulbs/bloom + area lights, layered on E's lighting; quality toggle; optional path-traced hero still. Mounted into the app (`<RealismLayer/>` + `<RenderControls/>` in RoomView; root `vite.config` R3F dedupe; 3 exact dep pins). Lights on/off toggle drives E's store.
- **Agent H — Photo Texture Mapping** (`/texturing`, `shared/texture_schema.json` + `shared/pbr_conventions.json` v1.0): photo → de-lit tiling PBR material → applied to archetype material slots; world-space tiling + triplanar fallback; textures stored as content-hash **references** (not bytes). Fully isolated (no source edits). App wiring deferred (needs A's additive `FurnitureItem.texture`).

### 🔧 Seam build-break found & fixed
G's mount commit `1ca1ec9` committed `src/three/RoomView.tsx` **entangled with Agent C's uncommitted in-flight multi-room plan-view code** (C had explicitly warned not to commit it solo). That version calls the old `layoutHouse({design,pos,type}[])` API, incompatible with main's committed `layoutHouse(RoomDesign[])` → root `tsc`/`vite build` broke (vitest masked it — esbuild skips types). **Fix:** reconstruct RoomView = main's working version + only G's rendering mount (2 imports + `<RealismLayer/>` + `<RenderControls/>`), dropping C's smuggled code (C lands it later). Diff vs main = 8 lines.

### Verification (authoritative — isolated worktree, every island)
- root (A + G mount): tsc ✓ · **201 tests** · `vite build` ✓
- camera-flythrough 28 ✓ · lighting 30 ✓ · persistence 50 ✓ · rendering 13 ✓ · texturing 65 ✓ — all tsc-clean
- Adversarial review: G's root config edits = PASS; H isolation + contracts = PASS
- ⚠️ **multi-room 48/49** — 1 failure that is **pre-existing on `origin/main`** (not caused by this PR): `roomTypes.test.ts` hard-codes `.toBe(91)` but the catalog is now 103 ids. Filed `ISSUE → AGENT-C`. Root CI doesn't run island tests, so it merged silently earlier.

### Decisions ratified (details in roomio.txt)
PBR conventions (albedo sRGB / data-maps linear / +Y normals / H owns maps, G owns renderer) · render↔light seam (`flat` kept, no double-ACES) · required cross-island R3F dedupe + exact dep pins.

### Open (none block the app)
`ISSUE → C` brittle catalog-count test · `REVIEW → A` own G's RoomView/root edits · recommend adding island tests to CI (after the red test is fixed) · deferred: H's app texture wiring + C's multi-room cluster (both uncommitted).

author: teknium1
body:
## Summary
Slack App-Level (Socket Mode) tokens — the `xapp-<num>-<hash>` format — are now redacted on both the agent and gateway secret paths, so `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` values no longer leak through to chat users with `security.redact_secrets` enabled.

Root cause: only `xox[baprs]-` was matched. The `xapp-` prefix was absent from `agent/redact.py` (`_PREFIX_PATTERNS`) and from `gateway/run.py` (`_GATEWAY_SECRET_PATTERNS`).

## Changes
- `agent/redact.py`: add `xapp-\d+-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}` to the prefix patterns.
- `gateway/run.py`: add `\bxapp-\d+-[A-Za-z0-9\-]{20,}\b` to the gateway secret patterns.
- `tests/agent/test_redact.py`: cover xapp- token redaction.
- `scripts/release.py`: AUTHOR_MAP entry for arthurzhang.

The `\d+-` anchor on the version segment keeps benign text like `xapp-store` from being over-matched.

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/agent/test_redact.py` | 133 passed |
| E2E — agent/redact path | `xapp-` token redacted |
| E2E — gateway secret path | `xapp-` token matched |
| E2E — benign `xapp-store` | not over-matched |
| E2E — `xoxb-` regression | still redacted |

## Credits
Salvage of #34718 (@arthurzhang, both-file fix + anchored regex). Test cherry-picked from #5282 (@Ruzzgar). Also fixes the gap identified in #4541 (@maymuneth). All three PRs targeted this same `xapp-` gap; closing #4541 and #5282 as duplicates with credit.

## Infographic
![Redact Slack App-Level Tokens](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa07c61/NKw1zlR-XULhbiNQgyS1n_aQEQqyzR.png)

dnf remove (microdnf) implicitly autoremoves packages that were pulled in as auto-dependencies during dnf upgrade, even if they are explicitly listed in packages-list.ocp. This caused iproute and psmisc to be silently removed from the ironic-agent container, leaving IPA without the ip command and preventing it from heartbeating to Ironic (resulting in cleaning timeouts).

rpm -e only removes the named packages with no autoremove behavior, matching the existing pattern used for git-core.

author: devopam
body:
## Summary

Implements the three WarehousePG/Greenplum MPP-dialect findings surfaced
once the `warehousepg-latest` CI lane was fixed (#210) to actually reach a
real server. Each was root-caused by reading the actual failing test DDL.

**15.9 — distribution-key-aware `UNIQUE`/`PRIMARY KEY` handling.**
WarehousePG requires every `UNIQUE`/`PRIMARY KEY` constraint on a table to
be a superset of its distribution key — impossible for two disjoint
single-column keys (e.g. `PRIMARY KEY(id)` + separate `UNIQUE(name)`) under
ordinary sharding. Fixed with a conditional `DISTRIBUTED REPLICATED` clause
(Greenplum-only syntax; a no-op on vanilla PG) via two new shared fixtures
in `tests/integration/conftest.py` (`is_warehousepg`,
`distributed_replicated_clause`), applied to **exactly** the 6 tables that
need it (`advisors`' `with_unique`, `composite`/`drizzle`/`sqlalchemy`/
`sqlc`'s `widget`, `ecto`'s `users`) — sibling tables with only a single PK
or only plain/partial indexes are untouched, since the MPP rule only
applies to `UNIQUE`/`PRIMARY KEY` constraints.

**15.10 — `DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE)` dialect fallback.**
That syntax is PG 13+; WarehousePG's older merge-base doesn't parse it.
The test's cleanup now tries `WITH (FORCE)` first and falls back to
explicitly terminating other backends on that database (via
`pg_terminate_backend`) + a plain drop — backend-agnostic, since it reacts
to the actual syntax error rather than guessing from server identity.

**15.11 — schema-scoped `dump_database` (+ fixes the `gp_toolkit` collision).**
Added a genuinely useful `schemas: list[str] | None = None` parameter to
`dump_database` (validated via the existing `_IDENTIFIER` regex, mapped to
repeatable `--schema=NAME` pg_dump flags; default behavior byte-for-byte
unchanged) and threaded it through the `dump_database` tool. The
dump/restore round-trip test now scopes to `schemas=[export_schema]`,
sidestepping WarehousePG's built-in `gp_toolkit` schema colliding on
restore — a fix that helps on any backend with extra default schemas, not
just WarehousePG.

## Verification honesty note

**This sandbox has no WarehousePG database.** Every local test run
(`is_warehousepg` always resolves `False`) only proves the
**vanilla-PG / unchanged-behavior path**. The `DISTRIBUTED REPLICATED`
branch, the DROP-DATABASE fallback's except-path, and the `gp_toolkit`
fix are **not verified locally** — only the real `Tests (PG
warehousepg-latest)` CI run on this PR can confirm them, and I'll watch
that run (pulling actual job logs, not just pass/fail) before merging.

## Tests
- 3 new unit tests for `dump_database`'s `schemas` param (argv
  construction, default-unchanged, invalid-identifier rejection).
- Full suite: **2731 collected, 0 failed** (2718 passed + 13 skipped with
  a live test DB; 2621 passed + 110 skipped without one — same collection,
  zero failures either way).
- Surface snapshot regenerated — diff is **only** `dump_database`'s
  description + new `schemas` property (confirmed via manual diff). No
  return-shape/output-schema changes (return type unchanged).

## Roadmap linkage

Advances roadmap row: 15.9, 15.10, 15.11 (all flipped to ✅ in this PR)

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated first (TDD); suite passes locally (0 failures)
- [x] `ruff`, `ruff format`, and `mypy src/mcpg` pass
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated under `[Unreleased]`
- [x] Roadmap rows cited above; 15.9/15.10/15.11 marked ✅
- [x] No hand-edits to `src/mcpg/_vendor/`

author: pragnyakhandelwal
body:
#### Reference issue (if any)

Part of #13926 (Phase 1 — legacy helper cleanup).
Follows #14007.

#### What does this implement/fix?

Removes `_get_eeg_calibration_info` from `egimff.py` and lets `mffpy` apply per-channel GCAL scaling natively instead.
Previously, `_get_mff_reader` disabled `mffpy'`s built-in GCAL calibration (`set_calibration("EEG", None)`) because `_get_eeg_calibration_info` was already baking GCAL into MNE's `cals` array. This split the calibration responsibility across two places. Now `mffpy` handles GCAL directly (as it does by default), and MNE's cals for EEG channels are simplified to a flat unit conversion (1e-6 for µV channels, 1 for V channels).
As a result, `_get_gains` in `general.py` loses its only caller and is removed entirely.

#### Additional information

The `value_range/bits` branch inside `_get_eeg_calibration_info` was dead code — both fields are hardcoded to 0 in `_read_header` and never updated.

## Description

This PR adds the Kubernetes CRUD API layer and React data-fetching hooks for the FeatureStore CRD to the `@odh-dashboard/feature-store` package. These are the foundational building blocks consumed by the creation wizard, management page, and deployment tracking UI in subsequent PRs.

These API helpers and hooks encapsulate all Kubernetes interactions for the Feature Store feature, providing a clean abstraction layer between the CRD and the UI components. The creation wizard ([RHOAIENG-61260](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-61260)), management page ([RHOAIENG-61262](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-61262)), and deployment tracking ([RHOAIENG-61261](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-61261)) all consume these modules. Shipping them as a standalone PR keeps the diff focused and reviewable.

No UI-visible changes. No new package exports needed — all modules are consumed internally within the `feature-store` package.

## How Has This Been Tested?

## Summary
This PR adds a new standalone Google Apps Script file (`CalendarToSheet.gs`) that extracts events from Google Calendar and writes them to a Google Sheet. This script was extracted from a larger `Shift.gs` file to provide focused calendar-to-sheet functionality.

## Key Changes
- **New file: CalendarToSheet.gs** - A complete, self-contained script for calendar event extraction with the following features:
  - Configurable output destination (sheet name and starting cell)
  - Flexible output orientation (vertical or horizontal layout)
  - Customizable date range and time window for event retrieval
  - Support for multiple calendars with per-user color coding

  - "① 設定シートを作成" - Creates a configuration sheet with sensible defaults
  - "② 予定を取得して反映" - Fetches calendar events and writes them to the specified sheet
