body:
## What

Every generated app now starts from ONE standard foundation with the full standard module set **present and active by default**, each **switch-off-able** per app. This closes a real gap: the packet docs (`template-credential-contract.md`) already named Email + Payments as standard, but the generator did not emit them.

## Standard modules now shipped (real, working code — not placeholders)

Emitted from a new `src/lib/engine/foundation-modules.ts`, spread into the generated bundle:

| Module | What ships |
|---|---|
| **Product catalog** | storefront `/products` + `/admin/products` + `/api/products` + `products` table/seed |
| **Support ticketing** | `/support` (submit + list own) + `/admin/support` queue + `/api/support` + `support_tickets` table; emails the owner on new tickets |
| **Email (Resend)** | `src/lib/email.ts` transactional send + `/admin/email` console + `/api/email/send` + `email_log` table |
| **Payments (Stripe)** | `src/lib/payments.ts` real Checkout + `/api/billing/checkout` + `/api/billing/webhook` + `payments` table; Buy button on products |
| **Feature flags** | `src/lib/app-config.ts` — `FEATURE_*` default ON; set `false` to switch a module off |

Plus generator wiring (schema/seed/`.env.example`/home-nav) and `templates.ts` flips (billing/notifications/marketplace → always-on) so the descriptive catalog matches.

## Cost/credential fence (important)

Modules are **fully wired and active**, but the ones that move money or send mail run on the **app owner's own credentials** (`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `RESEND_API_KEY` + `SENDER_EMAIL`). No key → the UI is live but real transactions/sends wait until the owner connects their keys. **No generated app can surprise-charge the ecosystem.**

## Verification

- ✅ Main app: `typecheck`, `build`, `source:check`, `generated-apps:guard` all pass
- ✅ **Generated a sample app through the real runtime (62 files, was 42) and BUILT it standalone** — every foundation route compiles (`✓ Compiled successfully`; `/products`, `/support`, `/admin/email`, `/api/billing/checkout`, `/api/billing/webhook`, `/api/email/send`, `/api/products`, `/api/support` all present). The temporary generation harness was removed before commit.

## Scope

Free-tier, default-on-but-off-able, owner-credential-gated for the paid surfaces. This is the core-product change that makes the packet a ready-to-go template.

## Problema

O gate advisory **Jana recall-eval (mock)** (`.github/workflows/jana-recall-eval.yml` → `php artisan jana:recall-eval --mode=mock`) estava **vermelho no main**. body:
> 🤖 **AI-generated PR** — written by Claude Code, posted by @yjkao.

Fixes #670. Unblocks #667.

## What

The block-sparse U(1)-Sz `ctm_tensor_2site(..., recipe="2x2")` sweep crashed with per-sector block mismatches on genuine **direction-dependent** (`A.l != A.r`, cell-consistent) states. Three localized bond-bookkeeping fixes, each anchored on the production energy/RDM convention in `_ctm_tensor_energy.py` and cross-checked against a variPEPS numerical oracle:

1. **`_build_enlarged_corner` (`bottom_left`)** — C4's two legs were glued to the wrong edges; now `c4_u↔t3_r`, `c4_r↔t4_u`.
2. **`_ctm_tensor_absorb_bottom_2plaq`** — C3·T2 paired `c3_l↔t2_d`; corrected to `c3_u↔t2_d`.
3. **`_ctm_sv_diff`** — asymmetric-bond states grow charge sectors during CTM warmup, so the concatenated per-sector SV vector changes length between iterations and crashed the convergence check; now zero-pads the shorter vector (eager, non-AD call sites → gradient-safe).

## Why it hid until now

All three are **no-ops on uniform/dense** states: for a leg-symmetric corner the swap is a benign gauge choice (single block, same energy), and the SV vector length is stable. The bug only bites block-sparse envs with `A.l != A.r`. Existing 2x2 tests only covered symmetric-corner states, so it was never exercised.

## Validation

- Direction-dependent symmetric 2x2 now matches dense to **4e-14** (E = −0.5421160718).
- Dense 2x2 energy **unchanged** (guard test locks it).
- #667 acceptance test un-xfailed and retargeted to `recipe="2x2"` — passes.
- Stale unit test `test_build_enlarged_corner_bottom_left_numerical` (its einsum reference encoded the old swapped C4 pairing) updated to the correct convention.
- Targeted CTM/iPEPS + u1sz suites green; full core suite gates via CI.

## Out of scope (follow-ups filed)

Same latent `c3_l↔t2_d` bug exists in two other code paths that are no-ops on the production (uniform) path:
- #674 — fermionic/fused twin `_ctm_tensor_absorb_bottom_2plaq_fused`.
- #675 — compiled path `_ctm_compiled_moves.py`.

author: den-run-ai
body:
Follow-up to the analytics reporter (#269). Its anomaly detector traced a **June-2026 GA4 event spike** to automated/bot traffic — bursts of `game_reset` / `game_over` / `session_health` with **no matching rise in `game_start`** (76 resets & 53 game-overs in a day vs. ~34 starts across the whole month) — not real players. It also found every finish was **double-counted** (both `complete_run` and `complete_game` fire).

This PR fixes both root causes.

## 1. Tag bot/automation traffic (`is_bot`)

`src/analytics-env.ts` (new):
- `isAutomatedClient()` — reads `navigator.webdriver` (set by Playwright/Puppeteer/Selenium and most headless bots).
- `withTrafficTag(params)` — returns a copy of the event params with a stable `is_bot` boolean added (never mutates).

Wired in centrally so **every** event is tagged:
- the `window.firebaseModules.logEvent` wrapper in `auth.ts` (covers `game_start`, `game_over`, `game_reset`, `share_result`, `feedback_submitted`, and the diagnostics seam), and
- the direct `logEvent` calls: `complete_run`, `new_high_score`, `login`.

**Tagging, not suppressing** — the data stays, and you exclude it in GA4 by registering `is_bot` as a custom dimension and filtering `is_bot = true`. This both cleans the anomaly class and makes the "42 active users" figure trustworthy.

## 2. De-duplicate the finish event

Removed the redundant `complete_game` emit from `result-overlay.ts`. `complete_run` — fired by `AuthModule.recordScore` (the scoring source of truth, carries `time`) — is now the single canonical finish event. (GA4 showed 47 `complete_run` vs 34 `complete_game`, i.e. genuinely redundant double-counting.)

## Tests

- New `tests/analytics-env-tests.js` (10 assertions) for the tag helper — webdriver detection, tag values, non-mutation, undefined params.
- `result-overlay-tests.js` updated to assert the overlay no longer double-logs a finish.
- Green locally: `typecheck`, `analytics-env` (10/10), `result-overlay` (31), `scores` (41), `auth`/bootstrap (24), `diagnostics` (23), `share` (54), `feedback` (61), `lifecycle` (9); 0 ESLint errors.

No physics/terrain/gameplay logic touched — analytics wiring only.

## Summary

Starts OOE 0.3 with a focused draft of Engineering State:

- Adds OOEP-0004 for the Engineering State proposal
- Adds `spec/04-engineering-state.md`
- Adds `examples/02-engineering-state-snapshot.md`
- Updates README navigation for the 0.3 draft
- Updates ROADMAP to reflect the 0.3 scope

## 0.3 goal

Define how OOE represents the current known state of engineering reality.

Engineering State is the durable, evidence-backed understanding that emerges from outcomes, constraints, observations, claims, evidence, decisions, assumptions, risks, and unknowns.

## Editorial intent

This PR intentionally stays narrow.

It does not introduce:

- Formal machine-readable schemas
- Graph model
- Database model
- Synchronization protocol
- Worker protocol
- Runtime engine
- UI representation
- Relationship model
- Belief model
- Derived state semantics
- Durablis or any internal product concepts

Those ideas remain deferred until the Engineering State foundation is stable.

## Review focus

Please review for:

- Whether Engineering State is clearly distinguished from code, tickets, deployment state, and worker memory
- Whether State Claims are the right bridge between evidence and current understanding
- Whether Unknowns, Decisions, Assumptions, and Risks belong in the 0.3 foundation
- Whether the example makes the concept practical without implying a formal schema too early
- Whether anything in this PR belongs in 0.4 or later instead of 0.3

## Suggested read order

1. `ooep/OOEP-0004-engineering-state.md`
2. `spec/04-engineering-state.md`
3. `examples/02-engineering-state-snapshot.md`
4. README and ROADMAP updates

## Key sentence

> Engineering State is the current known, evidence-backed representation of engineering reality relevant to one or more outcomes.

author: benemanu
body:
Follow-up to #21

Efficiency changes to how CI triggers, plus a dedicated always-on hygiene job.

## 1. Pull requests only
Drops the `push: branches: [main]` trigger from `ci-test` and `ci-checks`. We land PRs with **rebase-merge**, so the exact commits are already validated on the PR; re-running everything on the push to `main` just duplicated work. They now run on `pull_request` + manual `workflow_dispatch`. Concurrency guard simplified to `cancel-in-progress: true`.

## 2. Path-based filtering
Each workflow gains a lightweight `detect changes` job (`dorny/paths-filter`) and gates its expensive jobs on the result:

- **ci-test** — the macOS + Linux pytest matrix runs only when `src/**`, `tests/**`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.python-version`, or the workflow file change.
- **ci-checks / lint** (ruff + ty) — runs on `src`/`tests`/`pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`/`.pre-commit-config.yaml`/`justfile` changes.
- **ci-checks / web** — runs only when `apps/web/**`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` change.

## 3. File hygiene always runs
File-hygiene hooks (`check-toml`, `check-yaml`, `end-of-file-fixer`, `trailing-whitespace`) apply to every file, so they are split into a dedicated **`file hygiene`** job that is **not** path-gated — it runs on every PR, including docs-only ones. It stays cheap by running pre-commit through `uvx` (no project sync). Hooks are partitioned between the hygiene and lint jobs with pre-commit's `SKIP` env var (since `pre-commit run` takes at most one hook id).

Net effect: a README-only PR runs the `file hygiene` check and the near-instant `detect changes` jobs, but skips the pytest matrix, ruff/ty, and the web tests.

### Notes
- Manual `workflow_dispatch` still runs everything (no diff to inspect).
- Skipped jobs stay visible as their own check runs rather than the workflow silently not triggering — friendlier if these ever become required checks. If you make them required in branch protection, a docs-only PR would skip the gated jobs, so ping me for a small always-green gate job to avoid blocking.

## Verification
- Both workflow files parse as valid YAML.
- On this PR (which touches the workflow files) all jobs trigger; the `file hygiene` job runs and passes.

body:
## Summary

I7 of the configurability refactor (ADR 0017). `build_rootfs_plan` now takes a
`&NormalizationPolicy`, making the ADR 0013 D7 runtime-closure fallbacks
operator-toggleable:

- `ldd_closure` — the per-program static `ldd` `.so` closure.
- `nss_closure_fallback` — the glibc `libnss_*.so` widening.
- `python_closure_fallback` — the Python stdlib widening.

**Safety-monotone by construction:** every toggle, when disabled, only *removes*
library/data paths from the plan (a strictly more minimal rootfs). It is a
capability/degradation knob — it can make a granted dynamic program fail to
load, but can never widen the executable set or relax confinement (the D1
identity invariant holds regardless). Defaults are all-on == today's behavior.

Callers pass `NormalizationPolicy::default()`; the jaild daemon keeps today's
behavior until config is plumbed through the jail protocol (I8, #147).

## Test plan

- `just check` green: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` on both feature sets, full
  workspace tests (both feature sets).
- New regression test `rootfs_ldd_closure_is_toggleable` (fails on the old
  always-on path): with `ldd_closure = false`, cat's libc closure is dropped
  from the plan.

## Summary

Adds `apps/cli/src/contracts/` — the canonical, reconciled TypeScript contract surface every CLI coding-agent pipeline group builds against (per the Group 7 spec at `/Users/macanderson/Desktop/outputs/oxagen-cli-pipeline/group-7-typed-contracts/`).

The original `contracts/*.ts` stubs in that spec predate three groups that have since shipped on `main` (Group 1 runtime, Group 2 orchestrator/router, Group 4 assist tools) and disagree with them in several places. Per the Group 7 brief — *"If the JSON and the type disagree, fix the type to match the JSON, then flag it"* — this surface:

- **Re-exports the real shipped types verbatim** for already-built groups (zero drift by construction, since these ARE the shipped types, not a second copy):
  - `contracts/model-provider.ts` ← `../runtime/index.js` (Group 1): `ModelProvider`, `ModelKind`, `CompletionRequest`, `CompletionResult`, `CompletionUsage`, `CompletionMessage`, `ModelCapabilities`, `Quantization`, `ReasoningEffort`, `CapabilityRow`, `DeviceProfile`.
  - `contracts/router.ts` + `contracts/orchestrator.ts` ← `../orchestrator/index.js` (Group 2): `Router`, `RoutingTask`, `RoutingDecision`, `Coordinator`, `WorkerRequest`, `WorkerResult`, `Complexity`.
  - `contracts/tools.ts` ← `../pipeline/index.js` (Group 4): `PromptEnhancerInput/Output`, `JudgeInput/Output`, `Survey*`, `AssistTools`, `ToolName`, `ToolStatus`, `ToolEvent`, `LogField`.
- **Defines fresh, standalone interface stubs** (pure `interface`/`type`, no implementation) for the groups that haven't landed yet, kept independent of any not-yet-existing `src/context` / `src/monitors` / pipeline-state-machine modules:
  - `contracts/context.ts` (Group 3): `GraphQueryInput`, `ImpactedFile`, `GraphSymbol`, `GraphEdge`, `GraphResult`, `ContextResolver`.
  - `contracts/monitors.ts` (Group 5): `MonitorTargetType`, `MonitorDispatchInput`, `MonitorDispatchResult`, `MonitorReport`, `MonitorService`.
  - `contracts/pipeline.ts` (Group 6): `PipelineStep`, `StepResult`, `PipelineRunInput`, `PipelineRunResult`, `Pipeline` — importing its tool/router/orchestrator dependencies from the re-exports above.
  - `contracts/tools.ts`'s `plan` slice (Group 6): `PlanTask`, `PlanInput`, `PlanOutput` (referenced by `Pipeline.doWork`, not folded into the shipped `AssistTools`).
  - `contracts/timeouts.ts` (Group 8): `TimeoutConfig`, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS` (real `const`), `ModelCall`, `ProgressEvent`, `TurnRunner`.
  - `contracts/metrics.ts` (Group 8): `MetricsEvent`, `ModelUsage`, `SessionMetrics`, `PriceRow`, `MetricsBus`.
- **`contracts/config.ts`** — the unified `AppConfig` shape, reconciled to compose the re-exported `Complexity`/`Quantization` rather than redeclaring them.
- **`contracts/index.ts`** re-exports the whole surface; no naming collisions (verified — each contract file re-exports/declares a disjoint name set from every other).

## Reconciliation notes

Everywhere the original stub disagreed with shipped code, the canonical surface here follows the **shipped code**, per the Group 7 brief:

1. **`CompletionRequest`** — stub: `{ system?, prompt, maxTokens?, timeoutMs }`. Shipped (`runtime/types.ts`): `{ messages: CompletionMessage[], maxOutputTokens?, temperature?, effort?, signal? }` — a chat-message array instead of `system`/`prompt` strings, no required `timeoutMs` on the request itself (Group 8's `ModelCall.timeoutMs` carries the per-call deadline instead — matches the Group 7 hard requirement that "the turn does not [impose a timeout]").
2. **`CompletionResult`** — stub: `{ text, tokensIn, tokensOut, model, ms }`. Shipped: `{ text, usage: { inputTokens, outputTokens }, model, kind, costUsd }` — token counts nested under `usage`, no `ms` field, but adds `kind` (on-device vs cloud) and `costUsd`.
3. **`ModelCapabilities`** — stub: `{ codeScore, contextWindow, params?, minRamGB? }`. Shipped adds `id`, `kind`, `vendor`, `offline`, `tools`; `codeScore` is optional (`?`) instead of required.
4. **`ModelRegistry`** — the stub's single interface (`resolveBestOnDevice`/`provider`/`coordinatorCandidates`/`defaultCodeWorker`/`defaultJudgeModel`) has no shipped counterpart; Group 1 ships free functions instead (`loadRegistry`, `capabilityTable`, `resolveBestOnDeviceModel`, `roles`, etc., in `runtime/index.ts`). Not redeclared — flagging only.
5. **`AssistTools`** — the stub declares a fourth method, `plan(input): Promise<PlanOutput>`. Shipped Group 4 `AssistTools` ships only `enhancePrompt`/`judge`/`survey`; `plan` is pipeline step 3 ("do the work"), Group 6's territory, not yet built. `PlanTask`/`PlanInput`/`PlanOutput` are kept as fresh, standalone Group 6 stubs referenced by `Pipeline.doWork`, deliberately **not** folded into the re-exported `AssistTools`.
6. **`ToolLogMeta`** — stub: `{ tool, status, model?, tokens?, ms?, reason? }`. Shipped `pipeline/logging.ts` ships `ToolEvent` (`{ tool, step, status }`) plus an ordered `LogField` tuple list (`[key, value][]`) for the remaining fields — a materially different logging shape. Re-exported as shipped.
7. **`Complexity`/`RoutingTask`/`RoutingDecision`/`Router`** — shape is unchanged from the stub, but *ownership* moved: the stub had `router.ts` import `Complexity` from `config.ts`; canonically it's now owned by the already-shipped Group 2 (`orchestrator/types.ts`), and `config.ts` imports it from there instead.
8. **`CoordinatorModel`** — stub: closed union `"on-device" | "haiku"`. Shipped (`runtime/types.ts`'s `RuntimeConfigDefaults.coordinator`, `runtime/config.ts`'s `getCoordinator()`) types the coordinator as a plain `string` — any registry id is valid, and candidates are data (`models.json`), not a closed union. `CoordinatorModel` is dropped; `RuntimeConfig.coordinator: string` follows the shipped shape.
9. **`Coordinator`'s embedded collaborator types** — the shipped `Coordinator` (Group 2) is typed against orchestrator's own interim mirrors of `GraphQueryInput`/`GraphResult`/`JudgeInput`/`JudgeOutput`/`MonitorDispatchInput`/`MonitorDispatchResult`, which are narrower than this PR's fresh Group 3/5 stubs (e.g. fresh `GraphSymbol` adds a required `kind` field; fresh `GraphEdge.type` is a literal union vs. shipped's plain `string`). The fresh stubs are structurally assignable *into* the shipped mirrors (one direction only), so nothing breaks today, but this PR deliberately does **not** re-export orchestrator's mirror names under the canonical `GraphResult`/`JudgeInput`/etc. names to keep exactly one canonical definition per name in the barrel — Group 3/5, when built, implement against `contracts/context.ts` / `contracts/monitors.ts`, and Group 2 should adopt the richer shape at that point.

## Test plan

- [x] `apps/cli/src/contracts/` compiles under strict TypeScript with no implementation (pure interfaces / `type` / `const` defaults only).
- [x] `apps/cli/src/contracts/__tests__/contracts.test.ts` — exercises `DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS` directly and type-checks the barrel's full re-export surface.
- [x] `CI=true pnpm typecheck` (apps/cli) — clean, no errors.
- [x] `CI=true pnpm exec eslint src/contracts --max-warnings 0` — clean, exit 0, zero warnings, no `eslint-disable`.
- [x] `CI=true pnpm vitest run src/contracts` — 1 file, 2 tests, all passing.

Evidence saved to `verifications/session_017FQbKXKk5j3wz2dP7NdFEC/group7-contracts-tests.txt` (gitignored, local only).

Per project policy this PR does **not** run the full monorepo `pnpm gate` / whole-repo test suite — only the narrow test/typecheck/lint for the changed package, as instructed. CI will run the full affected gate on this PR.

## Summary The two-column scorecard rendered `[object Object]` in the score column for a turn that aggregates a play, a valid-challenge bonus, and end-of-game rack points -- e.g. the final turn of game `BoSCFpffhv` (#1895), where a player plays out and the word is then challenged (and holds). ## Bug `TwoColTurn` built the score column by appending the challenge bonus as a JSX fragment, then appended the end-of-game rack points with a template literal (`` `${score}+${endRackPoints}` ``). Interpolating the fragment into the template string coerced it to `[object Object]`. author: luannunes
body:
## Bug
Pulling to refresh on Home made the app **refresh eternally** — the spinner never stopped.

## Root cause
The ViewModel logic clears `isRefreshing` correctly, and the 30s network timeout rules out a hung call. The loop is in `PullToRefreshBox` (material3 1.3.1): when the reload resolves **within a frame**, `isRefreshing` flips `true→false` sub-frame, so the box never settles its gesture state and keeps re-firing `onRefresh`. The `onManualRefresh` re-entrancy guard can't catch it because the flag is already `false` by the time it re-fires.

This is most visible when the backend is unreachable — `getMonth` fails instantly with connection-refused, making the reload sub-frame fast.

## Fix
Hold `isRefreshing` for a **minimum 600ms** in `onManualRefresh` (the reload and the floor run concurrently via `coroutineScope { async {} + delay }`), so the indicator's transition is always a clean `true`-then-`false` the gesture can settle on. As a bonus it reads as intentional feedback instead of a flicker. The existing re-entrancy guard still covers the in-flight window.

## Tests
New test: `isRefreshing` stays true past an instant reload and clears after the floor. Existing manual-refresh tests (reload, success/no-toast, fail-soft, concurrency guard, silent ON_RESUME) still pass. Full suite green; `assembleLocalDebug` compiles.

## Note
Diagnosed from strong evidence (timeout rules out a hang; flag-clear logic is correct; symptom is a self-perpetuating loop = `onRefresh` re-firing; known material3 1.3.1 sub-frame-completion behavior), but I couldn't reproduce on a device here. Worth a quick on-device confirm with the backend both up and down.

body:
## Why

When an agent turn ended, everything before the final text block folded into a collapsed **"Worked for X"** section. That hid content the moment a turn finished — often mid-read — which broke reading flow. Hiding it was the wrong default.

## What changed

| Ended turn (`stopReason: end_turn`)     | Before                                                            | After                                       |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| research + trailing answer              | research folded into a collapsed "Worked for X"; answer inline   | whole trail rendered inline, nothing hidden |
| turn duration                           | shown in the collapse header                                     | not shown (unused)                          |
| streaming / cancelled / tool-only turns | already inline                                                   | unchanged                                   |

A finished turn now renders exactly like the live streaming view. The per-thought **"Reasoning / Thought for X"** collapse is a separate surface and is intentionally left untouched.

## Commits

- **`fix(agent-mode): always render the completed trail inline`** — delete the `WorkedForBlock` collapse and the `canCollapse` fork in `AgentTrailView`; `AgentTrail` always renders the linear trail + Copy/Insert actions. Remove the now-unused `splitTrailingText` helper. Adds a regression test asserting an ended turn with a tool call + trailing answer renders the tool card inline and shows no "Worked for" toggle.
- **`refactor(agent-mode): drop dead turnDurationMs plumbing`** — with the collapse gone, the turn's wall-clock duration is never read. Remove `turnDurationMs` end-to-end (session, store, persisted message type) and the `turnStartedAt` bookkeeping that existed only to compute it. `turnStopReason` is fully preserved (it still gates Copy/Insert off on cancelled turns).

## Notes

- `turnStopReason` is unchanged — only the duration is removed.
- Old persisted chats may still carry `turnDurationMs`; the load path is a plain snapshot with no strict schema, so the field is silently ignored. No migration needed.
- Multi-agent (fanout) turns render via a different path and never used this collapse — unaffected.

## Test plan

- `npm run test` — full suite green (301 suites / 4353 tests).
- `npm run build` — tsc typecheck + esbuild clean.
- `npm run format && npm run lint` — clean.
- `grep -rn "turnDurationMs" src` — zero hits.

author: markmc
body:
## Why

The quarterly `rebuild` workflow [run on 2026-07-01](https://github.com/sailscoring/canonical-logos/actions/runs/28502684030) flagged *"upstream logos diverged"* and tried to open a PR — but **nothing actually diverged**. All 52 logos were **pixel-identical** to `main`; the re-fetch/normalise toolchain (Pillow/zlib, SVGO, plus this run being force-migrated to Node 24) just re-encoded unchanged assets to byte-different output.

The old guard compared **raw bytes** and the manifest's byte-derived **sha256**, so it tripped on that encoder noise. The `create-pull-request` step then failed anyway, because the org blocked GitHub Actions from opening PRs — producing a red-X failure notification for a non-problem.

## What changed

- **Guard compares pixels, not bytes.** PNGs are decoded and compared pixel-for-pixel; SVGs are byte-compared; `sha256` is ignored alongside the moving timestamps in the JSON. Structural manifest changes (added/removed entry, new `source`/`quality`) still trip it.
  - Uses `ImageChops.difference(...).getextrema()`, **not** `.getbbox()` — on RGBA the latter defaults to `alpha_only=True` (Pillow ≥ 11), which would silently miss any pure recolour that leaves transparency untouched.
- **Silenced the toolchain warnings** behind the drift: dropped the invalid `python-version` input to `setup-uv`, bumped `setup-node` to Node 24.

## Out-of-band (already done)

- Enabled org setting *"Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"* (was blocking the built-in token org-wide).
- Created the `automated` / `data-refresh` labels the PR step tags (they didn't exist, and `create-pull-request` doesn't auto-create labels).

## Verification

Ran the new guard logic locally against the noise run (`main` → `bot/rebuild`): **`changed = False`** despite git seeing 97 changed files under `logos/`. Unit-tested that it still flags a 1-pixel recolour, an alpha-only change, an added manifest entry, and asset add/remove — while treating re-encodes and timestamp/sha-only churn as no-change.

body:
## Problem

Reported in Slack: on https://debug.octez-connect.tezos.com the watch-only **"add account"** flow is broken — a user could not add an address.

**Root cause:** adding a watch-only account calls `ApiService.getPublicKeyForAddress`, which resolves the public key by querying the *selected* RPC node. The default selected mainnet node was `https://mainnet.api.tez.ie` (dead — tez.ie was deprecated), and `teznode.letzbake.com` in the mainnet list is unreliable. With the selected node down, the lookup threw and the add flow failed.

## Changes

- **Mainnet** node list trimmed to the confirmed-working RPCs:
  - `https://tezos-mainnet.octez.io` (new default selected)
  - `https://mainnet.smartpy.io`
  - `https://rpc.tzbeta.net`
  - `https://rpc.tzkt.io/mainnet`
- **Shadownet** node list expanded to the confirmed-working RPCs:
  - `https://tezos-shadownet.octez.io` (default selected)
  - `https://shadownet.smartpy.io`
  - `https://rpc.shadownet.teztnets.com`
  - `https://rpc.tzkt.io/shadownet`
- **Removed Ghostnet** entirely (network config + node-selector dropdown), keeping only Mainnet and Shadownet.
- **Bumped the localStorage key to `nodes_v2`** so returning users who have stale, broken RPCs cached (e.g. `mainnet.api.tez.ie`) fall back to the fresh defaults instead of staying broken.

- `generate_tile_coords(img_w, img_h, tile_w, tile_h, overlap)` 生成覆盖全图的切片坐标，最后一列/行向前偏移以保证每个切片尺寸一致
- `slice_label(label_data, x0, y0, x1, y1, min_area_ratio)` 对每个 shape 按类型裁剪：
  - **polygon**: Sutherland-Hodgman 算法裁剪到切片矩形，自动丢弃退化多边形（面积 < 1px²）
  - **rectangle** (2-point): 矩形求交
  - **point / circle / line**: 边界检测
  - 坐标平移到切片局部坐标系，更新 `imageWidth`/`imageHeight`
- `--min-area-ratio` 过滤裁剪后面积占比过小的碎片标注
- `--skip-empty` 跳过无标注切片
- `--embed-image-data` 可选内嵌 base64 图片到输出 JSON

```bash
python utils/slice_images_and_labels.py \
    --images data/images --labels data/labels --output data/sliced \
    --slice-width 640 --slice-height 640 --overlap 128 \
    --skip-empty --min-area-ratio 0.1
```

author: scottschreckengaust
body:
## Summary

Removes the standing `allow-dependencies-licenses: pkg:pypi/aiohttp@3.14.1` exemption from the `dependency-review` job, rewrites the comment block into the steady-state policy (no standing exemptions; UNKNOWN = harvest lag = file a `license-review` issue), rewrites `docs/SECURITY-TOOLING.md` step 3 to route UNKNOWNs to a `license-review`-labeled issue, and creates the `license-review` label.

Part of #127 (Phase 1 — the "Immediate task" checklist only; the issue stays OPEN for Phases 2–3).

## Root cause (reproduced)

PR #123 (merged as 5e23f58) added this to `.github/workflows/security.yml` (was line 238, with its rationale comment block at lines 221–237):

```yaml
allow-dependencies-licenses: pkg:pypi/aiohttp@3.14.1
```

Two mechanisms make this the wrong pattern (confirmed by reading the action's source at the pinned SHA `a1d282b` / v5.0.0):

1. **Name-only purl matching.** `src/purl.ts` `purlsMatch()` compares only `type` + namespace/name — it never reads `version`:

   ```ts
   export function purlsMatch(a: PackageURL, b: PackageURL): boolean {
     if (a.type.toLowerCase() !== b.type.toLowerCase()) {
       return false
     }
     return fullName(a)?.toLowerCase() === fullName(b)?.toLowerCase()
   }
   ```

   `src/licenses.ts` uses this for `licenseExclusions` (line 184), so the `@3.14.1` in the entry was documentation, not an expiry — the entry silently exempts **every future aiohttp version** from license checking, precisely when the next bump would need the gate.

2. **PR-diff scoping makes it dead config.** The action only evaluates the base↔head dependency diff of the current PR. The moment #123 merged, no future PR re-presents `aiohttp@3.14.1` in a diff, so the entry can never fire for its documented purpose — its only possible future effect is the name-wide hole above. Meanwhile the UNKNOWN warning itself is self-expiring (only appears on a PR touching the package) and never fails the gate, so it's the better signal.

The post-merge design note on PR #123 ("Design note (post-review, pre-merge)") reached the same verdict and pointed to #127; `docs/SECURITY-TOOLING.md` step 3 still instructed "add the purl to `allow-dependencies-licenses`" as the standing remedy, contradicting that design.

## The fix

- **`.github/workflows/security.yml`** — deleted the `allow-dependencies-licenses` line and replaced the 17-line per-entry rationale block with a 10-line standing-policy comment: the key is intentionally absent (steady state: empty); UNKNOWN on a brand-new release is ClearlyDefined harvest lag, self-expiring, and routed to a `license-review` issue per #127 + docs/SECURITY-TOOLING.md; name-only purl matching is why standing entries are not kept.
- **`docs/SECURITY-TOOLING.md`** — step 3 of the UNKNOWN procedure now says: file (or update) a `license-review`-labeled issue for the purl recording the METADATA verdict + the ClearlyDefined definition link; the issue closes when ClearlyDefined shows a declared license (automation = #127 Leg B). Steps 1 (verify against wheel/sdist METADATA) and 2 (queue a harvest POST) are unchanged. The `allow-dependencies-licenses` mechanism is demoted to an explicit last-resort footnote retaining the name-only-matching caveat and the empty-list steady state.
- **`license-review` label created** (`gh label create`). Note: the description in the issue's suggested command exceeded GitHub's 100-char label-description limit (HTTP 422), so it was trimmed to 95 chars with the same meaning: "Dependency license undetected upstream (ClearlyDefined harvest lag); open until a verdict lands".

This is best-practice because it keeps the gate fail-closed-by-omission posture intact: the noisy-but-harmless warning stays visible as the signal, the durable artifact is a tracked issue (auditable, closeable on upstream verdict), and no permanent suppression outlives its evidence.

## Testing

- `pre-commit run --files .github/workflows/security.yml docs/SECURITY-TOOLING.md` — **all hooks pass** (check-yaml, actionlint, markdownlint-cli2, prettier, gitleaks, hygiene hooks). One iteration: prettier initially flagged the docs edit; fixed with `npx prettier --write docs/SECURITY-TOOLING.md`, re-ran clean.
- `grep -n "allow-dependencies-licenses" .github/workflows/security.yml` → only line 221, a comment (`# allow-dependencies-licenses is intentionally ABSENT ...`); **no active key remains**.
- `grep -rn "allow-dependencies-licenses" docs/` → only `docs/SECURITY-TOOLING.md:106`, the last-resort footnote.
- `gh label list --search license-review` → `license-review  Dependency license undetected upstream (ClearlyDefined harvest lag); open until a verdict lands  #5319e7`.
- Doc-drift check: `AGENTS.md` §Dependency notes and `docs/PINNING.md` describe the **pip `overrides.txt`** mechanism (checkov cap), which this PR does not touch — both remain true. No other file references the removed exemption.
- The `dependency-review` job only runs on PRs — **this PR is the live exercise of the edited job** (the dependency diff is empty, so it should pass trivially and prove the YAML is well-formed in-action).

## Dependencies / related

- **#127** — this PR is Phase 1 (immediate-task checklist). **Phase 2 (Leg B: B1 PR-time detect + B2 scheduled verdict poller) and Phase 3 (Leg A pip-overrides sweep + Leg C npm sweep) are queued follow-ups on the same issue; #127 stays OPEN when this merges (intentionally no closing keyword).**
- **PR #123** — introduced the exemption this PR removes; its post-merge design note is the trigger for #127.
- **#78** — Leg A (pip overrides redundancy sweep) is a leg of that automated toolchain-update workflow.
- Out of scope, noted only: the per-tool scanner-requirements split discussed on PR #123 is not part of #127; `.github/scanner-requirements/*` untouched.

## Problem
PR #62's `backfill-focal` route **failed the Vercel production build** (`main` is currently red, blocking all deploys). Build log:
```
./app/api/cron/backfill-focal/route.ts:8:14  Ecmascript file had an error
Turbopack build failed with 1 errors
```
This project runs **Next.js 16 Cache Components**, which forbids `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` (see the explicit note in `app/api/health/pipeline/route.ts`). tsc / eslint / unit tests / the authed route-smoke all passed — only `next build` (Turbopack) catches it, and it slipped because the isolated worktree's *symlinked* `node_modules` makes a local Turbopack build impossible.

## Fix
Removed the `export const dynamic` line. The route is already dynamic — it reads `request.headers`. `maxDuration = 300` stays (matches other cron routes).

## Verification
Vercel production build (the authoritative check that was failing) must go green on merge. Restores deployability of `main`; unblocks the #62 focal backfill.

author: aherriot
body:
Closes the **Explore → Read → Quiz → Steer** loop (docs/09 M4, docs/01 §6, docs/04). After the quiz, the child gets a Steer result screen to choose where to go next, and their reading level quietly adapts from how they did.

## Difficulty adaptation
- **`lib/reading/adapt.ts`** (pure, unit-tested) — a rolling window of the last 3 scores *taken at the current level* moves the reading level at most one step: avg ≥85% steps up, ≤50% steps down, otherwise holds. Only same-level scores count and a full window is required, so a single off day never yo-yos the level (docs/04).
- **`/api/steer`** re-grades the child's first-try answers against the loop's stored `quizJson` — the difficulty signal is computed server-side and can't be spoofed from the client — then writes `Loop.quizPct` and applies the adaptation to `Child.readingLevel` + `recentQuizScores`.

## Steer choices (post-quiz)
- **"Go deeper on {topic}"** opens a follow-up question that spawns a new *threaded* `Loop` with `parentLoopId` set, passing the parent topic as `parentContext` through `/api/explore` (normalize) and `/api/lesson`. Parent-loop ownership is verified before linking (a spoofed id is dropped, not honored).
- **"Explore something new"** returns to the Explore screen.
- A step **up** shows a quiet "leveling up!" note; a step **down** stays silent (docs/04).

## Scope
Kept to the Steer item. XP/levels/badges (**Progress**) and related-branch suggestions (**World map**) remain their own M4 items. The prompt-layer `parentContext` plumbing already existed; this PR wires it end-to-end.

## Tests
- `lib/reading/adapt.test.ts` — 9 cases covering the window, thresholds, level bounds, and same-level filtering.
- `e2e/steer.spec.ts` — go-deeper follow-up spawns a new lesson; "explore something new" returns to Explore. Updated `e2e/quiz.spec.ts` for the renamed result button.
- `npm run check` (typecheck + lint + prettier + design-system + 104 unit tests) green; Steer/quiz/explore/calibrate/auth e2e specs pass serially (CI runs `workers: 1`).

author: hashbender
body:
## Summary
Gateway `/resume` and `/sessions` are now scoped to the caller's own origin on every adapter, closing an IDOR where an authorized caller could bind their session to — or enumerate — another user's/room's transcript. Salvage of #52355 (@claudlos) onto current `main`, plus one follow-up commit closing the last reviewer-flagged gap.

Root cause: non-Matrix `/resume` resolved a persisted session id/title **globally** before calling `session_store.switch_session()`, and `/sessions all` enumerated ids + previews across every session — the ids/previews needed to target the IDOR (CWE-639).

## Changes
- `gateway/slash_commands.py`: generalize the Matrix-only room guard to an adapter-agnostic ownership check — live origin when active; DB row `source` + `user_id` + `chat_id` + `thread_id` for persisted-only rows. Applied to the direct-id/title path and the listing/numeric paths on every platform. Matrix path preserved and tightened to thread-level. Explicit admin `--all` override honored.
- **Follow-up (this salvage): fail closed on the persisted fallback when the caller keys on `user_id_alt`.** `build_session_key()` keys the participant on `user_id_alt or user_id` (Signal/Feishu), but the `sessions` table stores only `user_id`. A per-user row a caller shared the `user_id` of — but not the `user_id_alt` — mapped to a *different* live session key yet matched on `user_id` alone, so a co-member could resume/enumerate another member's persisted per-user group or no-chat_id DM session. The live-origin guard already compared `user_id_alt`; the persisted branch now fails closed for both per-user branches. Shared groups and chat_id-keyed DMs are unaffected.
- `hermes_state.py`: docstring documenting the `chat_id`/`thread_id` origin capture used for scoping.
- `locales/en.yaml`: resume-denied message.
- Regression tests in `tests/gateway/test_resume_command.py` (incl. the Signal/Feishu `user_id_alt` persisted probe).

## Validation
| Case (persisted path) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Signal per-user group, same `user_id` / different `user_id_alt` | resumes (IDOR) | denied |
| Signal no-chat_id DM, different `user_id_alt` | resumes (IDOR) | denied |
| Telegram per-user group, own row (no alt) | resumes | resumes |
| Shared group (`group_sessions_per_user=false`), co-member | resumes | resumes |
| Same user / different chat; blank-source; missing-owner; legacy NULL-chat | resumes (IDOR) | denied |

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_resume_command.py` → 48 passed. Sibling security suites (`test_matrix_project_context_isolation`, `test_session_boundary_security_state`) green.

Contributor authorship (@claudlos) preserved across the 7 cherry-picked commits; the follow-up fail-closed commit is mine.

Closes #52355.

## Infographic
![gateway resume IDOR scoping](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa08084/13bDRFM3_gu1e-swX-7bs_BNKi8fvl.png)

author: forevka
body:
## What & why

Phase 4b — the **C# write half** of WordprocessingDocument-style access, completing the C# story. **Stacked on #122 (Phase 4a, read query)**: this PR is based on the 4a branch so the diff shows only the edit surface. Will retarget to `main` once #122 merges.

## New C# API

```csharp
var doc = engine.ImportDocx(bytes);
var editor = doc.Edit()
    .SetParagraphText("p1", "New heading")
    .InsertParagraphAfter("p1", "A body paragraph")
    .ReplaceText("p2", 0, 5, "Hello");

editor.Undo();                       // multi-op edits undo as one step
bool more = editor.CanRedo;
File.WriteAllBytes("out.docx", editor.ToDocument().ExportDocx());
```

- `WordDocument.Edit()` → `WordDocumentEditor` (opens a stateful JS `DocumentEditor` in V8)
- `SetParagraphText`, `InsertText` / `DeleteText` / `ReplaceText` (UTF-16 offsets), `RemoveBlock`, `InsertParagraphAfter` / `InsertParagraphBefore`
- `Undo` / `Redo` / `CanUndo` / `CanRedo` — free from the operation engine's inverses
- `ToDocument()` → a `WordDocument` over the edited model (preserves embedded image bytes) to query or export

## How

No new mutation logic — it rides the existing 37-op engine via the Phase 2 `DocumentEditor`. A new `openEditor` bridge fn on the ClearScript entry returns a `DocumentEditor` instance; the C# `WordDocumentEditor` calls its methods (`InvokeMethod`) and reads `.doc` / `.canUndo` back. `ToDocument()` reuses `WordDocument.WithDoc` so image bytes / warnings carry over.

## Verification (end-to-end, showcase)

```
Edit:
  after 2 edits : first="EDITED HEADING", blocks=282, canUndo=True
  after 2 undos : first="canvas-word", blocks=281, canRedo=True
  round-trip    : re-imported edited docx → find 'EDITED HEADING' = 1
```

ClearScript lib + showcase build clean (net10, Release); frontend typecheck clean; bundle rebuilt.

## Notes

- Style patching (`SetParagraphStyle`) is deferred — it needs a `ParaStylePatch` record + `ToJs()` marshaling; logged for a follow-up. Text + structural edits ship here.
- CI does not build .NET, so the C# side was verified locally by running the showcase.

author: raullenchai
body:
## Summary

Closes #969.

The standalone `python -m vllm_mlx.server` entrypoint at
`vllm_mlx/server.py:1789` accepted `--kv-cache-turboquant` in argparse
but silently dropped the value at the `SchedulerConfig(...)`
construction site (line 2144). Additionally, `choices=["v4", "k8v4"]`
rejected the `--kv-cache-turboquant none` off-switch added in #962.

Two user-visible silent-flag-drop bugs of the same class as #400 —
argparse advertises the flag, engine never sees it.

## Docs check + option choice

`python -m vllm_mlx.server` is a **supported** public surface:

- Included in the `release-smoke` gate (docs/development/releasing.md).
- Covered by `scripts/audit_cli_config_fidelity.py` and
  `tests/test_cli_config_fidelity.py::test_prefill_step_size_is_plumbed_in_server_main`.
- Referenced across `tests/` as "the second supported entrypoint"
  (`test_serve_host_loopback_default.py`, `test_embeddings_extra_guard.py`,
  `test_audio_route_registration_gate.py`).
- Used in `examples/mllm_benchmark.py`.

Systematic invariant: since the entrypoint is supported, its flag
behaviour MUST match `rapid-mlx serve` (cli.py). **Option 1 (functional
parity)** is the systematic answer; Option 2 (fail-loud drop) would
break the supported-surface contract.

## Fix — extraction pattern

- **New helper**: `vllm_mlx/turboquant.py::turboquant_scheduler_kwargs(args)` returns
  the four SchedulerConfig kwargs (`kv_cache_turboquant`,
  `kv_cache_turboquant_bits`, `kv_cache_turboquant_group_size`,
  `kv_cache_turboquant_mode`) derived from the resolved argparse
  values.
- **Both entries call it**: `cli.py::serve_command` and
  `server.py::main` unpack `**turboquant_scheduler_kwargs(args)` into
  their `SchedulerConfig(...)`. Future TurboQuant fields land in both
  entries automatically — drift prevention by design.
- **Server-side**: `"none"` added to argparse `choices` (mirrors
  cli.py:5953); `resolve_turboquant_mode_default` called on the
  args prior to SchedulerConfig construction (mirrors cli.py:2172).
- **Audit-side**: `scripts/audit_cli_config_fidelity.py` learned to
  expand `**helper(args)` star-unpacking via an explicit
  `KWARG_INJECTOR_HELPERS` map, so the shared-helper pattern doesn't
  false-positive as drift.

`cli.py` behaviour is unchanged on the wire — the mutex check and the
banner code that greps `args.kv_cache_turboquant` remain in place;
only the four SchedulerConfig kwargs at the construction site are
delegated to the helper.

## Test coverage — `tests/test_turboquant_k8v4.py::TestServerEntrypointParity`

Three new regression tests. All three fail on `main` prior to the fix
(verified by `git stash` on the implementation) and pass after:

- `test_server_argparse_accepts_none_off_switch` — AST-scrapes
  `--kv-cache-turboquant` from `server.main` and asserts `"none"` is
  in `choices`. Would have caught the #962 off-switch rejection.
- `test_server_main_threads_turboquant_into_scheduler_config` — walks
  the `SchedulerConfig(...)` call in `server.main` and asserts every
  TurboQuant field is either passed directly or unpacked from a known
  helper. Would have caught the silent flag drop that shipped for
  every 0.9.x release.
- `test_shared_turboquant_scheduler_kwargs_returns_all_fields` — pins
  the helper's return shape so a future TurboQuant field addition to
  `SchedulerConfig` can't silently degrade `python -m vllm_mlx.server`
  while `cli.py` keeps working (the banner code in cli.py references
  the raw args).

Existing turboquant / cli-config-fidelity / help-fuzzy / no-mllm-flag
tests all pass (`143 + 49 = 192` selected). `ruff check` and
`ruff format --check` are clean on all touched files.

author: kwsantiago
body:
The payoff of the measured-boot work: with the appliance booting through a Lanzaboote UKI (so TPM PCR 11 is a real measurement of the kernel+initrd+cmdline), the FROST gate can seal the vault's LUKS key to `sealPcrs = [ 7 11 ]` and it now binds the boot image itself, not just Secure Boot policy (all PCR 7 covers). This closes the at-rest weakness where a swapped kernel/initrd could still satisfy PCR 7 and auto-release the key.

New `measured-seal` nixosTest (UKI boot + swtpm, no appliance-code change, `frost-gate.nix` already supports `sealPcrs`) proves the full property end to end:
1. **Seal binds PCR 11.** First boot provisions the vault and TPM2-seals it; the token's `tpm2-pcrs` is asserted to be exactly `[7, 11]`, not just `[7]`.
2. **Unchanged boot round-trips.** A reboot on the same UKI re-measures the same PCR 11, so the TPM releases the key, the volume unlocks, and a canary written before the reboot survives (unlocked, not reformatted).
3. **Changed boot fails closed.** Extending PCR 11 to a different value (what a swapped kernel/initrd/cmdline would measure) makes the TPM refuse to release the key: a fresh unlock attempt fails and no mapper is created. There is no passphrase keyslot to fall back on (the gate wipes it after enrolling the TPM2 token). This is the tamper-detection property measured boot exists to provide.

Reuses Lanzaboote's pinned image harness by reference; Secure Boot key enrollment is skipped (`keyFixture = false`, `allowUnsigned = true`) since PCR 11 is measured regardless and `mode = "tpm"` seals to PCR values, not to Secure Boot signatures.

author: nvaytet
body:
Sometimes you have a slice of data that contains all NaNs, but you still want to inspect the rest of the data with e.g. the `slicer`.

Example:
```Py
import plopp as pp
%matplotlib widget

da = pp.data.data3d()
da['z', 0].values[...] = np.nan
pp.slicer(da)
```

This would raise with a message saying it cannot compute limits because data is all NaN.
Now we instead return a NaN range, which get converted to a null range [0, 0].
The plot is just blank instead. Moving the slider can still be used to view other healthy slices.

`web_fetch` (and `memory_fetch`, gated on it) were turned **off** by default in #314's lean-edit shape — the reasoning being it looked redundant with `shell_exec` + `curl`. author: houdinnie
body:
💡 What: Optimized the `getUserStats` function in `server/db.ts` to use Drizzle SQL aggregate functions (`count`, `sum`, `max`).

🎯 Why: The previous implementation fetched all user sessions for a given user into memory and then performed aggregation using `Array.prototype.reduce` and `Array.prototype.sort`. This was an O(N) operation that increased in latency and memory usage as user history grew.

📊 Impact: Moves the aggregation to the database layer, reducing complexity from O(N) to O(1) in terms of data transfer and application-side processing. This results in faster dashboard loading times and lower memory overhead.

🔬 Measurement: Implemented comprehensive unit tests in `server/db.test.ts` using a new `setDb` dependency injection helper to verify that the optimized query correctly calculates session counts, message totals, and last active timestamps.

author: kennethreitz
body:
## Summary

Three targeted improvements surfaced by an audit of the framework — two reliability fixes and one CI gap. Ships as v7.1.3.

### 1. Redis rate-limit atomicity (bug fix)
`RedisBackend.hit` / `AsyncRedisBackend.ahit` performed `INCR` then `EXPIRE` as two separate round-trips. If the process died (or the connection dropped) between them, the key never received a TTL — permanently rate-limiting that client until manual eviction. Both now use a single atomic Lua `EVAL` that increments and, on the first hit of a window, sets the expiry.

### 2. Background task graceful shutdown
`api.background`'s `ThreadPoolExecutor` was never drained, so in-flight fire-and-forget tasks were abandoned on shutdown. Added `BackgroundQueue.shutdown()` and a registered shutdown event handler that drains the pool off the event loop.

### 3. CI now enforces lint + types
`ruff` and `mypy` previously ran only in the manual release guard, so lint/type regressions could land on `main`. New `Lint & Types` workflow runs both on every push and PR. The tree passes both today.

## Tests
- New `tests/test_v713_improvements.py` (7 tests): background drain/reject-after-shutdown, app-level shutdown drain, and Redis atomic-eval behavior (including a fake that fails if `incr`/`expire` are called directly).
- Updated the existing fake Redis in `tests/test_round4.py` to implement `eval`.
- Full suite: 740 passed, ruff clean, mypy clean.

## Notes
Also corrected the stale `[Unreleased]` compare link in the changelog (pointed at v7.1.1 despite v7.1.2 shipping).

author: emooreatx
body:
## What

**0.5.72** — the owner can now **bound** an act-on-behalf delegation grant, a single capability guard **enforces** the bound, and the delegate **sees exactly what it holds on every use**.

### Server
- **`DelegationConstraints`** `{ actions_allow (tri-state: `null`=all / `[]`=read-only / subset), actions_deny, goal }` — the enforceable subset of CC 2.4.1.2 `delegated_scope[]` + `delegation_purpose`. Rides **inside the signed `delegates_to` envelope** (durable + auditable; CC 2.1.1 forward-compat) and caches on the grant.
- **`authorize_delegated(caller, verb)`** + `require_verb` + a `CapabilityVerb` enum with a server **never-list** (`delegate` / `wipe` / `accord_halt`) in `src/auth/gate.rs`; wired after `require_owner` in claim-remote / announce / peering / set-age. Owner sessions (`actor.is_none()`) are unconstrained. Denials return a structured `403 {denied_by, verb, goal, detail}`.
- **`/delegate`** carries `constraints`; **`/approve`** folds them **tighten-only** (`tightened_with`: allow = ∩, deny = ∪ — an approver can only narrow, never widen).
- **Self-expiring edges**: `emit_signed_attestation` gained `expires_at` (= CC 2.4.1.2 `delegation_valid_until`).
- **Transparency**: an `x-ciris-delegation` response header on **every** dgrant-authenticated response (global middleware, `src/delegation_transparency.rs`) + a `delegation` object embedded in `/claim` + `/token` issuance bodies.

### Client (KMP/Compose)
- New models (`DelegationConstraints`, `GrantCharacteristics`, `CapabilityCatalog`), API-client wiring on `/delegate` + `/approve`, a collapsible **ConstraintsEditor** (goal + restrict-actions allow/deny chips + never-delegated note) and a **"what this delegation permits"** display. **Localized to all 28 languages.**

## Constitution
No change needed — CC 0.6.1 already defines `delegates_to { delegated_scope[], delegation_purpose, delegation_valid_from/until }`; deny-lists/tasks ride as CC 2.1.1 forward-compat extension members; enforcement is consumer-side policy.

## Tests
7 `gate` unit + 12 `device_grant` integration (transparency, constraint carry, tighten-only, never-list, allow/deny overrides) green; `claim_remote`/`federation_admin`/`ownership` suites green; clippy + rustfmt clean.

## Notes
- Substrate floor **unchanged** (edge v7.4.4 / persist v11.5.0 / verify v8.3.0).
- `tests/{claim_remote,ownership}.rs` carry **rustfmt-only** whitespace changes (mechanical).
- Deferred (spec-only): resources & tasks axes, per-request metering, reading constraints back from the graph edge in `resolve_bearer` (today enforced from the in-memory grant — consistent since the bearer is ephemeral; the envelope copy is the durable/audit record).
- Docs: `FSD/DELEGATION_CONSTRAINTS.md` (impl status), `FSD/RNS_CONTROL_RELAY.md`, `FSD/MESH_SEED_RUNBOOK_POST_DELEGATION.md`.

author: ddsalam
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to the Transaksi Pelanggan investigation. Locked root cause: SolaMax's pull is faithful to EasyMax at sync time, but each domain's trailing rescan window (pelanggan=3d, edc=5d, cash/tebus=7d, opname/delivery/tera implicit ~1h) never revisits a date once it ages out — so an EasyMax-side edit made after that point is silently missed forever. `sales` already has a proven fix for exactly this (`syncSalesRescan`: an independent, wider, business-date-keyed re-pull). This PR generalizes that pattern to the other 6 windowed domains: **pelanggan, edc, opname, delivery, tera, cash, tebus**. (`deposit`/`piutang`/`hutang`/`terra_resmi`/`masters`/`realtank` are full-sync every cycle already — immune by construction, untouched.)

Two automatic tiers, no human in the loop:
- **Tier 1** — nightly/weekly recent-window sweep per domain (pelanggan/edc 30d nightly, opname/delivery/tera 14d nightly, cash/tebus 30d weekly).
- **Tier 2** — full-history backstop, off-peak (02:00–05:00 WIB), so staleness has a coverage guarantee instead of depending on a manual `--resync`. pelanggan/edc get an additional weekly 90-day "wide" pass (heavy union/join queries on MySQL 5.0).

## Implementation
- `domains.ts` — bounded `[lo,hiExcl)` `*_RESYNC` query variants per domain. EDC/CASH/TEBUS/TERA just widen the existing hot-path query (reuse its `map()` unchanged). OPNAME/DELIVERY get a materially different query mirroring `SALES_RESYNC`: filtered by header business-date instead of `DTGLJAM`, without the hot path's `IS NOT NULL` filter, synthesizing a midnight-WIB timestamp when `DTGLJAM` is null (same NULL-shift-3 defect `sales` was fixed for).
- `sync.ts` — `walkDateWindowsForward` (generic chunked-by-date walker, always bounded — avoids the 288k full-view stall from 2026-06-21/`e3ea59a`), `isOffPeakWib` gate, 7 per-domain sweep functions, `SweepJob`/`SWEEP_TABLE`, `runManualSweep` (CLI-triggerable single run), `runSweepJobs` (per-domain try/catch isolation inside `runCycle`, matching existing convention). `runForever` computes due jobs and passes them into `runCycle`.
- `config.ts` — per-domain window/cadence knobs + shared off-peak hours + chunk width.
- `index.ts` — `--deep-sweep <domain> <days>` CLI flag for a manual single run (used to verify rollout before enabling the schedule).

Idempotency: every sweep re-pull goes through the existing REPLACE/UPSERT `/ingest` path unchanged — advisory-lock-protected for `pelanggan_sale`/`voucher_sale` (#45), `ON CONFLICT` for `edc`, natural-key UPSERT for the rest. **No backend changes in this PR.**

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm --filter @solamax/agent typecheck` / `pnpm -r typecheck` (repo-wide)
- [x] `pnpm -r lint`
- [x] `pnpm --filter @solamax/agent test` — 63/63 green, including new coverage:
  - `domains.test.ts`: each `*_RESYNC`'s bounded SQL shape; OPNAME/DELIVERY NULL-DTGLJAM synthesis
  - `sync.test.ts`: `walkDateWindowsForward` via `runManualSweep` (edc, pelanggan); `sweepJobs` per-domain failure isolation in `runCycle`; `isOffPeakWib` boundary behavior
- [ ] **Not yet run**: live rollout verification against the SPBU machine + Cloud SQL (needs physical/network access to the SPBU Windows box, which isn't available from this environment) — deploy + manual `--deep-sweep` trigger + Cloud SQL before/after diff still pending, per the plan.

author: fw-bot-adhoc
body:
## Problema

Al **cancelar el remanente** de una línea de venta no entregada, en ciertos casos en vez de bajar la cantidad en los pickings existentes se genera una **contraentrega** (movimiento inverso / picking de entrada fantasma) y el movimiento de salida queda huérfano en `confirmed`, comprometiendo stock.

## Causa

`button_cancel_remaining` bajaba `product_uom_qty` y delegaba la baja al recálculo de la regla de stock. Bajar la cantidad por debajo de lo ya aprovisionado genera un **procurement de cantidad negativa** (`_action_launch_stock_rule` → `product_qty = product_uom_qty - qty_procurement < 0`).

Ese move negativo solo se **fusiona** (`stock.move._merge_moves`) con el move de salida original si coinciden **todos** los campos de la clave de merge (`_prepare_merge_moves_distinct_fields`), entre ellos `location_id`. El move negativo nace con el `location_id` del **origen nominal de la regla**; si la salida original fue reservada desde una **sub-ubicación** distinta, `location_id` no coincide → no se fusiona → el move negativo sobrevive y en `_action_confirm` se da vuelta como contraentrega (swap de ubicaciones, qty × −1, `to_refund=True`), dejando el move de salida huérfano.

Esto explica la intermitencia: solo ocurre cuando la salida se reserva desde una sub-ubicación ≠ origen nominal de la regla (depósitos multi-ubicación). El reset de `printed` previo era una mitigación parcial que no cubría este caso.

## Solución

En `button_cancel_remaining`, en vez de depender del recálculo, se **cancelan explícitamente los movimientos de salida pendientes** de la línea (excluyendo devoluciones del cliente) y se setea la cantidad con `skip_procurement` para no relanzar la regla. Robusto ante cualquier sub-ubicación de reserva. Se eliminan el reset de `printed` y la validación comentada, mitigaciones parciales del mismo caso.

## Test plan

Nuevo test de regresión `tests/test_cancel_remaining_contraentrega.py`:

- Confirma una OV con la salida reservada desde una sub-ubicación distinta al origen nominal de la regla, cancela el remanente y verifica que:
  - la línea baja a la cantidad entregada,
  - el movimiento de salida queda **cancelado** (no huérfano),
  - **no** se genera contraentrega (sin picking de entrada / sin movimiento inverso vivo).
- Verificado que el test **falla sin el fix** (move de salida queda vivo + contraentrega) y **pasa con el fix**.

author: sbaerlocher
body:
## Summary

Fixes a self-DoS in the session refresh path reported in the Notion intake ([KV-Refresh-Lock pinnt User in 401-Loop bei transientem Parqet-5xx](https://app.notion.com/p/373bf097036e81fb93d9e75831db2e8f)).

When a near-expiry session refresh hit a non-2xx from the Parqet token endpoint, `maybeRefreshSession` returned early **without deleting** the `refresh_lock:{userId}` KV key, leaving it set for the full 60s TTL. Every request in that window saw the lock, served the expiring session, and — once it lapsed — hit Parqet with a dead access token. That tripped `ParqetAuthError`, which wiped the session + cookie and showed the "session ended" banner. The user was pinned in that state for up to 60s over a **transient** Parqet 5xx, even though the next refresh would have succeeded.

## Changes

- **Release the lock in a `finally`** — a failed refresh never strands the lock, so the next request retries immediately (the core fix).
- **Transient vs permanent failures** — `refreshAccessToken` now returns a discriminated `RefreshResult`. A 4xx is a permanent dead grant (session torn down cleanly → clean logout); 5xx / network / parse errors are transient (keep the still-valid session, retry next request instead of logging the user out over a blip).
- **Poll on a held lock** — when a peer holds the lock, briefly poll for its refreshed tokens (≤400ms) before falling back, so a request burst doesn't all serve the soon-dead token.

## Tests

- `pnpm test` — 175 passed
- `pnpm check` — 0 errors
- ESLint + Prettier clean

Added coverage for: transient (5xx/network/parse) vs permanent (4xx) refresh outcomes, lock release after both success and failure, and clean logout on a dead grant.

author: kshitijk4poor
body:
## Summary
Codex app-server exec/apply_patch requests on gateway/cron contexts now honor `approvals.mode: off` / `/yolo` / `HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1` instead of silently failing closed.

**Root cause:** On non-CLI contexts no approval-UI callback is wired, so `CodexAppServerSession._decide_exec_approval` / `_decide_apply_patch_approval` hit their fail-closed `return "decline"` path. Codex sees a synthetic "user denied" and drops to read-only — the bot appears responsive but can't write files, and no prompt surfaces anywhere.

**Fix:** When the user has explicitly opted out of Hermes approvals, build the session with `_ServerRequestRouting(auto_approve_exec=True, auto_approve_apply_patch=True)` so codex's own sandbox permission profile (`~/.codex/config.toml`) becomes the boundary. Defaults (`manual`/`smart`/unset) keep the current fail-closed behavior — a no-op for anyone who hasn't opted out.

Salvage of #26533 by @simpolism (also the reporter of #26530). Re-authored onto current `main`: the construction site the original PR targeted (`run_agent.py`) has since moved into `agent/codex_runtime.py::run_codex_app_server_turn()`. Authorship preserved.

## Changes
- `agent/codex_runtime.py`: resolve opt-out at session-build time via the canonical `tools.approval._get_approval_mode()` (which already normalizes the YAML-1.1 bare-`off`→`False` case) + `is_current_session_yolo_enabled()` + `HERMES_YOLO_MODE`; pass `request_routing`. Reading at build time means a mid-session `/yolo` toggle is honored too.
- `tests/run_agent/test_codex_app_server_integration.py`: 5 tests — config `off`, YAML `False`, `HERMES_YOLO_MODE`, session `/yolo`, plus the default `manual` fail-closed regression guard.

## Validation
| approvals state | auto_approve | real exec decision |
|---|---|---|
| `off` | True | `accept` |
| `manual` / `smart` (default) | False | `decline` |
| `HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1` | True | `accept` |
| `/yolo` session toggle | True | `accept` |

- 28/28 integration tests pass (23 existing + 5 new); 58/58 session tests pass.
- E2E with real imports + temp `HERMES_HOME` config: the gateway-context exec decision flips `decline`→`accept` only when opted out; fail-closed preserved otherwise.

## Notes
- The bigger "surface codex approvals in gateway channels" feature (async per-tool-call correlation) is out of scope — tracked by the #25889 / #27636 / #43217 cluster. This fix unblocks the immediate silent-read-only case.
- Not addressed here: the MCP `mcpServer/elicitation/request` fail-closed path for non-`hermes-tools` servers (reported on #26530 by @TAE58). That path declines by hard-coded server-name gating (arguably intentional) rather than `_routing` — a separate design question.

Closes #26530

---
### Follow-up commit (self-review, `hermes-pr-review` Phase 2)
`refactor(approval): extract is_approval_bypass_active(); use frozen-env bypass in codex routing`

Phase-2 review flagged that the initial adaptation re-read `os.getenv("HERMES_YOLO_MODE")` at runtime, which diverges from the repo's security invariant — `HERMES_YOLO_MODE` is frozen into `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN` at import time precisely so a mid-process skill can't set the env var and flip the approval bypass (prompt-injection escalation path). Fixed architecturally: extracted the canonical three-source bypass check into `tools.approval.is_approval_bypass_active()` (this was the 4th inline copy of that OR-chain; `codex_runtime.py` now calls the shared helper). Env-yolo test updated to patch `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN` (canonical pattern) instead of `setenv`. 28 integration + 77 session/yolo tests pass; E2E re-confirmed.

author: khamusa
body:
## Summary

Consolidates the fully-implemented, individually-reviewed stack of PRs #9–#20 into a single PR onto `main`. Each of the 19 commits here was previously implemented (Sonnet) and independently verified (Opus, re-running tests/lint itself, not trusting self-reports) as its own PR, stacked on top of the already-merged #2–#8. That stack hit squash-merge "ghost conflict" issues (each squash-merge of an ancestor PR rewrites history, so downstream branches show spurious conflicts in files every PR touches — SPEC.md's status table, CHANGELOG.md, `.rubocop.yml`), so rather than resolve the same mechanical conflicts 9+ times, this PR does it once: a clean `reset --hard origin/main && cherry-pick <range>` of every unique commit, conflicts resolved once, full suite re-verified.

Individual PRs #9, #10, #11, #12, #13, #15, #16, #17, #18, #19, #20 are superseded by this PR and will be closed with a reference to it.

### What's implemented

- **§4 Argument Derivation Engine** — `ObjectTypeToArgument`/`InputObjectToArgument` mappers, `ArgumentDerivation`, including Symbol (sibling-action) source support wired to the Rails plugin's controller registry.
- **§5 Field Derivation Engine** — `ObjectTypeToField` mapper, `FieldDerivation`, including ActiveRecord-model source support wired to the AR adapter.
- **§6 `DerivableInputObject`** / **§7 `DerivableObjectType`** — `derive_from` mixins with deferred resolution, inline-declaration collision detection, and (fixed mid-stack) recursive resolution + universal cycle detection so a `derive_from` chain resolves correctly regardless of declaration order, and a genuine cycle (same-mixin or crossing both mixins) raises `CyclicDependencyError` with the full path instead of a misleading error.
- **§8 Rails Plugin** — `ControllerConcern` (`argument`, `arguments_from`, `arguments`, `argument_namespace`, `eager_load_argument_sources!` with sibling-cycle detection) and per-namespace `ArgumentSchema`.
- **§9 ActiveRecord Adapter** — `ActiveRecordMapper` covering the full column-type table, Rails-enum generation, null-inference, and the `id`/`created_at`/`updated_at` exclusion.
- **Full-stack integration spec** proving the whole pipeline composes: AR model → `ActiveRecordMapper` → `FieldDerivation` → `DerivableObjectType` → `arguments_from` on a controller → `ArgumentDerivation` → `DerivableInputObject` → `ArgumentSchema` coercion.
- **Rails dev-mode reload safety** — `ArgumentSchema`/`ActiveRecordMapper`'s enum cache now de-dup/rebuild correctly under Zeitwerk class reloading (previously both risked `GraphQL::Schema::DuplicateNamesError` after a reload), plus a `GraphQL::Derivation::Rails.reset_for_reload!` utility and corrected SPEC.md guidance (`to_prepare`, not a one-shot initializer, for reloading dev/test apps) — `eager_load_argument_sources!`'s existing CI-validation role is preserved, not replaced.
- Several DX fixes from human review comments on PRs #7/#11/#13: clearer `ConfigurationError` messages (naming the source and available fields), eager `pick.override` keyword validation with typo suggestions.

SPEC.md's status table is fully `Implemented` for §2–§9 as of this PR.

author: erlloyd
body:
## What

Dashboard inbox overhaul so waiting/blocked sessions are visible and you can tell what they're waiting on, per Eric's three asks (+ one pulled-in enhancement).

**Inbox sorted by most recent activity.** The old sort tiered by `kind` first (review > reap > waiting > generic > check) and used recency only as a within-tier tiebreaker, so stale review rows floated above fresh waiting rows. Now it sorts purely by recency across all kinds. Recency is **session-transition-aware**: the server keeps an in-memory map that timestamps when each live session's `(status, state)` last changed (polled every 2s) and sorts on `lastActivityAt = max(bead.updated_at, last session transition)`. So a session flipping busy→waiting rises immediately, not just on a bead write. (`claude agents --json` exposes no per-session activity timestamp, so the server derives it from snapshot deltas — in-memory, resets to `startedAt` ordering on restart.)

**Both `status` and `state` shown, mirrored not collapsed.** Every inbox row now renders the raw session `status` (idle/busy/waiting) and `state` (working/blocked/done/failed/stopped) as chips, independent of the derived `kind` badge (`—` when no live session). The drill-in Sessions table already showed both.

**Waiting/blocked made loud.** Rows where `status === "waiting"` or `state === "blocked"` get a high-visibility treatment; the previous de-emphasis (opacity/muted border) on `check`-kind rows is removed so blocked-no-gate sessions no longer read as muted. On the drill-in view, the session `StatusBadge` gained an urgent case for waiting/blocked.

**"What it's waiting on" surfaced.** `waitingFor` — a real `claude agents --json` field emitted on permission-prompt-blocked sessions (value e.g. `permissionPrompt`), often absent locally — is passed through verbatim and rendered when present (inbox row + a drill-in "waiting for" column), degrading cleanly when absent. Also: the ask-block `context` prose is now plumbed through (the server was parsing it but the dashboard dropped it), and the `check`/`generic`/`review` `nextAction` falls back to the last real notes block instead of a constant.

**Drill-in extras.** A "last activity" relative-time in the header.

## Fixes found in review
- Drill-in **header** badge was fed the initiative's **bd issue status**, so a dependency-`blocked` epic false-fired the session-urgent red badge. Header now renders non-urgent (`urgent={false}` prop); the Sessions table keeps the urgent treatment (it's genuinely session-fed).
- `lastNotesBlock` could leak raw `<<<ateam-ask>>>` sentinel markup into a row's `nextAction` when a gate was cleared without a `--file` note; it now skips sentinel blocks.

## Testing
- `pnpm -r typecheck` clean (shared/server/web); `pnpm -r test` green (server 254, web 151); real `vite build` succeeds.
- Live Playwright verification of all inbox/drill-in behaviors against the running dashboard with real data (recency order, status/state chips, loud rows, drill-in badge/column/recency).
- Live smoke of the transition-recency change: server runs multiple poll cycles without crashing; `/api/snapshot` items carry `lastActivityAt` with correct max-semantics; inbox order sane.

## Scope / follow-ups (filed, not in this PR)
- Pre-existing React key warning on the drill-in Work Beads table.
- Extract the shared notes-block split helper (dedupe `lastNotesBlock` vs `notesHistory`).
- Remaining gated enhancements: relative-time chip, styling polish, richer REVIEW-row detail, structured-ask callout on the detail view. The pinned "Needs you" zone was explicitly dropped per Eric (loud-in-list retained).

author: penta2himajin
body:
## Summary
Unified, reproducible **measurement harness** — the baseline for Qwisp benchmarking. Replaces ad-hoc `/tmp` refs with a documented multi-regime ref set measured on **3 axes** per (regime × method), faithfully (invokes the real production runners).

## Ref set (benchmark-derived, natural length, gitignored → regenerate)
`qwisp/bench_prompts.py`: **code** (LiveCodeBench/SWE-bench style), **agentic** (BFCL format), **longctx** (RULER needle-in-haystack), **shortnl** (MT-Bench Q81 verbatim).
`qwisp/bench_refs.py`: generates all 4 refs in **one model load** → `<repo>/refs/` (gitignored).

## 3 axes (`qwisp/bench.sh`)
- **speed** — free-running tok/s (real `suffix-spec` / `bolt`).
- **fidelity** *(primary)* — teacher-forced per-token argmax vs strict-4bit greedy (**chaos-free**). `measureMLXFidelity` extended to buddy mode (`QWISP_SKIPMODE=3`) + f32-full + near-tie diagnostic.
- **correctness** — per-regime task hooks (`qwisp/bench_correctness.py`: ast.parse / tool-call / needle / non-degenerate), read as **delta vs strict**.

## Validated results (C=64, GEN=128, fast-SSD)
| method | code | agentic | longctx | shortnl | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| strict fidelity | 100% | 100% | 93.8% | 98.4% | 98.1% |
| bolt fidelity | 89.1% | 92.2% | 93.0% | 79.7% | 88.5% |
| strict tok/s | 21.8 | 20.9 | 25.4 | 23.9 | 23.0 |
| bolt tok/s | 27.5 | 29.6 | 31.2 | 24.7 | 28.2 |

All correctness PASS; strict-PASS→bolt-PASS every regime ⇒ bolt's ~12% divergence is benign.

## Key corrections this harness surfaced
- **Teacher-forced fidelity** shows bolt is ~88% per-token faithful — the old free-running token-match (4–17%) was **greedy chaos**, not infidelity.
- **Realistic strict fast-SSD ≈ 20–25 tok/s**; the earlier quicksort 150/88 numbers were a **repeat-pad + pathologically-repetitive-prompt artifact**.

Engine changes are additive/safe: `measureMLXFidelity` buddy mode + `PROMPT_TOKENS/OUT_TOKENS` dump behind `QWISP_DUMP_TOKENS`. Strict default path unchanged.

author: mcdonc
body:
## Summary

Adds `KLANGK_PRODUCT_NAME` (default `Klangk`) so a deployment can rename the product with one env var and **no frontend rebuild**. The value flows through `GET /api/v1/config` (`product_name`) into the browser tab title, the app-bar logo wordmark, and all outgoing emails.

Closes #1149. First item from the #261 deployment-customization tracking issue (Tier 1) — this is the foundational seam the runtime-logo, email-templating, and legal-link items build on.

## Changes

**Backend**
- `emailsvc.product_name()` interpolates the configured name into verification / password-reset / invitation email subjects and bodies. Resolved at send time via `resolve_env_value`, so the `file:`/`cmd:` prefixes work and no restart-on-change assumptions.
- `GET /api/v1/config` now returns `product_name` (module-level `PRODUCT_NAME`, consistent with `LOGIN_BANNER`).

**Frontend**
- New `lib/branding.dart` — a `Branding` helper (single source of truth for white-label display values) populated from `/config`. `@visibleForTesting reset()` keeps static state from leaking between tests.
- `AuthService._loadToken` and `LoginPage._loadConfig` feed `/config` into `Branding`.
- `MaterialApp.title`, page titles (`page_title.dart`), and the `KlangkLogo` wordmark now read `Branding.name`. Default `'Klangk'` when unset or when the field is absent (older backends), so existing deployments are unchanged.

**Docs**
- `docs/reference/environment.md` (new row), `.env.example` (commented example), and a new **Product Name** section in `docs/deployment/customizing.md`.

## Behavior note

The logo wordmark previously rendered lowercase `'klangk'` while titles/emails used `'Klangk'`. This unifies it to the configured name (default `'Klangk'`), per the acceptance criteria in #1149. The robot **icon** is intentionally out of scope — that's the separate runtime-logo item (#261 Tier 1).

The CLI's `--help` identity (`klangkc`, "Klangk Client") is also out of scope: it's the client tool's own identity, rendered before any server connection, and not derivable from a server's `/config`.

## Verification

- Backend: full suite passes (`2087 passed`), including new `test_emailsvc.py::test_uses_configured_product_name` and `test_api.py` config tests (default + reflected).
- Frontend: full suite passes (`833 passed`), including new `Branding` coverage in `auth_service_test`, a custom-name logo test, and updated logo assertions.
- `ruff`, `dart analyze`, `markdownlint`, `prettier` clean.

## Acceptance criteria (#1149)

- [x] Setting `KLANGK_PRODUCT_NAME=Acme Labs` updates browser tab title, `MaterialApp` title, and logo text — no rebuild.
- [x] Verification / reset / invitation emails use the configured name in subject and body.
- [x] Defaults to `Klangk` everywhere when unset — no behavior change for existing deployments.
- [x] `file:`/`cmd:` prefix resolution works (routed through `resolve_env_value`).
- [x] Documented in `docs/reference/environment.md` and `.env.example`.
- [x] `docs/deployment/customizing.md` describes product-name white-labeling as a runtime (no-rebuild) customization.
- [x] `/config` includes `product_name`; frontend falls back to `Klangk` when the field is absent.

author: matthewsuttles
body:
## Why

`main`'s `test` CI job has been red with **55 failures** (2 real production bugs, plus specs left stale by recent refactors — the `#356` LlmModelRegistry consolidation and the async HeartbeatJob rewrite). Every open PR inherits these failures, so nothing can go green. This gets `main` back to green.

## Production bugs

- **`ContextManager#context_window_for_model`** — the registry's generic `"ollama"` placeholder prefix-matches every local model tag and was shadowing the tag-specific `OLLAMA_MODEL_LIMITS`. `llama3.2` resolved to a 131072 context window instead of 8192, inflating the prune budget ~16×. Now consults the specific local table first, then the registry.
- **`ServiceResponse`** — added a `failure?` predicate to pair with the existing `.failure` constructor (specs and callers expect it; only `error?` existed).

## Specs realigned with current behavior

- `llm_model_registry_spec` — `described_class` was shadowed to `Model` inside the nested `describe`, so `.find` hit `Struct.find`. Resolve via the registry module explicitly.
- `cost_estimator_spec` — `RATES`/`DEFAULT_RATE` moved into `LlmModelRegistry`; assert via the registry.
- `anthropic_adapter_spec`, `model_router_spec` — reference registry constants instead of hardcoding superseded model IDs.
- `skill_version_spec` + factory — account for the `Skill` `after_create` version snapshot; guard the factory checksum against nil content.
- `relevance_scorer_spec` — context text now matches the literal trigger pattern.

## HeartbeatJob spec split (async refactor)

`HeartbeatJob` now dispatches to `ChatStreamJob.perform_later`; HeartbeatRun tracking, model/provider restore, memory overwrite, and broadcasting happen in `ChatStreamJob#finalize_heartbeat_session`. The 34-test spec still asserted the old synchronous path.

- `heartbeat_job_spec` — now covers dispatch, prompt building, session lifecycle, and model override-at-dispatch.
- `chat_stream_job_spec` — new coverage for `finalize_heartbeat_session` (HeartbeatRun, restore, memory, broadcast).

## Verification

- Full non-system suite: all previously-failing CI specs now pass. The only remaining local failures are the browser sidecar specs (`browser_executor*`), which need the `cache` Redis host and are green in CI.
- `rubocop -A` clean on changed files; `brakeman` 0 warnings.
