author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Turns on the wide-gamut working space (option W): the canonical 16-bit surface is now **ProPhoto** for sources that actually carry wide-gamut information (profiled CMYK), and the card/model/output boundary colour-manages **ProPhoto → sRGB**. P2b (space switch) and P3 (egress) ship together because switching the space without the egress would mis-colour every card output.

The loader now tags each surface with its *actual* space instead of forcing everything to `Srgb`:

```
cmyk_to_working(raw):
    if let Some(rgb16) = cmyk_to_prophoto16(raw):   # embedded CMYK ICC present
        WorkingImage::from_prophoto_rgb16(...)       # space = ProPhoto (16-bit, wide gamut kept)
    else:
        naive CMYK -> sRGB8 -> from_rgba8(Srgb)       # unchanged, byte-exact

load_rgba(...) = load_working(...).to_srgb_rgba8()
```

`to_srgb_rgba8` is the egress and branches on the tag:
- `ProPhoto` → moxcms `ProPhoto → sRGB` on RGB, alpha carried straight (never colour-managed).
- `Srgb` → **exact bit-narrow** (identical to `to_rgba8`).

So only genuinely wide-gamut sources pay the round-trip. Plain images and unprofiled/naive CMYK reach the cards **byte-for-byte**, which keeps the pinned cross-language naive CMYK contract intact (no test re-baselining was needed after all — the `乙` authorization to change it went unused because the space-tagging keeps the naive path off the ProPhoto round-trip). Profiled CMYK changes by a small ΔE vs the old direct `CMYK → sRGB`, now routed `CMYK → ProPhoto16 → sRGB`.

### Colour-management details
- New `cmyk_transform::cmyk_to_prophoto16` mirrors the existing sRGB ICC path (tetrahedral, high barycentric weight, Perceptual) but targets moxcms `new_pro_photo_rgb()` (gamma-1.8 D50) via `create_transform_16bit(Layout::Rgba, &prophoto, Layout::Rgb, ...)`. Returns `None` for unprofiled/invalid CMYK so the caller keeps the naive path.
- New `working_image` helpers: `srgb8_rgb_to_prophoto16` (widening ingest, for later RGB-source use), `prophoto16_rgb_to_srgb8` (egress), `WorkingImage::from_prophoto_rgb16`, and `WorkingImage::to_srgb_rgba8`.
- TRC stays gamma-encoded; linear-light remains deferred.

### Tests
- `working_image`: sRGB↔ProPhoto round-trip within ±3; ProPhoto white egresses to sRGB white with alpha narrowed straight; `Srgb`-tagged egress is byte-identical to the plain narrow.
- `cmyk_transform`: profiled CMYK reaches ProPhoto (structural white/black checks) and egresses within ±40 of the littleCMS sRGB reference; unprofiled/invalid CMYK returns `None`. The profiled test is gated on a system CMYK profile (skipped on runners without one), matching the existing ICC test.
- `studio_image`: existing loader tests updated to exercise `to_srgb_rgba8`; the unprofiled Adobe-CMYK fixture stays `Srgb` and byte-exact.

Note: local Rust build/test could not run in this environment (no MSVC linker; ffmpeg deps) — relying on CI as with the prior P1/P2 PRs.

### Docs
`docs/design/colour-pipeline.md` and `implementation-status.md` updated: P1–P3 marked landed; current-state section rewritten to describe the ProPhoto canonical + sRGB egress; P4 (manual 16-bit output) and P5 (Python parity) remain.

Follows #188 (P1 type) and #189 (P2 carrier plumbing).

## E16 PR-2 + PR-3 — quality-over-time history (read API, backfill CLI, UI)

Builds the read + surface half of E16 on top of the merged PR-1 snapshot store (#221). Answers Doug's June-24 *"how do I know if they were compliant in December? October?"* from the persisted aggregate, never a re-scan of the per-subject `outcomes`.

### PR-2 — backend
- **`GET /api/quality/history?measureId=&scopeLevel=&scopeId=&tenant=&from=&to=`** (`routes/quality.ts`) — bounded snapshot time-series read (period ASC). Requires `measureId` (400) to stay bounded at scale; validates `from`/`to` as inclusive `YYYY-MM` + the `scopeLevel` enum; authenticated read-only under the `GET /api/**` fallback (all roles). Wired in `worker.ts`.
- **`pnpm seed:quality-history [--months 12] [--as-of YYYY-MM]`** (`run/backfill-quality-history.ts` + `run/cli/`) — materializes **real evaluated** snapshots for past months, **superseding** the synthetic sine-wave `seed:trend-history` for the quality trend. Re-evaluates the live directory as-of each month's end (reuses the Simulate #197 anchoring); the generated 120k `mhn` scale tenant folds in via the bounded `aggregateScaleRun` (never per-subject rows) with its current, time-invariant distribution. Audited (`QUALITY_HISTORY_BACKFILLED`, before the upsert), idempotent + resumable at the month level, reversible (`DELETE FROM quality_snapshots`).
- **Scoping decision:** `programTrend` (the `/programs` overview cards) stays on live per-run aggregation as a safe fallback; the snapshot-backed trend lands at the presentation layer (below).

### PR-3 — frontend
- A **"Quality over time (source of truth)"** card on `/programs/[measureId]` — scope selector (All Systems / per WebChart system), as-of month picker, **"compliance on month M"** numerator/denominator KPI, and a snapshot-backed monthly area chart with a `ChartDataTable` sr-only accessible alternative (WCAG, per #218). Reads `GET /api/quality/history`; graceful empty state pointing at `seed:quality-history`.

### Invariants
- Descriptive only — counts what CQL already decided, never sets/overrides `Outcome Status` (ADR-008/ADR-021).
- Reconciles All = Σ tenants = Σ sites = Σ providers (reuses PR-1's pure `buildSnapshotRows`).
- No schema change (reuses PR-1's `quality_snapshots`); no new deps.

Dödar den eviga "Verifierar"/"Reparerar"-spinnern i buildern genom att konvergera de tva status-ytorna till en terminal kalla.

Spinnern (`useVersionStatus`) pollar `/version-status` som laste **bara** event-buss-projektionen. Den enda terminala stale-watchdogen (`STALE_VERIFICATION_TIMEOUT_MS`, ~route-budget) fanns **bara** pa `/readiness` och skrev **bara** DB `verification_state`. author: mezotv
body: ## What Removes `status` and `contentType` from `COMMA_SEPARATED_QUERY_PARAMS` in `src/notra-client.ts`, so multi-value post filters serialize as repeated query params (`status=draft&status=published`) instead of a comma-joined string (`status=draft,published`). ## Why The `list_posts` tool accepts `status`/`contentType` as arrays (comma-separated input is preprocessed into arrays in `src/post-filters.ts`). The client was then re-joining those arrays with commas for the query string. Per the OpenAPI spec (`https://api.usenotra.com/openapi.json`), `status` and `contentType` on `GET /v1/posts` are documented as single-value `string` enums — they are **not** comma-separated lists. Emitting `status=draft,published` sends a value the API does not parse as an enum. Repeating the param is the correct multi-value encoding here. `brandIdentityId` and `repositoryIds` are intentionally **kept** comma-joined — the spec explicitly documents `repositoryIds` as a comma-separated list (example `repo_123,repo_456`). ## Verification - `tsc --noEmit` passes. - Change is limited to the query-param serialization set; no behavior change for single-value filters. ## Not covered Does not address the separate `list_schedules` HTTP 500 (that's an upstream Notra API bug, unrelated to this file). --- ## Summary by cubic Serialize multi-value `status` and `contentType` post filters as repeated query params instead of comma-joined strings to match the OpenAPI spec and ensure GET `/v1/posts` parses them correctly. `brandIdentityId` and `repositoryIds` remain comma-separated as documented. Written for commit 8f66fa1fa76cd3a959a655bbd4274ee400a356c8. Summary will update on new commits.

author: silvath
body:
## Summary

Closes #661.

`d-for` only rendered correctly when it was the **last child** of its parent. When a loop
rendered, Drapo computed its "previously rendered items" as `Document.GetNextAll(elAnchor)`
— **every** sibling after the hidden template anchor — and then removed/diffed that whole
set. Any content after the loop (a second `d-for`, or static markup) was treated as the
loop's own output and destroyed/corrupted.

## Fix

Bound each loop to only the rows it actually rendered:

- Rendered clones are tagged in a `DrapoDocument` **owned-items registry** (a `WeakSet`,
  invisible to serialized HTML — so **no existing snapshot changes**).
- New `DrapoDocument.GetForRenderedItems(anchor)` returns only the contiguous run of
  owned siblings after the anchor, stopping at the first non-owned element (another loop's
  template or static content).
- The item-collection, viewport-reset, incremental, and empty-data rebuild paths in
  `DrapoControlFlow.ResolveControlFlowForInternal` now act only on the owned run.

No new author-facing attribute; fully backward compatible.

## Tests (DrapoPages render-comparison)

- **ForConsecutive** — two adjacent loops render independently (`A0..A2`, `B0..B2`).
- **ForTrailingStatic** — a loop followed by a static footer row; the footer is preserved.
- **ForConsecutiveMixed** — empty first loop + loop + static + loop (edge cases).

**Full suite: 347 passing, 0 failing.** The one `DiagnosticsImageTest` failure is
**pre-existing on `master`** and unrelated (that page has no `d-for`; it's a `d-sector`
snapshot-normalization mismatch) — verified by running it against a clean master build.
TSLint zero errors; `Drapo.sln` builds.

## Spec Kit artifacts

Full spec → plan → tasks under `specs/001-dfor-consecutive-siblings/` (spec, plan,
research, data-model, contracts, quickstart, tasks — all 24 tasks complete).

## Docs

- `doc/dfor.md` — new "Placement among siblings" section.
- `doc/architecture.md` — note on the owned-items registry under `DrapoControlFlow`.

author: kounelisagis
body:
Anchors for oriented boxes were taken from the axis-aligned envelope, so positions like `BOTTOM_CENTER` (the `PolygonZone` default) and the four corners (the `LineZone` default) could sit well off a rotated object. This skews zone and line counting, and shifts every anchor-based annotator.

`get_anchors_coordinates` now computes the anchor on the oriented rectangle when `xyxyxyxy` is present: corners map to corners, side anchors to side midpoints, center to the box center. Axis-aligned boxes are unchanged, and `CENTER_OF_MASS` still uses the mask.

Refs #2318

author: lakofsth
body:
## What

Two small, non-destructive quality-of-life additions to compose-mode:

### 1. Recall history for sent lines
A history (⟲) button on the compose bar keeps the recently **sent** lines in a small ring and lets you tap one to repopulate the field (without sending). Compose sends a line + submit blindly into the PTY; if it lands in a mode that discards it (a pager, a TUI selector, copy/transcript mode), the line is otherwise gone. The recall ring makes that recoverable.

- Most-recent first, capped at 20.
- **De-duplicated**: on send, any earlier identical entry is removed before appending, so the ring holds 20 *distinct* lines. Re-sending a recalled line just reorders it to the top rather than piling up duplicates that would evict good older lines.
- Opening the menu takes focus off the field (Android hides the soft keyboard); focus is restored on both select and cancel so the keyboard returns after the menu closes.

### 2. Preserve the unsent draft on close
Closing compose (✕) used to silently discard whatever was typed. Now the current field text is handed back on close, kept by the page, and restored when compose reopens — so closing (or getting closed) never loses a draft in progress.

## Notes

- Purely additive; no change to the send path or existing behavior.
- Validated on-device (Android): recall + tap-to-repopulate, keyboard returns after selecting, re-send dedupes (reorders, no duplicate), and close→reopen restores the draft.
- Touches the same `onSend` block as #101 (the discrete-Enter newline fix); if both land, the overlap is a trivial one-line merge.

## Contexto

Este PR adiciona um exemplo isolado de laboratorio SCADA para simular maquinas industriais recebendo dados em tempo real pelo simulador existente.

O objetivo e permitir avaliar uma arquitetura de fluxo visual para maquinas, sensores e estados operacionais sem interferir nas telas atuais do projeto.

## O que mudou

author: chenlinxi890-spec
body:
## Summary

Fixes a logic flaw in \MemoryParsingService._rule_based()\ where the ambiguity guard incorrectly blocked memory type classification when 3+ types matched with weak signals.

## Bug

The ambiguity guard condition \ est_total - second_total <= 1\ treated tied cumulative scores as ambiguous and returned \None\, forcing all memories to 'fact' fallback even when \TYPE_PRIORITY\ could deterministically resolve the classification.

**Bug case:** \'I dislike Vim and problems were found'\ matches:
- preference (dislike, score=3)
- error (problems, score=3)  
- fact (were, score=3)

Before: \None\ (guard blocks) → falls back to 'fact'
After: 'fact' (TYPE_PRIORITY tiebreaker resolves explicitly)

## Fix

Replace \nd (best_total - second_total) <= 1\ with \nd len(ranked) == 2\ in the ambiguity guard.

- **2 types tied with weak signals** → guard blocks (preserves original intent)
- **3+ types tied** → TYPE_PRIORITY tiebreaker resolves (no longer blocked)

## Changes

- \memanto/app/services/memory_parsing_service.py\: 1 line changed in ambiguity guard
- No new dependencies, no API changes, no breaking changes

## Testing

Verified:
1. Bug case now returns deterministic classification (not None)
2. All existing type detection still works (preference, instruction, decision, goal)
3. Two-way weak ties still blocked as intended

## Bounty

Closes #770 — Memanto Bug Challenge submission.

author: einsteindark-edgm
body:
## Problema

Origen: run `019f1b65` / sesión `wa_573125671604`. El cliente manda **varios mensajes seguidos** (una ráfaga) y el bot **solo procesa uno**. Dos causas raíz, confirmadas leyendo el código vivo:

1. **Race de arranque → signals perdidos.** `LoadOrStartSalesSession` arrancaba el workflow a mano (`get_handle → describe → start_workflow → signal`). Con 2+ inbounds concurrentes sobre un workflow inexistente, el 2º `start_workflow` chocaba con `WorkflowAlreadyStartedError` y su `signal` nunca corría → el mensaje **jamás llegaba al LLM** (que ve el turno SOLO por la vía del signal → `build_prompt`, no por el JSONL del dashboard).
2. **Sin conciencia de ráfaga.** Aun coalesciendo, el LLM no sabía que fueron varios mensajes → tendía a contestar uno.

## Solución (este PR)

- **Fase 0 — `signal_with_start` atómico** en el path Sales de `LoadOrStartSalesSession`. Arranca-si-no-existe **y** entrega el mensaje en un solo comando (`id_conflict_policy=USE_EXISTING`). Cero race, signals ordenados por Temporal. Precedente en repo: `eta_session` + `orchestration/dispatcher`.
- **`coalesce_inbox` + `InboxMsg` + nota de ráfaga** (`platform/workflow_helpers.py`). El workflow convierte la ráfaga a `InboxMsg` (seq = orden de llegada, determinista en replay), la coalescea en orden e inyecta al `plugin_context` una **nota determinista** que lista lo que el cliente escribió, para que el LLM responda al **hilo completo**. Detrás de `workflow.patched("burst-note-v1")` (replay-safe, R-DET / L-9). Preserva el manejo de handoff (L-12).

## Tooling — `hubara_agency/scripts/agent-test.sh`

Runner de tests **aislado y acotado** para agentes concurrentes (nace de un incidente de este mismo trabajo donde runs paralelos + un `pkill` global colgaron tests 50 min):
- Process group propio (`POSIX::setsid`) → cleanup **scoped** (`kill -- -$PGID`), **nunca `pkill` global**.
- **Timeout duro** (`perl alarm`) → resultado definitivo en ≤N s, jamás un cuelgue indefinido.
- Salida a **archivo** (inmune al proxy que vacía pipes) + `python -u` (unbuffered).
- venv del worktree directo (sin `uv run` → sin lock/sync que se cuelgue).

## Verificación (local, vía el script)

- `25 passed` — `test_coalesce_inbox` (5, incl. nota de ráfaga) + `test_coalesce_pending` (8) + `test_load_or_start_sales_session` (12, incl. **guard rojo** de la race de arranque).
- `7 passed` — suite completa `test_sales_workflow_debounce` (burst + 6 originales).
- `ruff --select F821` **limpio** — cazó un import borrado por el hook `ruff --fix` entre edits (habría sido `NameError` en la 1ª ráfaga real).
- `lint-imports` (R-DIP) verde.

## Alcance / siguientes incrementos

Este PR es el **núcleo del feature**. Lo que sigue (bandeja/watermark completos con `_acked_seq` + `CoverageRecord`, interrupción del turno en vuelo, reply-to/vistos) está diseñado en `.hubara/refinements/HU-burst-inbox-watermark/refinement.md` y va en PRs siguientes.

author: hurtener
body:
## R10-C — overflow-remediation ladder (rest of R10.11, HIGH · both)

Closes the second half of the opt-in `autofit` export flag. After the `Fill` pass, the export path renders, detects overflowing slides from the engine's LayoutWarnings, and applies a fixed deterministic ladder of pure IR rewrites to **only** the offending slides, re-rendering after each rung. Off (`Autofit=false`) is byte-identical.

### What changed
- **`render.Stats.LayoutWarnings`** — additive structured `[]LayoutWarning{SlideID,Node,Message}` mirroring the formatted `Warnings` 1:1, so remediation can act by slide without string-parsing. Existing `Warnings` consumers untouched.
- **`autofit.Remediate(doc, OverflowFunc)`** — a render-independent loop (the handler injects render+classify) applying a 2-rung ladder: (1) enable `AutoFit` on Hero/Heading/Stat, (2) step `Card.Size` down (lg→md→sm floor), via a pure copy-on-write node tree-walk (recurses two_column/grid/bento/card/card_section). Deterministic; caps at ladder length; never mutates input.
- **Export handler** shares one `AssetResolver` between the remediation probe renders and the final export, behind the `Autofit` flag.

### ⚠️ Scope — honest best-effort, NOT zero-overflow
The product IR exposes no lever that reduces a **vertical** stack overflow: `AutoFit` is a width-only shrink-to-one-line, `Card.Size` only trims size-driven padding, and the dominant leaf slot heights (Hero/Heading/Prose) are fixed and unreachable from the IR — while the engine already applies its own gap/body shrink *before* it warns. R10.11's strict "zero unresolved overflow warnings" acceptance needs an **engine `FitToRegion` knob** that shrinks content vertically and clears the warning (**engine gap filed**). Until then the ladder measurably improves overflowing slides (AutoFit prevents display-title clipping; card-shrink reclaims height) and the export never fails on residual overflow. This scope call was made explicitly with the maintainer.

### Tests
Ladder application / card-step / clean-no-op / purity / determinism / cap (fake `OverflowFunc`, engine-independent); render `LayoutWarnings` populated for an overflowing deck + empty for a clean one; export with `Autofit` on an overflowing deck yields a valid `.pptx`.

### Gate
gofmt · vet · build · `go test -race` · golangci-lint (0) · `dockyard generate` (idempotent) · `dockyard validate` · `dockyard test` (5/5) · mirror — all green.

author: kakumanu-harshitha
body:
## Summary
This PR hardens the `recentClusters` helper functions against corrupted `localStorage` data, browser storage exceptions, and type leakage, preventing application startup crashes.

## Related Issue
Fixes #6309 

## Root Cause
`getRecentClusters()` retrieves the `recent_clusters` key from `localStorage` and calls `JSON.parse` without a `try/catch`. If the data is corrupted, a `SyntaxError` is thrown on application startup, crashing the cluster-selection UI before the user can connect. Furthermore, the parsed output was forcefully cast `as string[]` without runtime validation; if the storage contained an array of objects, it would leak incorrect types and crash downstream. Finally, `setRecentCluster()` called `localStorage.setItem` without catching `QuotaExceededError`.

## Changes
- **`frontend/src/helpers/recentClusters.ts`:**
  - Wrapped `JSON.parse` in `getRecentClusters()` with a `try/catch`. On failure, logs a warning and returns `[]`.
  - Added strong runtime type validation (`recentClusters.every(item => typeof item === 'string')`) to prevent non-string elements from leaking past the `as string[]` cast.
  - Wrapped `localStorage.setItem` in `setRecentCluster()` with a `try/catch` to gracefully log errors if the quota is exceeded.
- **`frontend/src/helpers/recentClusters.test.ts`:**
  - Replaced the `toThrow(SyntaxError)` test with one that verifies it correctly catches the error, logs a warning, and returns `[]`.
  - Added a test to ensure it returns `[]` if the stored array contains non-string elements.
  - Added a test to verify `localStorage.setItem` throws are caught and logged.

## Steps to Test
1. Run `cd frontend && npx vitest run src/helpers/recentClusters.test.ts` to verify all 13 tests pass.
2. Open Headlamp, navigate to Local Storage in DevTools, and manually corrupt the `recent_clusters` key (e.g., set it to `{ broken JSON ]` or `[{"unexpected": "object"}]`).
3. Refresh the page. The app should load normally (ignoring the corrupted recent clusters) rather than crashing to a blank screen. 

## Verification
- [x] Linting and type checking (`npm run frontend:tsc`) pass.
- [x] 13/13 tests in `recentClusters.test.ts` pass.
- [x] Diff scope is minimal and targeted.

author: kiro-agent[bot]
body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @darko-mesaros :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro Web](https://kiro.dev/web/)</sub>

---
## Problem

Using an Anthropic Claude model (e.g. Opus) fails with:

> Model reached maximum token limit. This is an unrecoverable state that requires intervention.

Qwen works fine. This is a **model-configuration** issue, not a broken setup.

## Root cause

`agent.ts` created the model with only `modelId`:

```ts
new BedrockModel({ modelId: this.config.bedrockModelId });
```

In the Strands SDK's Bedrock provider, `maxTokens` is only sent to Bedrock **if explicitly configured** (`bedrock.js`):

```js
if (this._config.maxTokens !== undefined)
    inferenceConfig.maxTokens = this._config.maxTokens;
```

With it omitted, Bedrock applies its low per-model default output cap. Claude models hit that cap mid-response and return stop reason `maxTokens`, which the SDK turns into a fatal `MaxTokensError` (`model.js`). Qwen was unaffected because its default cap is higher. The new long-form system prompt makes the truncation far more likely to trigger.

## Fix

- Add optional `maxTokens` to `AppConfig`.
- Pass it through to `BedrockModel` in `agent.ts` (only when set, preserving prior behaviour if unset).
- Default to **8192** in `index.ts`, overridable via the `BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS` env var (validated: must be a positive finite number, else falls back to the default).
- Add a `maxtokens` knob to the `justfile` and document `BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS` in the README.

## Usage

```bash
BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS=16384 BEDROCK_MODEL_ID="<claude-model-id>" npm start
# or
just maxtokens="16384" model="<claude-model-id>" profile="personal" run
```

## Testing

- `npm run build` — clean.
- `npm test` — all 260 tests pass.
- Validated `just` recipes with `--dry-run`: `BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS` is injected (default `8192`, override respected).

## Notes

- Default of 8192 is a safe, generous cap for long articles; raise via env var if you want even longer output.
- Not yet exposed in the settings UI (only via env/config) — happy to add a field there as a follow-up if you'd like runtime control.
- Independent of the system-prompt PR, though the two pair well: longer answers + a high-enough cap.

The Grade dropdown's grades list only has names (no id field), but the select bound to grade_id and used g.id as each option's value. With no id, React drops the value attribute so the browser falls back to the option's text, sending the grade's *name* as grade_id. That string then hit an unguarded CAST(... Switch the Grade filter to grade_name, which already has a working text match on the backend. Also harden _coerce_value and the season/grade multi-select parser so a malformed UUID drops that filter instead of throwing, as defence in depth for any other caller.

author: eth-interchained
body:
## Summary
Two fast-follow commits on top of the merged boot-logic refactor (#73), both compiled and validated live against real production data (a ~7.9M-object datastore):

1. **`store.rs`**: the cold-scan wait loop had a real bug hiding behind a missing progress bar — it capped at 300s and then printed "scan complete" unconditionally, whether the scan had actually finished or not. On a large datastore the scan legitimately runs past 300s, so `Store::open()` returned with the index still cold, and `tip_header()` correctly came back `None` — the node fell back to a full genesis resync. Fixed by waiting on the real `scan_status().scan_complete` signal with no artificial timeout, and added a live progress display (holographic sweep, spinner, live object count, indexing rate, elapsed time) in its place.

2. **`Cargo.toml`**: bumps the `nedb-engine` workspace pin `v2.5.44 → v2.5.45`, which fixes a companion bug found by watching the above UI against live data: `scan_status().indexed_count` stayed at exactly `0` for the entire slow disk-read phase of a cold scan, because the engine only populated its seq index in a second pass *after* that phase finished. On a multi-million-object store, that meant `0 objects indexed` for 100+ seconds straight before the fix.

## Validated
Compiled clean on both commits (12.19s incremental, then 56.80s pulling in v2.5.45). Run live against the real ~7.9M-object datastore this was diagnosed against — progress now climbs in real time during the scan instead of sitting at zero.

## Details
See the individual commit messages for the full root-cause writeups (both were diagnosed live from pasted boot logs, not guessed at).

author: depre-dev
body:
## What
Two fail-closed **mainnet startup guards** from the solo-auditor Medium findings (both Claude-owned).

## B-02 — mainnet must sign on-chain via KMS
`assertMainnetSignerPosture`: on mainnet (chain `420420419`) with the gateway live, `SIGNER_BACKEND` must be `kms`. A `local` signer means a raw `SIGNER_PRIVATE_KEY` in the process env signs real value-bearing settlement txs — exactly the hot-key exposure KMS exists to remove. Fail-closed, **no override**. No-op off mainnet or when the gateway is disabled (nothing signs).

## D-02 — verify the RPC serves the configured chain
`assertChainIdMatchesRpc`: when the gateway is live and `AUTH_CHAIN_ID` is set, fetch the RPC's `eth_chainId` and **fail closed on a confirmed mismatch** (backend configured for one chain, RPC serving another → wrong contracts, wrong SIWE domain, wrong settlement). If the RPC is *unreachable* at boot it **warns and continues** — that's a liveness concern the gateway's own health handles, and a chain-id *check* shouldn't make the process un-bootable during a transient RPC blip (relevant given how flaky the testnet RPC has been).

## Where
- New `mcp-server/src/services/startup-guards.js` (isolated, dependency-light) + `startup-guards.test.js` (10 tests).
- Wired into `bootstrap.js` next to the existing `assertSafeAuthBrokeringPosture` — sync `initStep` for B-02, async try/catch (mirroring the KMS-credential check) for D-02.

## Test
`node --test mcp-server/src/services/startup-guards.test.js` → **10/10** (both fail-closed paths + every no-op / warn path).

Closes **B-02** and **D-02** in `docs/MAINNET_AUDIT_REMEDIATION.md`.

## Changelist

In this PR, I have optimised the **Fibonacci** and **Making Change** recursive algorithms by implementing manual memoisation. These changes transform functions that previously had exponential time complexity into efficient, linear-time operations.

A comprehensive breakdown of the logic, state-tracking strategies, and specific code changes is provided in the **`CHANGES_MADE.md`** file included in this PR.

#### Key Improvements

**1. Fibonacci Sequence**
- **Performance**: Reduced time complexity from **$O(2^n)$** to **$O(term\_index)$**.
- **Caching**: Implemented a dictionary-based `memo` to store and reuse results of previously calculated terms.
- **Readability**: Renamed the parameter to `term_index` and added type hints to clarify the function's purpose.

**2. Making Change Algorithm**
- **State Tracking**: Developed a unique cache key using a **Tuple** `(total, len(coins))` to track sub-problems based on both the remaining amount and available denominations.
- **Structural Refactor**: Introduced a helper/wrapper pattern. The wrapper ensures the cache is cleared between different calls, while the helper manages the recursive logic.
- **Legacy Integrity**: Maintained the original variable names from the legacy code to ensure continuity while improving underlying performance.

#### Testing Done
All implementations were verified against the provided test suites:
- **Fibonacci**: Confirmed that `fibonacci(200)` now returns results instantly.
- **Making Change**: Verified that `test_9176` (which produces a result in the quadrillions) completes in milliseconds, demonstrating the efficiency of the cache.

#### Learning Reflection
These tasks served as a practical application of the **Space-vs-Time trade-off**. By "spending" memory (the `memo` dictionaries), I successfully "saved" massive amounts of CPU time, allowing the algorithms to scale to much larger inputs.

author: aaronmullan
body:
## Root cause

Sentry feedback REACT-NATIVE-11 ("Strange naming on Lizzy's birthday"). Confirmed against production data: recipient **Lizzy** has an occasion stored with `occasion_type = "lizzy_birthday"` — the recipient's name is baked into the type. AI occasion extraction occasionally does this (it slugifies a free-text name like "Lizzy's Birthday" into the stored type).

Occasion titles are composed as `` `${possessive(name)} ${formatOccasionType(occasion_type)}` ``. With the name already in the type, that doubles it:

- Home hero: "Lizzy's lizzy birthday is coming up."
- Next Up / On the Horizon cards + Moments calendar: "Lizzy's" / "Lizzy Birthday"

A DB-wide scan found exactly **one** such row, so this is a rare extraction glitch, not systemic.

## Change

Added `stripRecipientName(occasionType, name)` in `utils/home-occasions.ts` that drops a leading copy of the recipient's first name (with optional possessive `s`/`'s`) from the raw `occasion_type` **only when a separator follows** — so legitimate holidays that merely start with the same letters (`samhain` for "Sam", `christmas` for "Chris") are left intact. Applied it at every site that composes a title from name + type:

- `components/home/HomeHeroCard.tsx` (both day-of and coming-up copy)
- `components/home/NextUpCarousel.tsx`
- `components/home/OnTheHorizonGrid.tsx`
- `app/(tabs)/calendar.tsx`

This is a display-time fix, so it heals the existing stored row and any future extraction glitches everywhere titles render, without a data migration.

## Proposed data backfill (needs sign-off — not run)

The display fix resolves the user-visible bug, but the stored value is still malformed (gift-suggestion prompts etc. would read `lizzy_birthday`). Recommend normalizing the single row after review:

```sql
update occasions set occasion_type = 'birthday'
where id = '51afad57-90e0-4350-84e5-3c0b79016b0e';  -- occasion_type was 'lizzy_birthday'
```

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only)
- Unit-checked the strip against real cases: `lizzy_birthday`+Lizzy → `birthday`; `christmas`+Chris → `christmas`; `samhain`+Sam → `samhain`; normal types unchanged.

- **Fails closed:** if an outsider couldn't reproduce our verdict from the live site, the deploy isn't done. Because `GITHUB_SHA` is set in the deploy job, the verifier's reconciliation also confirms the live artifacts carry *this* deploy's commit (freshness), a strict superset of the external-party check.

## Verified
- Workflow YAML parses; step ordering confirmed: `Invalidate CloudFront Cache` → `External verifier smoke test` → `Run Post-Deployment Compliance Check`.
- The verifier itself was proven end-to-end against the live site in #203 (`RESULT: PASS`); `verify-published.sh` is tracked `100755` and invoked via `bash` (mode-independent).
- Tools (`cosign`, `jq`, `python3`, `curl`) are all present in the deploy job.

## Couldn't verify locally
- The step exercises AWS (`cloudfront wait`) + the live invalidation, so it only truly runs in the deploy job. I'll watch the deploy on merge and confirm the smoke step goes green (and that the invalidation-wait keeps it deterministic). Per the #195 lesson, this is the honest residual — the verifier logic is proven live, the CI wiring is proven on the first deploy.

author: ken-ci[bot]
body:
## What changed

Implements the minimal module and import system specified earlier: named modules, all four import forms, private-by-default visibility with an explicit `pub` to export, and abstract export (exposing a name whose concrete implementation is hidden from importers). A module is expanded and flattened into the same declarations the kernel has always understood before anything reaches the kernel-facing pipeline, so nothing about modules is a new kernel concept. Abstract export reuses the existing mechanism for an opaque, kernel-checked constant rather than introducing anything new.

## Why

This turns the previously spec-only module system into a real, usable feature in the elaborator, letting Ken programs actually be organized across modules with real visibility enforcement rather than only having the design written down. Keeping it a pure front-end transformation — expand modules, then feed the kernel exactly what it already expects — means the feature adds real surface convenience without adding any new kernel machinery or any new item to the trusted set.

## How it's verified

Independently reviewed for soundness by inspecting the actual generated output, not just running the tests: confirmed the flattened output is identical, item for item, to what the kernel would see without modules at all, and confirmed that "abstract export" really is the pre-existing opaque-constant mechanism rather than a new, unaudited concept. A real defect was caught and fixed mid-review — a top-level exported type outside any module was silently having its constructor stripped with no error — and the fix was independently re-verified (the new regression test fails on the pre-fix commit and passes on the fixed one). Full elaborator, interpreter, kernel, and CLI test suites green throughout. CI (build, conformance, clean-room, path-guard) green before merge.

Fixes two confirmed P1 findings from the 2026-07-01 audit.

## GO-CP-1: body-wide sources stamped with the crawl job's country
IAC/ECCAA/BAGAIA/BEA listings are body-wide, but staged docs inherited the job's country_id and whichever country's job ran first claimed every record (live corruption: Belarus EW-307SL and Kazakh UP-MI872 events recorded as RU).

## GO-CP-3: transient infra failures burned the 3-attempt budget
A 3-day LLM-tunnel outage permanently retired fresh IAC docs ("dial tcp ... connection refused" ×3). Now OCR/LLM connection-level errors (errors.As through wrapping: *net.OpError / net.Error) skip RecordFailure and abort the pass with a typed InfraAbortError (distinct log + non-zero exit for the notification layer). New `reset-failed --db --store --error-like` subcommand for operator recovery. Note: LLM timeouts are also classified as infra (no attempt burn) — acceptable given MAX_INPUT caps prompt size, and reset-failed covers edge cases.

author: venosta-web
body:
Closes #406.

## Problem

Multiple `growspace-manager` cards on one dashboard shared plant selection and edit mode: `selectedPlants$`/`isEditMode$` lived as module-level atoms in `slices/ui`, and each per-card `GrowspaceUIStore` merely aliased them. Selecting plants or toggling edit mode on one card affected every other card on the page.

## Fix

Mirrors the per-card `$viewMode` pattern from #409.

- **`GrowspaceUIStore`** now owns its own `$isEditMode` + `$selectedPlants` atoms. The mutation logic (toggle / selectAll / clear / deselect, and `setEditMode` clearing selection + cancelling transplant on exit) lives in the store methods; `$cardViewState` reads the per-instance atoms.
- **Batch dialog openers** (`slices/ui/dialogs.ts`) now take `selectedIds: string[]`; new `store.ui.openBatch{Watering,Training,Clone,PrintLabels}Dialog()` snapshot *this card's* selection into the payload.
- **`selectAllPlantsInSelectedDevice()`** moved to `GrowspaceStore`, reading the per-card `grid.$selectedDevice`/`$activeDevices` (also fixes a latent stale module-device read).
- **`lib/keyboard-navigation.ts`** threaded with the card `store` — `handleKeyboardNavigation(key, store)` / `deleteSelectedPlants(store)` — so Delete/Escape/selection act on the card that has focus. Keyboard *focus* stays page-global (out of scope, tracked by #408).
- **Writers rerouted** through the per-card store: grid-cell toggle, both cards' select-all/clear/water/training/print/clone/delete handlers, dialog-host clear-on-close/deselect.
- Module-level `isEditMode$`/`selectedPlants$` + mutators kept and `@deprecated` for the slice's own unit tests, exactly as `viewMode$` was.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Each card instance owns its own selection set and edit-mode flag; one card no longer changes another on the same dashboard
- [x] All selection/edit-mode writers go through the per-card store, not the module-level slice functions
- [x] `$cardViewState` reflects the per-instance selection/edit values
- [x] Regression test: two `GrowspaceStore` instances mutate selection/edit mode independently
- [x] lint, test, and build pass

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors
- `npm test`: 2794 passed, 0 failed
- `npm run build`: passes

Also verified via grep that no production code still reads the module-level selection atoms or the module `cardViewState$`/`isCompactView$` computeds.

author: vsndrg
body:
## Проблема

Instagram Reels перестали скачиваться — на любую ссылку бот отвечает «Что-то пошло не так. Оригинал.».

**Причина:** Instagram больше не отдаёт медиа неавторизованным запросам и возвращает `empty media response`. yt-dlp падает с ошибкой, которая ловится в `handlers.py` и превращается в общее сообщение об ошибке. Воспроизведено и на закреплённой версии yt-dlp `2025.04.30`, и на свежей `2026.06.09` — обновление yt-dlp не помогает, нужны cookies залогиненного аккаунта.

## Решение

- `api/yt_dlp_client.py` — добавлена опция `cookiefile`, пробрасывается в yt-dlp.
- `api/instagram.py` — путь к `cookies.txt` читается из переменной окружения `INSTAGRAM_COOKIES`.
- `README.md` — инструкция по экспорту cookies и настройке переменной.
- `.gitignore` — `cookies.txt` добавлен, чтобы не закоммитить сессию.

Если `INSTAGRAM_COOKIES` не задана — поведение не меняется (TikTok/YouTube работают, Reels требуют cookies).

## Что нужно сделать на сервере после мёржа

1. Экспортировать `cookies.txt` из браузера с залогиненным (лучше одноразовым) аккаунтом Instagram.
2. Положить файл на сервер и добавить в `.env`: `INSTAGRAM_COOKIES=/путь/к/cookies.txt`.
3. Перезапустить бота.

⚠️ Instagram может ограничивать/банить аккаунт за автоматические запросы — лучше отдельный аккаунт, cookies иногда придётся обновлять.

author: mooknop
body:
Final code slice of the spellshape-automation epic (#1001). Automates **Sicken Spell** (Scepter of Sickening): a chained spell resolved by a **basic Fortitude save** applies *sickened 1* on a failed save, *sickened 2* on a critical failure — whether or not the spell deals damage.

## What's here

**1. Basic-save resolution (global fix)**
`mapSpellDefense` now strips a leading `"basic "` prefix, so spells authored as `"basic Fortitude"` / `"basic Reflex"` / etc. resolve to `target-save` instead of falling through to `mode: 'none'`. This was a **latent gap**: ~22 basic-save spells in the seed generated *no save request at all* on cast. New `isBasicDefense()` reports the basic-ness so save requests carry the correct `basic` flag (which drives `computeSaveDamage`'s halve-on-success / double-on-crit-fail). Wired into both save paths:
- `ChainedSpellSection` (chained spellshape casts)
- `UseAbilityModal` (direct casts)

**2. Conditional rider injection**
`ChainedSpellSection` gains:
- a `basic-fortitude-save` picker filter (scopes the chained-spell list to valid Sicken targets)
- `chain.injectRiders` support — a spellshape's authored condition riders merge into the chained save profile. A profile *shell* is built even for no-damage spells, since Sicken applies "whether or not the spell deals damage".

The degree-scoped riders serialize into `getResults`' damage payload, so the GM `RequestedSaves` UI logs `-> Failure . sickened 1` / `-> Critical Failure . sickened 2` through the **existing** condition-rider machinery — no new GM-side code.

## Chosen scope
The basic-save resolver fix is intentionally **global** (agreed up front): it fixes the latent gap for direct casts too, not just the chain flow. Larger blast radius, but correct and consistent.

## Tests
- `rollResolution` — `mapSpellDefense` basic-prefix stripping, `isBasicDefense`, basic-Fort spell -> target-save.
- `ChainedSpellSection` — `basic-fortitude-save` filter, degree-scoped rider serialization, no-damage-spell rider carry.
- Fixed 4 `rollResolution` vi.mock factories to preserve the new exports (`importActual` spread) — the known new-export mock gotcha.
- Full suite green: **6131 tests / 421 files**, lint clean.

Content (the scepter's `chain` block) ships in a companion `content` PR.

Part of #1001 (Slice 4 — the last slice).

body:
## O que

`jana:distill-module-truth --all --dry-run` (pré-condição do cron do Kernel, P11 KL-E3) **crashou na 1ª execução real** no CT100: `Undefined constant "GLOB_BRACE"` em `scanAudits()`.

- `GLOB_BRACE` é extensão **glibc** — indefinida em **musl/Alpine** (containers CT100). Referenciar a constante lança `Error` e derruba o comando inteiro antes de qualquer módulo.
- O CI (ubuntu/glibc) nunca pegaria — exatamente o padrão "ILUSÓRIO: parece feito, nunca rodou" que a [avaliação adversarial 2026-07-01](https://github.com/wagnerra23/oimpresso.com/blob/main/memory/sessions/2026-07-01-sdd-avaliacao-adversarial.md) deu 30/100 pro E3.
- Precedente catalogado: mesmo bug no Module Grade v4 (`ScopedScorecardEvaluator::globBrace`, triage Q2 2026-06-13).

## Fix

Globs separados sem brace: `AUDIT*.md` já cobre `AUDITORIA*` + `CAPTERRA*.md` em glob próprio. Bônus: elimina o double-match do brace (AUDIT* e AUDITORIA* casavam o mesmo arquivo → evento de auditoria duplicado na proveniência).

## Evidência (R1 — rodado no lugar canônico, CT100 musl)

Pest por path direto no container `oimpresso-staging` (CT100):

```
Tests:    6 passed (17 assertions)
Duration: 3.24s
```

Antes do fix, o MESMO comando crashava com `Undefined constant GLOB_BRACE` (log `/root/p11-e3/dryrun-20260701.log` no CT100). Teste de regressão novo cobre a coleta AUDIT/CAPTERRA (1 linha de proveniência por arquivo).

Nota: `php artisan test --filter=...` no staging esbarra num conflito de `uses()` pré-existente (`tests/Feature/Support/SuporteConcederCommandTest.php` × `tests/Pest.php:5`) — não relacionado a este diff; rodei por path direto.

author: michael-denyer
body:
The Claude Code desktop app passes every enabled plugin to the CLI as a session-only `--plugin-dir`, which strips marketplace identity (`pstack@inline`). The cross-marketplace dependency on `plugin-dev@claude-plugins-official` can never resolve in that mode, and the loader disables the entire plugin with `dependency-unsatisfied` — pstack loaded in the CLI and VS Code but silently vanished from desktop-app sessions.

`optional: true` on a dependency entry passes `claude plugin validate` but is not honored by the loader (tested on 2.1.197), so the dependency is demoted to documentation: README > Dependencies now carries the manual `plugin-dev` install steps. `marketplace.json` drops the matching `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn`.

Verified by spawning the desktop bundle's binary with `--plugin-dir plugins/pstack`: before, `Found 1 plugins (0 enabled, 1 disabled)` with `dependency-unsatisfied`; after, `1 enabled`, 44 skills and the poteto-agent load.

Bump 0.9.2 -> 0.9.3.

author: stevensacks
body:
## What

Closes the Class-9 (distribution-boundary) gap the health audit graded "A": the `workflow-denylist` leak-check in `.gaia/release-scrub.yml` is line-based regex and matched only the block-list inverted form (`- "!*.md"`) and the `paths-ignore:` key. An inverted entry smuggled into an **inline flow array** (`paths: ["src/**", "!*.md"]`) carries the same denylist fail-quiet semantics but slipped past the pattern.

## Change

- **`.gaia/release-scrub.yml`** — add a quote-anchored third alternation (`\[[^\]]*['"]!`) to the `workflow-denylist` pattern so the inline flow-array form is flagged, keeping block-list handling intact. The quote anchor prevents a stray `[!` in a run-step string from false-positiving. Verified zero matches against the current workflows (all allowlist form).
- **`.gaia/cli/src/release/scrub.test.ts`** — regression tests: inline-array hit, block-list/`paths-ignore` hit, and a pure-allowlist FP guard.
- **`.gaia/cli/health/taxonomy.md`** — update the accepted-limitation note to reflect the closed gap.

No `scrub.ts` change (the check is entirely config-driven via the generic `runLeakCheck` line matcher), so **no CLI rebundle** — the YAML is read from disk at runtime, never compiled into the binary.

author: dkuratowski
body:
The `deploy-to-cloudflare` workflow failed at **startup** on every run (feat branches, `development`, and the `stable/staging` promotion) — no jobs ran.

**Cause:** the `worker` job used `matrix.env` in its **job-level `if:`**, but `matrix` isn't an available context in a job-level `if` (only `github`, `needs`, `vars`, `inputs`). GitHub rejects the workflow ("Unrecognized named-value: 'matrix'").

**Fix:** each trigger maps to exactly one environment, so the matrix was unnecessary. Dropped it and derive the environment from the branch:
`production` on a push to `stable/production`, otherwise `staging` (a `stable/staging` push, or a PR plan-only review gate). README CI section updated to match.

After this lands and is promoted to `stable/staging`, the staging worker deploy will actually run.

author: jhacarreiro
body:
## Summary

This PR makes explicit Antigravity (`agy`) model pins validate against the live Antigravity CLI catalog instead of Octopus' generic shell-token model validator.

The current system has a fragile gap:

- Octopus exposes `OCTOPUS_AGY_MODEL` as the control for Antigravity model selection.
- Real `agy models` labels include spaces and parentheses, for example `Gemini 3.5 Flash (Low)`.
- The generic `validate_model_name` rejects whitespace and parentheses by design, so a valid Antigravity model label is rejected before it reaches the `agy` CLI.
- The only reliable workaround is to avoid `OCTOPUS_AGY_MODEL` and let the account-level Antigravity default decide the model.
- That fallback is operationally weak: changing the model in the Antigravity UI/TUI can silently affect every Octopus run without a config diff, run log pin, or reproducible model declaration.
- Antigravity's model list is service-owned and can change independently of Octopus releases, so hardcoding aliases in Octopus would become stale quickly.

This PR uses the opportunity to make Antigravity model selection explicit and dynamic: if `OCTOPUS_AGY_MODEL` is set for provider `agy`, Octopus validates it by exact membership in `agy models`.

## Changes

- Adds `validate_agy_model_name()` to `scripts/lib/model-resolver.sh`.
  - Accepts `default` and `agy/default` without calling the CLI.
  - For explicit pins, calls `agy models` and requires an exact label match.
  - Keeps the generic strict shell-token validator for all other providers.
- Updates resolver env override handling so `OCTOPUS_AGY_MODEL='Gemini 3.5 Flash (Low)'` can resolve for `agy`.
- Updates `scripts/helpers/agy-exec.sh` so both `default` and `agy/default` mean "do not pass `--model`".
- Adds a focused unit test covering:
  - exact `agy models` label acceptance;
  - generic validator remaining strict;
  - invalid `agy` labels rejected;
  - resolver returning explicit labels with spaces/parentheses;
  - helper not passing `--model` for `agy/default`;
  - helper passing explicit labels as a single `--model` argument.
- Updates docs/help text to describe `OCTOPUS_AGY_MODEL` as `default`, `agy/default`, or an exact label from `agy models`.

## Validation

Passed:

```text
git diff --check
bash -n scripts/lib/model-resolver.sh scripts/helpers/agy-exec.sh scripts/helpers/octo-model-config.sh tests/unit/test-agy-provider.sh
bash tests/unit/test-agy-provider.sh
bash tests/test-resolve-model.sh
bash tests/test-model-config-simple.sh
bash tests/smoke/test-syntax.sh
```

Also validated with a live authenticated `agy` CLI without generation:

```text
OCTOPUS_AGY_MODEL="Gemini 3.5 Flash (Low)" resolve_octopus_model agy agy tangle decomposer
→ Gemini 3.5 Flash (Low)
```

Noted but not caused by this patch:

```text
bash tests/test-model-config-v849.sh
→ failed in existing model-catalog/probe-ranking expectations unrelated to agy dynamic validation.
```

body:
Lands reliability Item C (drift-parity tests): converts two "documented as intentional, unproven" sync surfaces into test-enforced contracts. Test-only; zero production-code changes (+458 lines). ## 1. Shared Rust<->TS length-unit-scale golden The geometry length-unit scale is genuinely computed twice: Rust `extract_length_unit_scale` (`rust/core/src/units.rs`, drives geometry scaling via the prepass) and TS `extractLengthUnitScale` (`packages/parser/src/unit-extractor.ts`, used by the columnar parser, authoring, MCP, export). Both are now pinned to ONE fixture, `rust/core/tests/fixtures/unit_scale_vectors.json` (the `ifc_string_parity` pattern), so they cannot drift: - `rust/core/tests/unit_scale_parity.rs` — also guards that the streaming pre-pass sibling `try_extract_length_unit_scale` never contradicts the full extractor (it may defer on conversion-based units). - `packages/parser/src/unit-scale.parity.test.ts` — same vectors via relative path, `describe.skipIf` outside the monorepo. 8 vectors: SI MILLI/base/CENTI, conversion-based FOOT/INCH by name, a custom conversion unit resolved through `IfcMeasureWithUnit` with a MILLI component (the most drift-prone path), late-`IfcProject` ordering, and default-when-missing. **All 8 agree Rust vs TS today** — the PR pins that, it did not have to fix anything. Scoping note: `plane_angle_to_radians` is intentionally NOT in the golden — no TS counterpart exists (TS consumes the Rust prepass value). The TS georef resolvers compute a different quantity (`IfcProjectedCRS.MapUnit` scale) and are out of scope here. ## 2. Rust site-local rotation golden (previously untested path) No TS code re-derives the site transform (all consumers read Rust mesh output; the `buildingRotation` scalar is Rust-computed and camera-only), so this is a Rust-only golden rather than a fake cross-language test. The non-identity rotation path in `processor/site_local.rs::convert_mesh_to_site_local` had **zero test coverage** — every existing fixture uses identity rotation. `rust/processing/tests/site_rotation.rs` (inline synthetic IFC, no external fixtures): - 30-degree yaw + (10,20,0) translation: asserts the `site_local` tier is selected, `origin_shift` = site translation, `site_transform` carries the actual cos30/sin30 entries (guards against the fixture silently degrading to identity), every vertex (`origin + position`) matches hand-computed inverse-rotated corners (eps 1e-5), and normals are unit-length AND axis-aligned in the site frame (catches a missed normal rotation independently). - Translated-only site (identity-rotation fast-out) and fully-identity site (`raw_ifc` passthrough) as controls. Test strength was verified by mutation: stubbing `convert_mesh_to_site_local` to a no-op fails the rotated case and only that case. ## Verification - `cargo test -p ifc-lite-core --test unit_scale_parity` — 1 passed - `cargo test -p ifc-lite-processing --test site_rotation` — 3 passed - `pnpm --filter @ifc-lite/parser test unit-scale.parity` — 9 passed (full parser suite: 210 tests green) - All re-run independently after implementation review. No changeset: test-only (no published-package source changes).

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge with minimal risk. The PR is test-only and the added fixtures/tests match the existing Rust and TypeScript code paths reviewed. No files require special attention.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - I ran the unit-scale parity checks and observed an initial failure due to missing parity files and unbuilt workspace dependencies. - After running pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and building @ifc-lite/data/@ifc-lite/encoding, the unit-scale parity checks passed with Rust exit 0 and TS parity reporting 1 file / 9 tests. - I reviewed the site-rotation golden pre-run state, which showed the base worktree command, base commit, TEST\_FILE\_PRESENT: no, and an exit code 1 caused by a nightly cargo component issue before cargo could report the absent integration test target. - After the head run, the site-rotation golden tests completed successfully: running 3 tests, all three tests ok, final test result: ok, and EXIT\_CODE: 0. - Source inspection reveals the changed test file is tied to process\_geometry and includes the rotated, translated-only, identity, transform, vertex, and normal assertions. author: colocarletti
body:
Description:
Moves the LogUp auxiliary trace build (Round 1) from the CPU to the GPU, and keeps the data on the GPU instead of copying it back and forth.

What changed:
- The aux trace columns are now built on the GPU and stay there. The aux LDE reads them in place, so there's no download + re-upload.
- The aux build reuses the main trace that's already on the GPU (from the main LDE) instead of uploading it again.

Result (ethrex 5-tx, RTX 5090): aux build drops from ~1.74s to ~1.33s. The proof is byte-for-byte identical to the CPU version and all tests pass.

Note: this is a building block. On its own the win is small, because the stages around it (trace generation, constraint evaluation) are still on the CPU and force data across the bus. The bigger speedup comes when those move to the GPU too and the whole chain stays on the device — this PR adds the plumbing (resident aux trace, main-trace reuse, device-input LDE) they build on.

Known limit: preprocessed tables still upload their main trace, since they have no GPU copy to reuse.

author: skialpine
body:
## Summary

Follow-up work on the crash in #1408 (SIGABRT in `BatteryManager::readPlatformBatteryPercent()` via JNI). Two parts:

### 1. Crash reports now capture the ART abort message (the real diagnostic gap)

Re-analysis of the #1408 backtrace: the abort fires from a `LOG(FATAL)` **inside** `art::JavaVMExt::AddGlobalRef` (frame 7, with `LogMessage::~LogMessage` → `Runtime::Abort` above it). The only FATAL path in that function is **global reference table overflow** (max=51200). JNI global refs are VM-level, not Activity-level — Activity teardown cannot make `AddGlobalRef` abort, so the initial "JNI during suspend teardown" theory doesn't hold.

The numbers point at a slow global-ref leak over the 12.3 h session: the battery poll's ~8 refs/cycle are released properly (≤6k even if fully leaked), while the screensaver logged **397 video transitions**, each destroying/recreating the MediaCodec-backed MediaPlayer — ~125 leaked refs per cycle would land exactly at the 51,200 cap. The battery poll was just the allocation that hit the full table; the suspend timing was coincidental.

We can't verify this from the existing report because ART writes the FATAL reason **and a ref-table dump naming the dominant class** to logd before raising SIGABRT — and our crash reports never captured it. Now the Android signal handler appends `logcat -d -t 200 --pid=<us>` to `crash.log` (fork + execl; the child only calls dup2/execl; bounded 3 s wait; apps can always read their own logs). `crash.log` flows verbatim into the auto-reported issue's "Crash Log" section, so **the next occurrence of this crash will name its own cause**, including the leaking class.

### 2. BatteryManager suspend gate (kept, reframed as hygiene)

`BatteryManager`'s 60 s poll timer isn't lifecycle-aware, so it kept firing JNI battery reads after `Qt::ApplicationSuspended`. There's nothing useful to poll then: `ensureChargerOn()` has already forced the DE1 USB port ON (and the DE1's 10-min auto-enable keeps it there), and resume re-runs `checkBattery()` immediately. New `setAppActive()` gate, cleared first thing on suspend, restored on resume. This removes the suspended-poll trigger seen in #1408 but is **not** claimed to fix the underlying abort — comments corrected accordingly.

## Notes for review

- Not reproducible locally (unknown reporter, older release v1.7.6), hence the emphasis on self-diagnosing reports.
- `fork()` in a signal handler isn't strictly async-signal-safe, but the child does only AS-safe calls, and the existing handler already uses stdio/demangling/malloc — this doesn't lower the bar.
- The logcat section goes only into `crash.log`, not the `debug.log` copy (whose tail is submitted separately) — no duplication.
- New code is all `#ifdef Q_OS_ANDROID`; macOS build verifies nothing of it → needs a CI Android test build before merge.

## Test plan

- [x] Builds clean via Qt Creator (0 errors, 0 warnings)
- [ ] CI Android test build (`android-release.yml`, no upload)
- [ ] Next auto-reported Android SIGABRT should include the "System log tail" section with ART's abort message

Related to #1408 (deliberately not "Fixes" — the suspected global-ref leak is still at large; the next report will confirm or refute it)

author: randbrown
body:
Extends the chart-fallback ladder with tier 3: web search for shared Nashville Number charts in the wild (Drive/Dropbox links from community collections), plus tier 4 to draft a real chart doc from scraped chord data instead of a blank template.

## Key changes

**Worker (`workers/setlist-sync/index.js`)**
- Added two new routes:
  - `GET /web/chart-search?title=&artist=` — web-searches for shared chart files (NNS collections on Drive/Dropbox), verifies Drive hits via the API, walks shared folders with bounded recursion, and returns candidates ranked by match score
  - `GET /web/chart-data?title=&artist=` — finds Ultimate Guitar chord sheets, parses sections + chords, converts to Nashville numbers (key from source or inferred from chords), returns structured data for chart drafting
- Refactored `handleDriveFolderRecursive` → `walkDriveFolder` (pure function) + handler wrapper, enabling reuse by web-search folder walks
- Implemented web-search provider chain: Google Programmable Search (if `GOOGLE_CSE_ID` set) → Brave (if `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY` set) → keyless DuckDuckGo HTML scrape (fallback)
- Added fuzzy title matching (Levenshtein distance + normalization) duplicated from client-side `match.js` for scoring candidates
- Implemented Ultimate Guitar scraper: extracts `js-store` JSON from page, parses chord markup (`[ch]...[/ch]`), infers song key from chord progression, converts to Nashville numbers

**Client (`src/lib/setlist/`)**
- `sync.js`: Updated `searchChartForSong()` to return structured result with tier info and candidates; added `linkChartCandidate()` for user-picked web hits; added `fetchWebChartData()` wrapper for tier 4
- `chart-build.js` (new): Builds chart text from web chord data (real draft) or template (fallback); includes `chordLegend()` for the key's number→chord decoder ring
- `views.js`: Added `renderChartCandidates()` UI for web-search hits below the action bar (preview/use buttons); updated "create chart doc" flow to call `fetchWebChartData()` first, then `buildChartText()` or `buildTemplateChartText()`
- `gdrive-backup.js`: Renamed `createBlankChartDoc()` → `createChartDoc()` (now accepts content parameter); uploads chart text as plain-text to Drive, which auto-converts to a Doc

**Docs & UI**
- Updated `docs/setlist-app.md` to document the new tier 3 (web search) and tier 4 (chart drafting) with provider chain details
- Added CSS for chart-candidate picker (`.sl-chart-candidates`, `.sl-chart-candidate`, etc.)
- Updated `wrangler.toml` comments to document optional env vars for web search

## Notable implementation details

- Web-search candidates must score ≥ 0.85 to auto-link; weaker hits (0.55–0.85) appear in a picker for manual review
- Drive hits are verified (reachable with API key = link-shared = scrape/offline-cache will work); Dropbox links are marked `unverified` (can't verify without OAuth)
- Shared folders from web search get a bounded walk (max 3 depth, 20 folders, 600 files) to protect worker execution time
- Key inference uses weighted diatonic scoring across all 12 major keys, with extra weight on first/last chords; detects relative minor if song starts and ends on that chord
- Chart text format matches the worker's existing plain-text scraper (`extractFromText`), so docs generated by this module can be re-scraped for metadata
- HTML entity decoding and browser UA spoofing for web scraping; DuckDuckGo search has a 10s timeout to prevent hung fetches from stalling the request

author: beer4code
body:
## What

Fixes Dynatrace token detection to cover **all** token types, and adds opportunistic verification of a token against a co-located tenant URL via the `/api/v2/apiTokens/lookup` endpoint.

## Why

Dynatrace tokens have the shape `dt0<type><nn>.<public-id>.<secret>`, e.g. `dt0c01` API/PAT tokens and `dt0s01`/`dt0s16` platform tokens. The existing rule hardcoded the `dt0c01` prefix, required a fixed 24-char public-id, and used `dt0c01.` as its keyword, so every other token type was silently missed (the keyword alone stopped the regex from even running on them). A Dynatrace token only authenticates against its own tenant, so when a tenant host appears nearby we can confirm the token is live.

## How

Three rules (existing rule kept as the always-on baseline; two appended):

- **`dynatrace-api-token`**: fixed regex `\bdt0[a-z][0-9]{2}\.[A-Za-z0-9\-]{8,128}\.[A-Z0-9]{64}\b`, keyword `dt0`. Always reports the token, verified or not.
- **`dynatrace-tenant-url`**: `skipReport` helper matching Dynatrace SaaS tenant hosts (`*.live.dynatrace.com`, `*.apps.dynatrace.com`, `*.{dev,sprint}[.apps].dynatracelabs.com`). For the validation request, `.apps.` is stripped.
- **`dynatrace-api-token-verified`**: composite requiring a nearby tenant; `validate` POSTs to `/api/v2/apiTokens/lookup`:
  -  200/403 → valid,
  - 401 → invalid,
  - other → unknown/error,  

Given a higher `specificity`, the rule `dynatrace-api-token-verified` dedups against the `dynatrace-api-token` finding, so: 
  - token **with** a nearby tenant → reported as `dynatrace-api-token-verified` finding, with tenant carried verbatim in `requiredSets` and `validationMeta.tenant`,
  - token **without** a tenant → still reported as `dynatrace-api-token` (unverified).

Multiple tenants in one fragment are handled by the engine's cartesian `requiredSets`.

## Note: generator change

`cmd/generate/config/rules/config.tmpl` now emits a rule's `specificity` whenever set (previously hardcoded only for `generic-api-key`). 

This is required so `dynatrace-api-token-verified` (specificity 200) suppresses the plain `dynatrace-api-token` (default 100) when both match the same token, collapsing to a single reported finding. It affects only rules that set a non-default specificity.

## Testing

- `go generate ./...` (regenerates + validates rules), `go vet`, `go build`, `go test ./...` pass. 
- Manually verified against live tenants: verified token, invalid token (401), unreachable tenant, nonexistent tenant (404), 2×2 cartesian (token × tenant), no-tenant (always flagged), platform token (`dt0s16`, 403), and `apps` → API host rewrite. 
  - In all cases the token was successfully surfaced; validation reflected the live result; and the tenant was reported correctly.

Closes the gap identified in #1047 (superseded by epic #1309): the docs site's own deploy already ran on Workers Static Assets, but the adapter, `zfb preview`, doc content, and CI plumbing still assumed Pages.

### Adapter (`@takazudo/zfb-adapter-cloudflare`)

body:
## Summary

`buildSubnetYield` reported a fabricated `block_number: 0` for a subnet whose snapshot's first neuron row has a **null** chain height, instead of the `null` the contract defines. This surfaces through both `GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/yield` and the newly-added `get_subnet_yield` MCP tool (#2612), which share this shaper.

The snapshot block was stamped via `Number(row.block_number)`, and `Number(null) === 0` is finite, so a null cell became the genesis height `0`:

```js
const block = Number(row?.block_number);
blockNumber = Number.isFinite(block) ? block : null;
```

`block_number` is a nullable `INTEGER` in the `neurons` table and `loadSubnetYield` selects it unfiltered, so a null is reachable; the contract (`SubnetYieldArtifact`) and the MCP output schema both model it as `["integer","null"]`. This is the same coercion class the maintainers just fixed in the global validators leaderboard (#2611) and the neuron snapshot stamp / detail (#2623).

## What Changed

- `src/subnet-yield.mjs` — guard `block_number == null` before `Number()` so a null cell yields `null`, while a numeric string like `"8454388"` from D1 still passes. `captured_at` is `INTEGER NOT NULL`, so it is intentionally left unchanged.
- `tests/subnet-yield.test.mjs` — regression test: a neuron row with `block_number: null` yields `block_number: null` (the existing coercion test only covered a non-numeric *string* block, not `null`).

No schema/contract change, so no regenerated committed artifacts.

## Registry Safety

- [x] No secrets, PATs, wallet data, private dashboards, private URLs, or validator-local state.
- [x] Generated artifacts were produced by repo scripts, not hand-edited.
- [x] R2-only/high-churn detail artifacts are not committed.
- [x] Public API/OpenAPI/schema changes are intentional and documented. (no contract change; aligns runtime with the existing `["integer","null"]` contract)

Follow-up to the post-merge review on #27 (dashboard console).

## Fixes
- **MinionBar timer leak** — the fade `setTimeout` was "cleaned up" by a function returned from the `setInterval` callback, which React never uses, so the timeout could fire after unmount and call `setState`. The console shell relies on `@keyframes` (the 11 minion animations), `::before` pseudo-elements (activity lines), `backdrop-filter`, and fixed-position transitions — none expressible as pure Tailwind utilities — and the stylesheet is scoped under `.fd-console` to isolate the dark-glass theme from the app's light `sb-` theme. Having an LLM hand-write SVG plateaus — it can't produce consistent icon sets or polished raster rewards, and edits drift after a few rounds (research-confirmed, docs/RESEARCH-ASSET-GEN.md). body:
## Summary

This PR comes out of a full readiness assessment of the CRM. It fixes the one defect that made the project unusable on any machine other than the original developer's, plus two smaller infrastructure issues, and adds setup documentation for the planned two-person (Darnell + Shria) shared-instance workflow.

## Fixes

- **`vitest.config.ts` imported vitest from a hardcoded path on the original dev machine** (`/home/ubuntu/em-campaign-studio/node_modules/...`), and vitest was not a dependency. This broke `pnpm test` outright and — because the config file is included in type-checking — also failed `pnpm build` and the `pnpm verify` typecheck step on every other machine. Vitest is now a proper devDependency and the config imports from `vitest/config`.
- **`pnpm-workspace.yaml` contained unfilled placeholder text** (`set this to true or false`) under a non-standard `allowBuilds` key, which silently prevented pnpm 10 from running the Prisma/esbuild install scripts. Replaced with the correct `onlyBuiltDependencies` list.
- **n8n had no Docker volume**, so any workflows/credentials would be lost when the container was recreated. Added a named volume (`em_n8n_data`), and removed the obsolete `version` key from docker-compose.
- Removed `debug_import.mjs`, a leftover scratch script whose cases are covered by the real test suite.

## Docs

- New **"Sharing One Instance Between Two People"** section in `LOCAL_SETUP.md`: LAN/Tailscale access, the required `NEXTAUTH_URL` change, retrieving magic-link emails from MailHog on the host, a warning against exposing ports to the public internet, and a recommendation to run production mode (`pnpm build && pnpm start`) for daily use.
- Marked n8n as optional in setup docs (`docker compose up -d postgres mailhog` for the minimal stack).

## Verification

- `pnpm test`: 24/24 tests pass
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: zero errors
- `pnpm build`: compiles cleanly (all pages and 31 API routes)

body:
## What

**RFC-0011 Phase P4.** An in-app connection form (`Ctrl-N`) to add / edit / remove connection profiles — no more hand-editing `config.toml`.

- **`cairn-core/src/forms.rs`**: `FieldSpec` + `scheme_fields(scheme)` — the per-scheme **endpoint** field schema (ssh/s3/gcs/azure), keyed to exactly what `connect.rs` reads.
- **`Overlay::ConnectionForm`** (SchemePicker → Fields stages) + **`Overlay::ConfirmDeleteConnection`**; `TextEdit::Next/PrevField` (Tab/Shift-Tab), `Action::New/Edit/DeleteConnection` (`Ctrl-N`; `E`/`D` contextual in the switcher, no-ops on auto-discovered rows).
- **Effect runner**: `SaveConnection`/`DeleteConnection` write `Config` and update the switcher; local profiles mount immediately.

## Scope boundary

P4 is **secret-free** — it saves the endpoint config only. Credential capture + vault storage is **P5** (after P4.5 vault-create); `FieldSpec::secret` is forward-declared but unused. A credential-bearing profile added in P4 saves fine and shows as `NeedsVault`/`NeedsOpen`; it becomes connectable once P5 lands. New remote profiles need a restart to open this session (the live descriptor swap is a tracked P6 item); local profiles are live immediately.

## Review gates

bug-bot + code-review. The three headline risks (index safety, auto-discovered edit/delete guard, `secret_ref` preservation on edit) were verified handled. Findings fixed before merge:

- **CRITICAL (code-review):** the S3 form stored the custom endpoint under `endpoint_url` but `connect.rs` reads `endpoint` — MinIO/custom-S3 endpoints were silently ignored. Fixed, and a **field-key fidelity test** now asserts every `scheme_fields` key matches a key `connect.rs` reads, so the form and config can't drift again.
- Scheme-change field leak (stray keys from a previously-picked scheme are now pruned); failed-save no longer discards the form (stays open with values); edit preserves the scheme-prefixed label (computed in the effect runner); honest "applies on next open/restart" status for edits; `e` removed from the global keymap; deletion now goes through a confirm overlay; `Ctrl-N` doc alignment.

`cargo test --workspace` + `--all-features` (0 failures); lean + all-features clippy (`-D warnings`); the **exact** CI rustdoc (`--workspace --no-deps --all-features`); fmt — all clean. New tests: `scheme_fields` correctness + key fidelity, submit validation, scheme-change prune, edit pre-fill + `secret_ref` preservation, auto-discovered edit/delete rejection, label patch, delete flow, failed-save retention, input routing.

## Docs

`CHANGELOG.md`, RFC-0011 (`Ctrl-N`), `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.

author: litianningdatadog
body:
### What does this PR do?

Stops MicroVM's async `/run` lifecycle hook from mutating `Agent.GlobalTags` and routes the dynamic `lambda_microvm_id` tag update through the (already serverless-owned) span modifier instead.

Concretely:
- `pkg/serverless/trace/span_modifier.go`: `tags` field is now `atomic.Pointer[map[string]string]` (using `go.uber.org/atomic`, per repo convention); `ModifySpan` applies each tag lock-free via `Load()`.
- `pkg/serverless/trace/trace.go`: adds `UpdateRuntimeTags`, which updates only the span modifier — never `GlobalTags`. The existing `SetTags` (called once, synchronously, at startup before the trace agent runs) is untouched and still updates both.
- `cmd/serverless-init/main.go`: the two async `TraceTagSetterFunc` closures wired into the MicroVM lifecycle server now call `UpdateRuntimeTags` instead of `SetTags`.
- `cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle/server.go`: updated a doc comment that named the (now stale) method satisfying `TraceTagSetter`.

### Motivation

Codex flagged a data race on #53036: `serverlessTraceAgent.SetTags` is invoked from a goroutine inside the MicroVM lifecycle server's `/run` handler, which runs concurrently with the trace agent's span-processing loop. `SetTags` calls `Agent.SetGlobalTagsUnsafe`, whose own doc comment says "Unsafe for concurrent use" — it does a bare `a.conf.GlobalTags = tags` write, while `pkg/trace/agent/agent.go` (hot path, lines 531/711) and `pkg/trace/api/telemetry.go` read `a.conf.GlobalTags` with no synchronization at all. `GlobalTags` is computed once at config-build time, before the trace agent starts running, and every one of those readers assumes that invariant holds forever — MicroVM's dynamic per-invocation tag update is the only thing in the codebase that breaks it.

In practice the write is a pointer swap to a new map rather than an in-place mutation, so the realistic worst case is a span in flight at the moment of the swap missing `lambda_microvm_id` — not a crash. But it's a genuine data race under the Go memory model: `go test -race` / `bazel test --config=race` will flag it the moment a concurrent test exercises this path, and nothing guarantees it stays benign under future compiler optimizations.

The fix avoids touching any code shared with the non-serverless trace agent (`pkg/trace/agent`, `pkg/trace/api`, `pkg/trace/config`) by reusing `SpanModifier`, which already runs at the identical point in `agent.go`'s span-processing loop (right after the `GlobalTags` loop) and is exclusively serverless-owned. Its `tags` field existed before this change but was dead code — written by `SetTags`, never read by `ModifySpan`; this fix makes it real.

This is scoped entirely to MicroVM. Every other cloud service (`AppService`, `CloudRun`, `ContainerApp`, `CloudRunJobs`) ignores `LifecycleCtx` in `Init`, so they never invoke the async closures — they only ever call the original, still-synchronous `SetTags` once at startup, unchanged by this PR.

### Describe how you validated your changes

Added regression coverage for every change (7 new/extended tests):
- `TestSpanModifierSetTagsConcurrentWithModifySpan` — hammers `SetTags`/`ModifySpan` from two goroutines under the race detector; this is the actual bug repro.
- `TestSpanModifierModifySpanBeforeSetTags`, `...AppliesTagsSetDynamically`, `...ReflectsLatestSetTags` — functional coverage of the new atomic-pointer-backed tag application.
- `TestServerlessTraceAgentSetTagsUpdatesGlobalTagsAndSpanModifier` — confirms the untouched synchronous `SetTags` path still updates both `GlobalTags` and the span modifier.
- `TestServerlessTraceAgentUpdateRuntimeTagsDoesNotTouchGlobalTags` — the core assertion: `UpdateRuntimeTags` never writes `GlobalTags`.
- `TestServerlessTraceAgentUpdateRuntimeTagsNoSpanModifier` — no-op safety when `SpanModifier` doesn't implement `taggable`.
- Extended `TestSetupWithoutAPIKey` to also exercise `noopTraceAgent.UpdateRuntimeTags`.

Run locally with:

```sh
dda inv test --targets=./pkg/serverless/trace,./cmd/serverless-init,./cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle,./cmd/serverless-init/cloudservice --race
dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/serverless/trace,./cmd/serverless-init,./cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle,./cmd/serverless-init/cloudservice
```

All 302 tests pass (4 skipped, platform-gated) with the race detector enabled; linter reports 0 issues.

### Additional Notes

Stacked on #53096 (`tianning.li/microvm-07-05-main-wiring`) — base branch will move to `main` once that merges. `BUILD.bazel` files were checked (`bazel run //:gazelle -- update` + buildifier on the one Gazelle-managed directory touched, `cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle`); no changes needed since the rest of the touched files are under pre-existing `gazelle:exclude` directives (not yet Bazel-migrated).
