author: amarcher
body:
## Workstream 2 — Daily co-op + cross-day leaderboard (both race modes)

One link → lobby → **choose a mode** → everyone released into the SAME daily at the same instant → results + streak/board to come back to tomorrow.

### The two modes (host picks in the lobby — new `RaceModeSelector`, broadcast via `game_started` settings + persisted for rejoiners)

**1. ASYNC — "Time trial" (separate grids)**
- Every player solves their OWN copy. Input validates locally only (`asyncInputLetter`) — no claims, no broadcasts; **one player's letters never appear on another's grid** (E2E-verified: host 9 cells filled, peer grid 0). Wrong-answer lockout still honored.
- Filling your copy = your finish: elapsed from the shared start clock, broadcast (`race_finished`) + persisted (`players.race_seconds`) for rejoiners. Your result modal opens immediately with **your time** and live standings ("Solving…" for the rest); when everyone's in, the fastest finisher wins (competition ranking, pure + unit-tested `rankRaceStandings`). The in-game sidebar shows live standings instead of the cells scoreboard.
- **Feeds the daily leaderboard**: each async finisher posts their OWN time (keep-best) to `daily_results` (`mode: race`).

**2. SYNC — one shared grid (two flavors)**
- **Competitive (default "Compete")**: today's existing claim-cell multiplayer, REUSED untouched — winner by cells/clues, shared race time headline.
- **Co-op**: identical engine, team framing — "Solved together!" + team time on the result and the share card (🤝), no winner ranking.

### Entry + return loop (unchanged from the first revision, rebased on WS1)
- Menu **⚔️ Race friends** hands today's mini straight to the existing host flow (no import step); works identically for any imported puzzle.
- Shared race clock: `games.started_at` + broadcast timestamps; refresh/rejoin-safe.
- `/daily/leaderboard`: today's fastest (solo + async race, mode chips), viewer row highlighted, streak badge, play/race CTAs; degrades offline.
- Solo daily finishes post keep-best times; ALL modes roll the local streak.
- Boast share: result card carries time + standing (feeds WS4 links when both merge).

### Verified end-to-end (two isolated browser contexts, 375px)
- **Versus**: lobby → join via one URL → synchronized start → both clients showed identical race time (0:53), winner, rank table, leaderboard CTA.
- **Async**: mode selector in lobby → start → grid isolation confirmed → first finisher (1:01) saw personal result + "Waiting for the others…" → second finisher (1:29) → both clients agreed "RacerBen wins!" ranked by time.
- Offline path: leaderboard degrades to streak + note; solo untouched.

### Tests / build
`pnpm build` clean; suite green — **561 tests** (new: `raceResults` standings/ranking, `dailyLeaderboard` ranking/keep-best/identity). i18n en/es parity for all new strings.

### ⚠️ Deploy note
Run `npx supabase db push` when merging (adds `games.started_at`, `players.race_seconds`, `daily_results`). Code tolerates an un-migrated DB (best-effort writes, `select("*")`), so previews can't break existing multiplayer — but async standings won't survive refreshes and leaderboard rows won't persist until it's applied. (Schema pushes weren't authorized from this run.)

### Assumptions (per the working agreement)
- **Sync results don't post times to the daily board** — a team-shared grid time isn't comparable to individual solves; async + solo times are the board's currency. Sync completions still roll the streak.
- Async mid-solve refresh loses local letters (the clock stays honest via `started_at`; the player keeps racing). Accepted v1 limitation.
- TV/narrator spectating is meaningful for shared-grid modes only (async grids are private by design).
- Host-click start is the release mechanism (GOAL allowed host or countdown).

author: 8beeeaaat
body:
Fixes #173

## Background / fact-check

The issue states that "TouchDesigner 2025+ **bundles** the official MCP SDK as `site-packages/mcp`", but checking the official documentation shows **this is not accurate**:

- The [official list of bundled 3rd-party packages](https://docs.derivative.ca/Python_Classes_and_Modules) does not include `mcp` or `anthropic`.
- The Python packages added in the 2025.30000 release notes are only `box` / `tzdata` / `pygdtf` / `pymvr` / NumPy.
- All [Release Notes](https://derivative.ca/UserGuide/Release_Notes) up to the reporter's build (2025.32820) contain no mention of a bundled `mcp`.
- The follow-up comment on the issue describes the SDK as "(Anthropic, **installed via pip**) ... sits in **AppData**/.../site-packages" — a different origin/path than the install dir.

Accurate root cause: **when a same-named package (`mcp`, or the very generic `utils`) ends up in TouchDesigner's Python — pip-installed or side-loaded via tdPyEnvManager — it shadows this project's local `modules/mcp` / `modules/utils` packages.** A real, reproducible collision — just not caused by TD bundling the SDK. The fix is the same either way.

## Changes

**1. `import_modules.py` — sys.path priority + sys.modules eviction**
- `sys.path.append(...)` -> `sys.path.insert(0, ...)` so the local `modules/` dir wins.
- Evict any already-imported `mcp*` **and** `utils*` from `sys.modules` before re-importing. `sys.modules` caching takes precedence over `sys.path`, so if a competing package was imported before `setup()` runs, path reordering alone would not help — eviction forces re-resolution against the project paths. (`utils` covered per Codex review; it is a more likely collision name than `mcp`.)

**2. Missing `__init__.py`**
- Added `modules/mcp/__init__.py` and `modules/utils/__init__.py` so they are regular packages that can shadow a same-named installed package.
- These files were simply **never present in the repository** (not a Windows-extractor problem). Since the release zip is built from `td/modules` as-is, adding them to the repo also fixes the release artifact.

**3. Re-synced the embedded DAT inside `mcp_webserver_base.tox`**
- The `import_modules` DAT is embedded in the `.tox` (its `file` parameter is empty), so the on-disk `.py` is **not** what executes at runtime — the baked-in copy is. Replaced the embedded contents with the final fixed code (mcp + utils eviction) and re-saved the component.

## Verification

- Reproduced `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp.controllers'` in a sandbox by placing a competing `mcp` at the front of `sys.path`; confirmed the fix makes local `mcp`/`utils` win and `mcp.controllers` resolve locally.
- Reproduced `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'utils.error_handling'` with a competing `utils` already cached in `sys.modules`; confirmed local resolution after the generalized eviction.
- Confirmed a **clean `ControllerManager` init in TouchDesigner 2025.31550** after re-saving the `.tox` (HTTP server started, 12 routes loaded).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass.

## Note

- **`td_server/__init__.py`** — intentionally not added: `td_server` is a generated/gitignored artifact and is not imported as a package (its `sys.path` entry only serves `openapi.yaml` lookup).
- Long-term, consider linking the embedded `import_modules` DAT to the external `import_modules.py` (set its `file` param + Load on Start) so the two can't drift again — this PR required re-saving the `.tox` twice for that reason. Out of scope for this fix.

author: tieguy
body:
## Summary

Design docs (no code) establishing **Wikidata as a first-class SP42 target** — not
just a book-metadata source, but a patrol target and a bidirectional bridge with the
citation work. SP42 already *resolves* `wikidatawiki`/`testwikidatawiki` (ADR-0014)
but can't *review* them: a Wikidata revision is entity JSON, so the diff view renders
raw JSON and every wikitext signal misfires.

- **PRD-0011** — Wikidata as a first-class target: the shared read module + a
  patrol-read MVP, with the use-case family (book/entity enrichment, citation→Wikidata
  facts, Wikidata→sources) sequenced as follow-ons. Six design decisions resolved
  in-doc.
- **ADR-0016** (platform) — Wikidata entity content-model: per-revision `content_model`
  (routing keys on the revision, never the wiki id), entity revision read, a new
  `EntityDiff` (full statement depth, never-a-no-op), `ContentDiff` routing, and
  content-model capability gating.
- **ADR-0017** (platform) — Wikidata statement-proposal write contract: reuses
  ADR-0010 propose/confirm with an entity+`lastrevid` locator and a grounded,
  referenced statement payload; respects the FRBR work/edition split.
- **Design plan** `2026-07-01-wikidata-read-model.md` — the shared platform Wikidata
  read model and a line-by-line convergence mapping from PR #103's `wikidata.rs`.

New `docs/domains/wikidata/` domain, indexed in `docs/README.md` and
`docs/domains/README.md`.

## Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Build, CI, or release
- [ ] Security-sensitive change

## Validation Required

Docs-only change (Markdown under `docs/`); no source, build, or test surface touched.

```sh
# nothing to run — no code changed
```

## Risk

- [ ] Touches auth/session/cookies/CSRF
- [ ] Touches deployment/runtime configuration
- [ ] Touches desktop packaging
- [ ] Touches scoring or Wikimedia action behavior
- [x] Needs an ADR

Two ADRs are *included* here (ADR-0016, ADR-0017), both `Proposed`. No further ADR is
required to merge these drafts.

## Notes For Reviewers

**Coordination dependency — PR #103 (PRD-0010, MCP surface).** #103 ships the first
Wikidata read in the codebase (`verify_wikidata_statement`, `sp42-mcp/src/wikidata.rs`)
but in the `sp42-mcp` shell. Per the reuse-by-design rule, ADR-0016 **promotes that
entity/statement parser into platform** so patrol, the MCP verb, and the write lane
share one read model. The design plan gives the line-by-line mapping; #103's own design
plan already anticipated a platform home for the renderer, so this is convergence, not
conflict. **Whichever of #103 / this lands first, the other consumes or refactors onto
the shared module — #103's public verb contract (PRD-0010) is unchanged either way.**
ADR-0017 is the exact inverse of #103's verb (propose a referenced statement vs. verify
an existing one).

**Numbering.** #99 holds ADR-0015 (fetch edge), so these took the next free global
numbers, 0016/0017. PRD is 0011 (0010 is #103's).

**Ecosystem due-diligence (baked into the docs).** OL and Wikidata already sync (P648;
OL's official Wikidata Integration; `cdrini/openlibrary-wikidata-bot`). SP42 does **not**
rebuild identifier sync — its value is the grounded/referenced-statement layer, which
answers the standing WikiProject complaint that most bots add unsourced statements. And
ADR-0017 respects the **FRBR work/edition split** (ISBN/publisher on the edition item,
sourced there; decline rather than create a missing edition — avoiding the ~40k
mis-placed-edition-ID class of bulk-import error). A follow-up note tracks mirroring the
de-dup point into PRD-0009 (PR #104).

**Most worth scrutiny:** ADR-0016 Decision 5 (content-model capability gating as a new
axis on the profile) and the PRD's resolved Q1 (hybrid/defer on domain placement — no
new crate for the MVP). Everything is `Draft`/`Proposed`; this PR exists to get the
design reviewed before code.

Follow-up to #117, addressing the review comment left on it (https://github.com/mikelward/scripts/pull/117#discussion_r3508865541).

During a fresh bootstrap, `setup` runs `$SCRIPTS_DIR/setup-kde` straight out of the just-cloned repo, before any login shell has put `~/scripts` on PATH — so #117's warn-and-skip guard would skip *every* launch shortcut even though `browser1`, `terminal`, etc. sit right next to `setup-kde`. `add_app_shortcut` now falls back to the script's own directory before treating a launcher as absent; PATH still wins when the launcher is found there.

author: ezyjtw
body:
First code that WRITES to Xero. Every push is gated by isPushEnabled() (connected + required mapping complete + flag ON) at both enqueue and run time, idempotent, and posts to the mapped BANK account. TaxType NONE.

Pipeline: payment_intent.succeeded, transfer release, and writeRefundSuccess ENQUEUE a XERO_PUSH BackgroundJob (only when pushing is enabled); the existing cron worker drains it and posts via the refresh-aware Xero client. Keeps webhooks fast and the push retryable.

Real-money anchoring (per the field-set ruling — Xero reconciles with the Stripe balance, not the snapshot plan):
- gross RECEIVE = totalAmountCharged; clearing line = getTransferAmountPence (cleanerEarnings) = the actual transfer; commission+fee = the remainder, split ONLY by the snapshot ratio platformCommissionAmount:customerServiceFee.
- PAYMENT_RECEIVED -> Receive Money, 3 lines (commission/fee income + cleaner net to clearing). PAYOUT -> Spend Money from bank, clearing.
- REFUND -> reversing transaction mirroring the RefundRecord proportionally (proportion = refundRecord.amount / totalAmountCharged). Pre-release = one reversing SPEND; post-release = SPEND (customer) + RECEIVE (cleaner clawback). The cleaner's share is captured at enqueue time (pre-mutation) because A5.2 reduces cleanerEarnings on a pre-release refund. Represents the attempted reversal (notes the withdrew-already deficit asymmetry).

Idempotency: XeroPushLog @@unique([bookingId, event, externalRef]) — a COMPLETED row means skip; externalRef = stripeRefundId for refunds, "" (not null, so Postgres actually enforces uniqueness) for payment/payout. Plus Xero's Idempotency-Key header = bookingId:event:externalRef. Never double-posts on a webhook re-delivery or queue re-run.

Contact: single "Rena Marketplace" contact, found-or-created once and cached on XeroConnection.platformContactId.

Additive schema (XeroPushLog + platformContactId). Push flag still defaults OFF.

author: hiddevandebeek
body:
## Why

The nightly **Slow tests** job has been red on `main`. Two independent M3 tests fail:

1. `iov_m3_ode_matches_closed_form_estimates` — the closed-form and ODE legs of an engine-consistency check disagreed by ~0.77 OFV (inner-EBE under-convergence on one flat, heavily-censored subject, amplified by #641). **Already fixed on `main`** by #654 (`inner_tol = 1e-11`).
2. `bloq_m3_foce_analytic_matches_nonmem` — ferx's Sheiner–Beal **FOCE**-M3 converged to TVCL ≈ 0.1399, ~6.7 % off the NONMEM value the test pinned (0.131073, tol 1 %). This anchor is **invalid by construction**, and nothing addressed it, so the job stayed red even after #654.

**NONMEM has no genuine first-order, non-interaction "FOCE M3" method.** M3 BLOQ in NONMEM is the F_FLAG mixed likelihood, which *requires* `$EST METHOD=1 LAPLACE`. The pinned reference file `tests/nonmem/warfarin_bloq_foce.lst` is in fact a `METHOD=1 LAPLACE` (no-INTER) run mislabeled "FOCE". NONMEM's LAPLACE-M3 corresponds to ferx's **FOCEI**-M3 — already cross-checked against `warfarin_bloq.lst` by `bloq_m3_analytic_lbfgs_matches_nonmem`. ferx's FOCE-M3 (linearized-marginal moments, #646) is a genuinely different, ferx-specific optimum with no NONMEM twin.

## What changed

- Rewrote the FOCE-M3 slow test as a **self-consistency** check — the established idiom for this engine (cf. `iov_m3_analytic_matches_fd_estimates`): the analytic FOCE-M3 outer gradient (`GradientMethod::Auto`) must drive the optimizer to the same MLE as the finite-difference gradient (`GradientMethod::Fd`) of the identical marginal. Renamed `bloq_m3_foce_analytic_matches_nonmem` → `bloq_m3_foce_analytic_matches_fd`; asserts equal OFV / θ, finite OFV, and that FOCE-M3 stays distinct from FOCEI-M3 (TVKA < 0.76).
- Deleted the misleading `tests/nonmem/warfarin_bloq_foce.{ctl,lst}` fixtures. The valid FOCEI anchor `warfarin_bloq.{ctl,lst}` (LAPLACE INTER) is untouched.
- The IOV failure needs no change here — #654's fix is already on `main` and this branch inherits it.

## Breaking changes
- [x] None

## Numerical validation
Ran the affected slow tests locally (ci-test profile + `slow-tests`, WSL):

```
test bloq_m3_foce_analytic_matches_fd ... ok        # analytic ≡ FD reach the same FOCE-M3 optimum
test bloq_m3_analytic_lbfgs_matches_nonmem ... ok   # FOCEI anchor (warfarin_bloq.lst, LAPLACE INTER) unchanged
test iov_m3_ode_matches_closed_form_estimates ... ok
  M3+IOV closed-form vs ODE: OFV 382.49464 vs 382.49463   (θ agree to 0.00%)
```

- [x] Compared against: prior ferx behaviour / NONMEM method semantics (FOCE-M3 has no NONMEM equivalent — see Why)
- [x] Not applicable for a new NONMEM anchor (the point of this PR is that one cannot exist for FOCE-M3)

## Performance
- [x] No significant impact expected (the FOCE-M3 test now runs two fits instead of one, but it is slow-tier only).

## Tests
- [x] Regression coverage: `bloq_m3_foce_analytic_matches_fd` fails if the analytic FOCE-M3 outer gradient diverges from FD; the deleted NONMEM assertion could never pass for this estimator.
- [x] No new unit tests needed (validation restructured, not new behaviour).

## Docs
- [x] No user-visible change (test-only + fixture removal; no `CHANGELOG` entry required per repo policy).

## Reviewer hints
- Key claim to sanity-check: `warfarin_bloq_foce.ctl` uses `$ESTIMATION METHOD=1 LAPLACE` (no INTERACTION) — that is Laplace, not FOCE, so it was never a valid FOCE-M3 anchor.
- The self-consistency test uses L-BFGS for both legs; the 3 % θ band absorbs optimizer-path noise on the flat KA ridge (both legs converged to identical θ in local runs).

author: kixelated
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #1973. The paced TS egress there stamps a whole frame at one `pace` instant, so every packet in the frame leaves in a single burst at the frame boundary. A downstream TS decoder assumes a near-constant arrival rate, so a per-frame burst overruns its buffer model (glitches and PCR errors) unless the mux is padded to CBR (ffmpeg's `-muxrate`). This trickles each frame out instead.

- **moq-mux**: new `Output::spread(span, chunk)` slices a frame into `chunk`-sized pieces, each due at an instant interpolated across the frame's on-wire duration.
- **moq-cli `--pace`**: sleeps per chunk instead of per frame.
- **moq-srt egress**: stamps each SRT payload's TSBPD instant from the spread.

Both consumers estimate the frame's on-wire duration from the previous frame's `pace` gap (tracks a steady frame rate; collapses to an immediate burst on a tune-in re-anchor), so no lookahead buffering and no added latency.

## Scope / what this does NOT do

This is the **delivery half** only. Per @ArielM's IRD findings, it does **not** re-stamp PCR: the PCR values still come from `author_dts` per video frame, so a hardware IRD's PLL (which rebuilds its 27 MHz clock from PCR and needs uniform, ≤40 ms-spaced samples per TR 101 290) will still see a sparse, non-uniform clock. The operative IRD fix is a separate PCR re-stamp (uniform cadence, value from the pace/media clock, no null padding) layered on top of this. Happy to fold that in here or land it as a follow-up.

## Public API (moq-mux, additive)

- new `pub fn ts::Output::spread(&self, span: Duration, chunk: usize) -> impl Iterator<Item = (Instant, Bytes)>`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p moq-mux -p moq-cli -p moq-srt` (spread covers even split, short final chunk, zero-span burst)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p moq-mux -p moq-cli -p moq-srt --all-targets` clean
- [ ] Not exercised end-to-end against a real IRD (needs the PCR re-stamp for that)

author: rdself
body:
## Problem

After the v3.8.40+ origin hardening, dashboard writes can fail behind changing public hosts unless `OMNIROUTE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is pinned to the exact browser URL. This breaks normal UI workflows such as combo/model tests, saving combo edits, provider/model edits, settings/UI configuration saves, and other dashboard management actions when the dashboard is reached through an ephemeral tunnel, CDN host, or HTTPS proxy.

The v3.8.41 CSRF repair only covered the model/combo test endpoints. The rest of the dashboard still relied on public-origin matching, so authenticated same-origin UI writes could still return `INVALID_ORIGIN` even though the user was using the dashboard normally.

## Root cause

Dashboard CSRF validation was path-limited to:

- `/api/combos/test`
- `/api/models/test`
- `/api/models/test-all`

The frontend also attached the token only at those individual call sites. Regular management mutations such as `/api/settings`, `/api/combos/*`, `/api/providers/*`, `/api/quota/pools`, `/a2a`, and other dashboard writes did not get the portable session-bound CSRF fallback.

## Changes

- Allow a valid dashboard CSRF token to satisfy only the `invalid-origin` branch for authenticated `dashboard_session` + `MANAGEMENT` + unsafe methods.
- Keep cross-site Fetch Metadata fail-closed: `sec-fetch-site: cross-site` is not bypassed by CSRF.
- Install one dashboard-level fetch wrapper early from `DashboardLayout`, before child passive effects can issue initial writes.
- Attach `x-omniroute-csrf` automatically to same-origin dashboard management mutations.
- Exclude client API and public API surfaces from the wrapper (`/api/v1*`, `/v1*`, `/v1beta*`, `/responses`, `/models`, `/codex`, public auth/OAuth routes, and cross-origin requests).
- Cover explicit top-level management routes used by the dashboard, including `/a2a`.
- Move the traffic-inspector system-proxy unload revert from `sendBeacon` to `fetch(..., keepalive: true)` so it uses the same CSRF mechanism.
- Remove one-off CSRF header plumbing from combo/model test call sites.
- Update reverse-proxy/tunnel docs to clarify that dashboard writes do not require a static public base URL; OAuth callbacks and generated public links still do.

## Validation

- `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/ui/use-system-proxy-exit-guard.test.tsx tests/unit/authz/csrf.test.ts tests/unit/authz/pipeline.test.ts`
- `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/unit/ui/dashboard-csrf-fetch.test.tsx 'src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/providers/[id]/__tests__/useModelVisibilityHandlers.test.tsx' tests/unit/ui/use-model-visibility-handlers-test-all.test.tsx`
- `npm run typecheck:core`

author: slisbeth1523-netizen
body:
## Resumen tecnico

Implementa el procesador base del Domain Event Engine. Permite bloquear eventos `PENDING`, moverlos a `PROCESSING`, consultar subscriptions declarativas activas y ejecutar un dispatcher simulado sin listeners reales ni llamadas externas.

## Migracion creada

- `database/sqlserver/migrations/012_domain_event_processor.sql`
  - Agrega `LockedAt`, `LockedBy`, `NextAttemptAt`, `LastAttemptAt` y `MaxRetries` a `events.DomainEvents` si faltan.
  - Actualiza el CHECK de `Status` para incluir `PROCESSING`.
  - Agrega constraint para `MaxRetries >= 1`.
  - Agrega indice `IX_events_DomainEvents_Pending_Lock` orientado a bloqueo por tenant y estado.

## Archivos creados/modificados

- `apps/api/src/modules/events/application/DomainEventProcessorService.ts`
- `apps/api/src/modules/events/application/DomainEventDispatcherService.ts`
- `apps/api/src/modules/events/infrastructure/DomainEventRepository.ts`
- `apps/api/src/modules/events/domain/events.types.ts`
- `apps/api/src/modules/events/validators/events.validators.ts`
- `apps/api/src/modules/events/api/routes/events.routes.ts`
- `database/sqlserver/migrations/012_domain_event_processor.sql`

## Endpoints creados

- `POST /api/events/process`
- `POST /api/events/:eventId/retry`
- `GET /api/events/subscriptions/active/:eventName`

Permisos usados:

- `events.process`
- `events.retry`
- `events.subscriptions.read`

## Processor implementado

- `processPendingBatch(limit)` bloquea eventos pendientes del tenant actual.
- `processEvent(event)` procesa un evento bloqueado.
- Eventos sin subscriptions activas se marcan como `IGNORED`.
- Eventos con subscriptions activas se despachan de forma simulada y se marcan como `PROCESSED`.
- Fallos incrementan `RetryCount`; si queda margen de reintentos, vuelven a `PENDING` con `NextAttemptAt`; si alcanzan `MaxRetries`, pasan a `FAILED`.

## Dispatcher simulado implementado

- No llama HTTP.
- No ejecuta codigo dinamico.
- No usa `eval`.
- No usa `Function`.
- Solo registra con `logger.info` el subscriber que habria recibido el evento.

## Estrategia anti doble procesamiento

`DomainEventRepository.lockPendingBatch()` usa una actualizacion atomica con:

- `UPDLOCK`
- `READPAST`
- `ROWLOCK`
- filtro por `TenantId`
- `LockedBy`
- expiracion de lock por `LockedAt`

Esto evita que dos procesos tomen el mismo evento pendiente en paralelo.

## Auditoria implementada

Se registran eventos funcionales tolerantes a fallos mediante `auditEvent`:

- `DOMAIN_EVENT_PROCESSING_STARTED`
- `DOMAIN_EVENT_PROCESSED`
- `DOMAIN_EVENT_IGNORED`
- `DOMAIN_EVENT_FAILED`
- `DOMAIN_EVENT_RETRY_SCHEDULED`

## Verificacion realizada

- `npm install`: exitoso, sin vulnerabilidades reportadas.
- `npm run typecheck`: exitoso.
- `npm run build`: exitoso.

Endpoints base confirmados con API local:

- `GET /api/health`: HTTP 200.
- `GET /api/health/db`: HTTP 503 controlado con SQL Server no disponible, sin detener el proceso.
- `GET /api/version`: HTTP 200.

DE-001 sigue compilando porque esta rama esta basada en `feature/de-001-domain-event-foundation` y la verificacion completa pasa sobre la cadena actual.

## Fuera de alcance confirmado

No se implementaron listeners reales, webhooks reales, notificaciones reales, jobs reales, DGII, inventario, CxC, CxP, facturas, compras, clientes ni ejecucion dinamica de codigo.

author: joeyorlando
body:
## Why

The **Type checking, linting, formatting, unit tests** step took ~8.5 min of the ~11.5 min \`Platform Lint and Unit Tests\` job — all of it backend vitest. Profiling showed the dominant cost was not the tests themselves but **per-file isolation re-importing the entire backend module graph 588 times** (~3000s aggregate import cost; ~6.3s/file).

## What

### 1. Two-project Vitest split (\`backend/vitest.config.ts\`)

\`vi.mock\` registrations live in the worker's shared module/mock registry, which Vitest does not reset between files when \`isolate: false\` ([vitest-dev/vitest#4894](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/4894), [#10145](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/10145)) — measured here as 127 of 156 \`vi.mock\` files failing without isolation, while 428 of 432 mock-free files passed. So:

- **\`clean\` project** (~438 files, no module mocking) runs \`isolate: false\` — each worker imports the module graph once and reuses it.
- **\`mocked\` project** (~150 files using \`vi.mock\`/\`vi.hoisted\`) keeps full isolation.
- Routing is computed **from file content at config-load time** — a new test that adds \`vi.mock\` self-sorts into the isolated project; no manual list.

### 2. Cross-file leak guards (each killed a class of order-dependent flake)

Shared workers turn "forgot to restore" into cross-file poison, so the shared setup now guarantees restoration of every leakable global:

- **fetch**: \`unstubGlobals\`/\`unstubEnvs\` in config + an always-runs-last \`afterEach\` restore of \`globalThis.fetch\`; eleven module-scope fetch stubs re-apply per test.
- **the DB**: PGlite init awaited before test code (browser-global fakes raced its environment detection); \`@/database\`'s forwarding proxy no longer replaced by a concrete instance (better-auth's adapter was pinned to a closed DB); injected DB cleared on file teardown (unhandled "PGlite is closed" rejections became the handled "Database not initialized" path).
- **config**: tests mutate the real config object; the setup snapshots pristine config per worker and restores it before every test (shared-worker project only). This flushed out that the app suites' CI pass depended on a cross-file \`config.apps.enabled\` leak — \`ARCHESTRA_APPS_ENABLED\` is now forced in test env like \`ARCHESTRA_PROJECTS_ENABLED\`.
- Local full-suite runs cap \`maxWorkers\` at cores−2 so they don't pin the developer's machine (CI keeps all cores).

### 3. Mock architecture: canonical \`__mocks__\` + boundary mocking

320 \`vi.mock\` call sites hand-rolled factories for the same few modules. Now:

- **Jest-style \`__mocks__\` dirs** (bare \`vi.mock("@/auth");\`) for \`@/auth\` (was ×46), \`@/auth/utils\` (×6), \`@/logging\` (×13, silence-only mocks deleted), \`@/observability\` (×10, memoized proxy trees so the metric surface can't drift), and \`@/cache-manager\` (×11, Map-backed stateful fake with real cache semantics, auto-reset per test). Verified the \`__mocks__\` sibling resolution works through our absolute-path \`resolve.alias\`.
- **\`@/config\`** keeps a parameterized factory (\`configModuleMock(overrides)\` deep-merges onto the real config) — needed only when code reads config at import time; otherwise tests now mutate the real config in \`beforeEach\` (the restore guard covers them) and drop the mock entirely.
- **HTTP boundary mocking with MSW** (\`src/test/msw.ts\`, per-test lifecycle): jira.js and @gitbeaker/rest connector tests run the REAL clients against wire-level handlers — both files fully mock-free now — and four knowledge-base suites serve real OpenAI wire responses (incl. base64 Float32Array embeddings for openai@6) instead of mocking the \`openai\` module.
- The typed shared mocks surfaced latent bugs the untyped bespoke ones hid (a "deny" permission mock resolving a truthy object; a delete-subsequent-messages test racing same-millisecond \`createdAt\` ties).

### 4. Sharded CI (4× \`vitest run --shard=k/4\`)

Backend unit tests move out of the lint job into a 4-shard matrix running in parallel with it (the lint job's backend swaps \`check:ci\` → \`check:commit\`, identical minus vitest). Shards build backend's workspace deps first (Rust NAPI bindings; seconds on a turbo remote-cache hit). A stable-named **\`Backend Unit Tests\`** gate job aggregates the matrix for branch protection / merge queue.

### 5. Guidance for future test authors

- New skill \`.claude/skills/archestra-dev-backend-tests/SKILL.md\` — isolation model, canonical mocks, MSW boundary mocking (incl. client-retry and path-to-regexp gotchas), stub/config hygiene, DB fixtures.
- \`platform/CLAUDE.md\` (\`AGENTS.md\` symlinks to it): skill registered, backend-testing bullets updated.

## Measured results (local, 18-core; multiple shuffle seeds)

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Full-suite wall | 314s | **~195–210s** |
| Aggregate import cost | 3005s | ~1200–1300s |
| Failing files | 2 (env-dependent on dev machines; green on CI) | same 2, no new failures |
| Unhandled rejections | occasional (better-auth init race) | 0 |

CI: lint job ~2.5–3 min, each test shard ~2–2.5 min, all parallel — the lint+test critical path drops from ~11.5 min to **~3 min**.

## Required-check follow-up (repo admin, after merge)

Add **\`Backend Unit Tests\`** (the gate job, not the per-shard names) to the main-branch ruleset's required status checks. The workflow already runs on \`merge_group\`, and the gate uses \`if: always()\` so it always reports. Do this **after** this PR merges — adding it before would block other open PRs that don't have the job yet.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs)

- \`ai\` SDK mocks (9 chat/agent files): converting to the boundary means emulating provider SSE stream wire formats in the suite's most complex tests — deliberately excluded from this PR.
- \`@/models\` mocks (11 files) should become real-PGlite tests.
- Product edge surfaced here: message "delete subsequent" ordering uses a strict \`createdAt\` comparison — two messages created in the same millisecond tie and the later one survives.

author: heridotlife
body:
## Bug fixes (reported)

**1. Mobile admin: tapping the burger menu logged you out.**
The closed slide-out menu was hidden only with `opacity-0` + transform, so it still received taps. Translated up by its own height, its invisible full-width **Logout** button sat exactly on top of the nav bar and intercepted taps meant for the burger button. The closed menu is now `pointer-events-none invisible`, with a component regression test.

**2. Blog: creating a draft appeared to not save.**
Drafts *were* saved to D1, but `getAllPublishedPosts` ignored the `status` option and hardcoded `WHERE isPublished = 1` — so the admin list could never show a draft, even on its "draft" tab. The query now honors `status` (`'all' | 'draft' | 'published' | 'archived'`, public listings unchanged), selects the `status`/`isPublished` fields the admin cards render, and the admin `GET /api/blog/posts` defaults to `'all'`.

## Improvements (full P1–P4 from the project review)

### P1 — redirect hot path no longer defeats its own cache
- Clicks used to **evict the URL's KV cache entry** and **await the D1 write before the 302**, making every redirect of an active URL a cache miss + blocking write. Clicks now leave `urlLookup` alone and the write runs via `ctx.waitUntil` after the redirect.
- The URL/category admin routes built a **raw `D1Helper`**, bypassing cache invalidation (masked by click-eviction). Now on `CachedD1Helper`, with an invalidating `toggleShortUrlActive` override.

### P2 — security
- **KV-backed login rate limiter** (5/5min/IP in the `SESSION` namespace) — the in-memory limiter was per-isolate on Workers.
- **Astro-managed CSP** (`security.csp`): SSR pages get hashes for Astro's hydration scripts; the middleware splices the per-request `'nonce-…'` into `script-src`. **`script-src` now has no `'unsafe-inline'`** — resolves the standing middleware TODO. Verified across `/`, `/admin/login`, `/categories`, `/blog` that every inline script is nonce- or hash-covered.
- Removed the deprecated `X-XSS-Protection` header and the `/api/analytics/vitals` no-op endpoint + its client beacon.

### P3 — cleanup
- Deleted dead `src/lib/prisma.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, `tailwind.config.mjs`.
- RESTful `/api/admin/categories/[id]`, removed the phantom `authorId` and the `getSession(context as any)` cast.

### P4 — migrations, tests & CI
- **`wrangler d1 migrations`** adopted: `migrations/0001_baseline_schema.sql` (idempotent snapshot), legacy SQL archived under `migrations/archive/`, `db:migrate*` scripts rewired.
- **Component tests** (first React coverage): `BlogPostForm`, `BlogPostsPage`, `CategoriesPage`.
- **Integration tests** (real D1+KV): cache-invalidation semantics, `KVRateLimiter`, draft→publish transition.
- **E2E smoke** now seeds local D1 via migrations and grew 4 → 12 checks (`/blog`, `/categories`, 302 fallback, auth-guard redirect, sitemap, RSS, search API, hardened headers).
- **CI coverage step is now gating** (was `continue-on-error`); thresholds 85/85/80/85, current ~94%.

## Dependency updates (folds in Dependabot #212 + #213)

Rather than merging the two open Dependabot group PRs separately, their bumps are applied here and the lockfile regenerated (which also pulls the transitive `parse5` bump).

Production (#213): `@astrojs/cloudflare` 14.0.2→14.1.0, `astro` 7.0.4→7.0.5, `lucide-react` 1.22.0→1.23.0, `vite` 8.1.2→8.1.3, `parse5` 7.3.0→8.0.1 (transitive).
Dev (#212): `@cloudflare/workers-types` →4.20260702.1, `@types/node` 26.0.1→26.1.0, `sharp` 0.35.2→0.35.3.

The e2e build+boot run (below) is what validates the Astro/adapter bump against routing and CSP regressions.

## Summary

- APNs (`api.push.apple.com`) requires HTTP/2; `requests` speaks only HTTP/1.1
- Every push call was failing with `ConnectionError: BadStatusLine` (APNs sends back an HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame that `requests` can't parse)
- Replaced `import requests as http_req` with `import httpx` in `_send_apns()` and switched to `httpx.Client(http2=True)` — also changed `data=` to `content=` per httpx's API
- Added `httpx[http2]==0.28.1` to `requirements.txt` (`h2` package provides the actual HTTP/2 support)

This was the root cause of the Sentry `PYTHON-FLASK-R` error: `ConnectionError: ('Connection aborted.', BadStatusLine(...))` triggered whenever a push notification was dispatched.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI build passes
- [ ] `_send_apns()` no longer errors in Sentry after merge + Railway deploy
- [ ] Verify a push arrives on device after invite acceptance (the action that triggered the original error)

author: sauersml
body:
### Motivation
- Device CSR construction previously allowed creating a `DeviceCsrMatrix` with a `rowptr` buffer whose length did not equal `rows + 1`, enabling an invalid-free / out-of-bounds deallocation hazard.

### Description
- Add a `DeviceCsrError` type and a checked constructor `DeviceCsrMatrix::new(...) -> Result<Self, DeviceCsrError>` that rejects `rowptr` lengths not equal to `rows + 1` and uses `checked_add(1)` to avoid overflow surprises.
- Make `DeviceCsrMatrix` fields private and expose read-only accessors `rows()`, `cols()`, `rowptr()`, `colidx()`, and `values()` so callers cannot bypass the invariant with struct literals.
- Re-export `DeviceCsrError` from the `gam-gpu` module so callers can handle construction failures.
- Update the regression test to construct CSRs via `DeviceCsrMatrix::new`, assert that an invalid `rowptr` returns `Err`, and assert that a valid CSR preserves the `rowptr.len() == rows + 1` invariant.

### Testing
- Ran `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/gam-target-csr timeout 600s cargo check -p gam-gpu`, which completed successfully (exit 0).
- Attempted to run the targeted integration test via `cargo test -p gam --test regressions <...>::device_memory_representations_guard_against_invalid_csr_and_double_free_style_states`, but the run could not complete in this environment due to the Cargo target/artifact directory being locked by earlier build activity; the test was updated to exercise the new constructor and its error path.

author: grazuc
body:
The stock silero_vad.onnx cannot be loaded by OpenVINO. read_model fails with "The input data tensor's rank has to be known (static)" on the Conv ops inside the If subgraphs, as reported in #705. The graph has one top level If for the sample rate plus 7 nested If nodes per branch left behind by TorchScript tracing, so folding the sample rate constant alone is not enough.

This PR adds examples/openvino with a conversion script, a verification script and a README. convert.py inlines every If by evaluating its condition empirically with onnxruntime, removes the dead branch including its weights (2.27 MB to 1.23 MB), folds Identity nodes (recent OpenVINO serializes them as opset16::Identity, which older CPU plugins cannot execute) and fixes static shapes. It supports both sample rates through a --sr flag. The result loads and compiles in OpenVINO directly, as ONNX or exported IR.

One finding worth flagging on its own: on bf16 capable CPUs the OpenVINO CPU plugin defaults to bf16 inference, and for this model the per chunk error compounds through the recurrent state until the speech segmentation actually changes (measured up to 3e-1 max abs diff on real audio, against 2e-6 with f32). The README documents setting INFERENCE_PRECISION_HINT to f32, which costs nothing for a model this size.

Validation, with chained state throughout, against the stock model at commit dbacf53 (sha256 1a153a22f4509e292a94e67d6f9b85e8deb25b4988682b7e174c65279d8788e3). In onnxruntime the converted model is bit exact for both sample rates, so the transformation is the mathematical identity for the chosen rate. In OpenVINO with f32: max abs diff 2.3e-06 at 16 kHz on tests/data/test.wav plus examples/c++/aepyx.wav (229 seconds, 7161 chunks) and 4.5e-06 at 8 kHz on examples/c++/aepyx_8k.wav, with identical speech segmentation in all cases (29/29, 65/65 and 79/79 segments). Reproduced on Linux and Windows across two OpenVINO versions.

How to test:

```
cd examples/openvino
pip install numpy onnx onnxruntime openvino
python convert.py
python convert.py --sr 8000
python verify.py silero_vad_16k.onnx ../../tests/data/test.wav "../c++/aepyx.wav"
python verify.py silero_vad_8k.onnx --sr 8000 "../c++/aepyx_8k.wav"
```

verify.py exits nonzero unless the onnxruntime comparison is bit exact and the OpenVINO segmentation matches the stock model.

Caveats: each converted model is single sample rate with batch fixed to 1 (batch 1 is validated exhaustively, larger batches are not), and IR files should be regenerated with the target OpenVINO version, or the cleaned ONNX loaded directly with read_model.

Closes #705. Also relevant to the export format discussion in #706. Happy to move or rename things to whatever layout you prefer.

`scanText`'s scattered-invisible floor used a hand-rolled counter that mirrored only the EMOJI carve-out (VS16-on-pictograph, emoji-sequence ZWJ) of `src/invisible.mjs`. The stripper's real carve-out (`countPayloadInvisible`) also preserves linguistic ZWNJ/ZWJ (cursive joining, virama half-forms) and VS15 text-presentation selectors. The mismatch meant a ZWNJ-dense Persian doc (30 ordinary words), a virama+ZWJ-dense Devanagari doc, or 30 text-presentation hearts (`❤︎`) tripped the "scattered invisible chars (possible threshold evasion)" finding on content `stripInvisible` fully preserves — a false positive, plus a scan/clean incoherence (`cleanFile` rewrote a byte-identical file while returning `true`).

Fix: count the scatter floor with the exported `countPayloadInvisible` SSOT instead of the local mirror (net −60 lines of duplicated carve-out logic). Precision-preserving direction only: recall on genuine payloads (non-pictograph-anchored VS16 runs, dangling joiners, scattered ZWSP) is unchanged and still pinned by the existing "STILL flags" tests.

The bug was found by a new semantic-correctness fuzz harness: unlike the existing structural property tests (never-throws, shape), it interleaves known-benign constructs with known-payload runs/scatter units and asserts each specific token's exact fate (finding count, order, line, charCount, method, decoded).

## Changes

- `src/instructions.mjs`: replace `countInvisibleForScatter` (emoji-only mirror) and its helper regexes with `countPayloadInvisible` from `./invisible.mjs`; update the scatter-floor comment.
- `test/instructions.test.mjs`: three deterministic pinning tests — Persian ZWNJ-dense doc, Devanagari virama+ZWJ-dense doc, VS15-heart-dense doc all yield zero findings.
- `test/instructions-semantic-fuzz.test.mjs` (new): fast-check precision fuzzing — (1) random benign/payload interleavings must produce exactly the payload findings, byte-exact decodes and line numbers; (2) the scattered charCount must equal exactly the planted scatter units, unmoved by benign joiner/selector density (this generator reproduces the pre-fix bug reliably; `size: "max"` is required, the default array size never reaches the threshold boundary).

- New fuzz suite fails on pre-fix source (verified via `git stash`) and passes post-fix.
- `pnpm test` (1283 tests, 100% stmt/branch/func/line coverage), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check`, `npx prettier --check .` all pass; `FC_REPRODUCIBLE=1` seed run green.

author: daniboomerang
body:
## Summary

Herald's home page (`/`) crashed on a hard refresh with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'displayName')` inside animate-ui's `Slot` component. Worked fine on client-side navigation, only broke on fresh SSR load — the signature of a React Server Components boundary issue.

Root cause: `LandingPage.tsx` has no `'use client'`, so it's a Server Component. The `<NextLink>` JSX it authors inside `<Button asChild>` gets RSC-serialized before reaching the client-side `Slot` primitive, which needs to introspect `children.type` directly -- that introspection is what crashes.

Three commits:
1. Defensive children-filtering in the wrapper layer (`components/interactive/button.tsx`) -- doesn't address this specific crash (LandingPage always passed exactly one valid element), but is harmless, reasonable hardening for a different failure mode. Keeping it.
2. `'use client'` on `LandingPage.tsx` -- the actual fix.
3. `turbopack.root` anchored in all 6 Next.js apps (herald, vada, atta-ai, attalabs, vitakka, aeg studio) -- a separate, real bug found while testing fix #2 from a worktree: Turbopack auto-detects workspace root by walking up for a lockfile, and a worktree checks out its own copy of `bun.lock` alongside the main checkout's, so it can silently pick the wrong root -- corrupting module/env resolution for the whole dev server (confirmed: DB queries and Clerk middleware failing under the misdetected root). Same fix, same reasoning, across every app.

No `Closes #N` -- found live during manual testing, not a planned task.

## Test plan

Test Plan: unit-tests-only

- Repeated hard refreshes of `/` in a real browser, both UI fixes applied -- no Slot/displayName error across many reloads (previously reproduced on every refresh).
- `turbopack.root` fix verified directly: ran the dev server from a worktree, confirmed the "multiple lockfiles" warning is gone from the startup log, and the DB/Clerk errors it was causing no longer reproduce.
- `bun run check` green locally (typecheck + biome + tests) across all three commits.

## Scope

`packages/ui/libraries/animate/components/interactive/button.tsx`, `apps/herald-ai/web/src/components/portal/LandingPage.tsx`, and `next.config.ts` in all 6 Next.js apps (herald-ai, vada-ai, atta-ai, attalabs, vitakka-ai, aeg/web/studio).

**Tier:** 0 -- pure bug fixes, no new documented behavior or contract change.

Doc-waiver: .claude/skills/ui-library-system/SKILL.md — the `components/interactive/button.tsx` change is defensive children-filtering inside the existing wrapper pattern the skill already documents; no new pattern, API, or convention introduced.

body:
## What this is

Full-stack Cloudflare deploy path for the read-only 3G sandbox wireframe (follow-up to the merged POC in #1).

```
Browser ─▶ Cloudflare Pages (React UI)
              │ /api/*
              ▼
      Cloudflare Worker ─▶ https://shipdlx-sb.3gtms.com   (SANDBOX ONLY)
      (dlx-tms-sandbox-wireframe)   read-only: loadList / orderList
```

## Why a session cookie in prod

A Cloudflare Worker can't run Playwright, so live data uses an injected **`TMS_SESSION_COOKIE`** secret. `skills/3g-tms-browser/refresh_session.py` (Playwright login, **read-only**) rotates it; the Worker returns `401` when the session expires so the operator knows to re-run it.

## Changes

- **`cloudflare/worker.js`** — live direct-sandbox path via `TMS_SESSION_COOKIE`, CORS + preflight for the Pages origin, expired-session → `401`. Production still refused; read-only allow-list unchanged.
- **`cloudflare/wrangler.toml`** — `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` var + same-origin route notes.
- **`skills/3g-tms-browser/refresh_session.py`** — emits the sandbox session cookie for `wrangler secret put`.
- **`frontend`** — `VITE_API_BASE` makes the proxy origin configurable (`.env.example`); same-origin `/api` by default.
- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** — builds the frontend and deploys Pages + Worker on push to `main` (cookie stays out-of-band).
- **`DEPLOY.md`** — end-to-end runbook.

## Guardrails preserved

| Constraint | How |
|-----------|-----|
| Sandbox only | Worker refuses production `TMS_ORIGIN`; frontend never calls 3G directly |
| Read-only | Worker allow-lists only `loadList`/`orderList`, rejects write verbs |
| Isolation | Separate Worker `dlx-tms-sandbox-wireframe` — never the B.R.A.T. prod Worker |
| No repo secrets | Session cookie + Cloudflare token are secrets set out-of-band |

## Verified here

- Frontend builds clean with the new `VITE_API_BASE`.
- `worker.js` passes `node --check`; smoke-tested all guard paths: `health→worker-live`, CORS preflight `204`, production refusal `403`, unknown route `404`, unconfigured `500`, missing `savedQueryId` `400`.
- `refresh_session.py` compiles.

## Deferred (needs Cloudflare creds + sandbox egress)

The actual deploy and the first cookie refresh must run where those exist — this build environment blocks egress to `shipdlx-sb.3gtms.com` (403) and has no Cloudflare credentials. All config/build/lint steps are verified; only the live push-button is the operator's to run per `DEPLOY.md`.

author: itpick
body:
Two workflows (\`test-images-kind\`, \`test-images-charts\`) already used \`cachix/install-nix-action@v31\`. The other eight still ran a hand-rolled retry loop against \`curl … https://nixos.org/nix/install | sh\` that:

- took ~22s per job (vs. ~7s for the cachix action — pre-cached tarball, no daemon-setup blocking),
- silently continued (\`exit 0\`) if all three attempts failed, then downstream steps no-op'd via \`env.NIX_INSTALLED == 'true'\`. **Real install failures were invisible** unless someone read the logs.

## Change

- Swap the \`Install Nix\` step for \`cachix/install-nix-action@v31\` in the remaining 8 workflows so we're on one installer everywhere.
- Keep the \`NIX_INSTALLED=true\` env-var (via a tiny follow-up step) for compat with the two callers that still gate downstream steps on it.

## Wall-clock savings

~15s per matrix leg. With ~20 images per typical \`build-containers\` run × 3 test workflows + build-and-push, roughly ~90s off each run's critical path.

## Behavior change

If \`cachix/install-nix-action\` fails, the job fails fast (no silent-swallow retry). This is the correct behavior — before, an install failure just made all downstream steps skip and the job passed green with nothing built. Now you'll see the real error.

## Not in this PR

- Nix binary cache (\`nix-community/cache-nix-action\` etc.) — would let closures survive across jobs via GHA cache. Bigger speedup than the installer swap alone but more knobs. Follow-up if this lands cleanly.

Related: #413 (skip GHCR push on PR — independent, no conflicts).

author: johnisag
body:
## #17 — Manifest shortcuts + Web Share Target

**Long-press the installed Stoa icon** → app shortcuts for **New Session / Fleet Board / Ask Stoa / Live Wall**. And the **OS share sheet** can now send text/URLs *into* Stoa — share an article/issue/error from any app, and Stoa opens the New Session dialog pre-filled with it.

### How it flows
- `share_target` POSTs `title/text/url` (form-encoded) to **`/share`**, which composes a prompt and **303-redirects** into the app shell as `/?action=new-session&prompt=…` (GET fallback supported).
- The app's **first-ever URL handling**: a mount-only reader (ref-guarded against StrictMode double-invoke) parses `?action=` via a **pure grammar** (`lib/share-intake.ts`, zero imports) and dispatches to the same handlers the keybindings use — then `history.replaceState` strips the query so a reload can't re-fire.
- A shared prompt seeds the New Session dialog via a `promptSeed` prop (applied on open, cleared on close — never clobbers user edits).

### Security posture
- **/share is stateless**: nothing stored, so the necessarily-unauthenticated share endpoint can't write anything.
- **Relative `Location`** (RFC 7231): the redirect is never derived from `request.url`, so a spoofed Host header can't steer it anywhere — and it keeps working on every host Stoa serves from (localhost, LAN IP, **Tailscale**).
- **User-confirmed intake**: a crafted link/share can only open a *pre-filled dialog* — the user reviews and clicks Create before anything runs. The red-team explicitly cleared prompt-injection-by-link, header injection/response splitting, CSRF via the 303, SW precache interception, and history leakage.
- Unknown `?action=` values **drop to a plain app open**; prompts clamped to 4k chars.

### Platform notes (documented in ROADMAP)
Shortcuts: Android + desktop + iOS 15.1+. `share_target`: Android/ChromeOS/desktop — iOS Safari cannot receive shares (its users get shortcuts + Ask Stoa). Images deferred; text/URL is the core loop.

### Verification
- `tsc`, `npm test` (**2660 tests**, incl. 11 new for the pure grammar), `npm run build` (new `ƒ /share` route compiled), surface-guard — green.
- **4-agent adversarial review**: simplicity + red-team **CLEAN**; conventions nits (effect-deps style) applied; the one raised "Host-header open redirect" was **mooted with the relative-Location hardening** (the suggested hardcoded-origin fix would have broken Tailscale access). Round-2 verification runs on the committed code.

author: eiei114
body:
## Summary

Fix the double-trigger pattern in release automation. Previously, a single version bump on `main` could fire **four** concurrent publish attempts via:

1. `push: tags` — tag push from auto-release
2. `release: published` — GitHub release creation
3. `workflow_run` — Auto Release workflow completion
4. `workflow_dispatch` — explicit `gh workflow run` from auto-release

Now one release produces exactly one publish run.

## Changes

- **`auto-release.yml`**: Remove the explicit `gh workflow run publish.yml` dispatch step. The tag push already triggers `publish.yml` via `push: tags`.
- **`publish.yml`**: Remove `workflow_run` and `release: published` triggers. Keep only `push: tags` (canonical automatic path) and `workflow_dispatch` (manual trigger).

## Reference

- Successful publish run: `28547477139` (`workflow_dispatch`)
- Failing sibling run: `28547482506` / job `84636340169` (`workflow_run`)
- Both target commit `b9b6a20589ae502c3c21e39965e5aa1ca27200f3`

Multica Issue: DOT-496

---

## 確認シナリオ

### 操作手順
1. このPRをマージする（`main`ブランチへのプッシュがトリガー）
2. `Auto Release`ワークフローが実行され、新しいバージョンタグが検出された場合にタグ作成＋リリース作成を行う
3. タグプッシュにより`Publish to npm`ワークフローが**1回のみ**トリガーされることを確認
4. 重複した`Publish to npm`実行（`workflow_run`由来の赤い失敗）が発生しないことを確認

### 期待結果
- 1回のバージョンリリースにつき、`Publish to npm`は**1回だけ**実行される
- 成功したpublishの後に重複した失敗実行が残らない
- 既存の`npm publish`の重複防止ロジック（`Skip already published version`ステップ）はそのまま維持

### 確認コマンド
```bash
# Actionsタブで該当ワークフロー実行を確認
# Publish to npmワークフローが期待通り1回のみ実行されていることを確認
```

### 注意する失敗パターン
- マージ後に複数の`Publish to npm`実行が同時に発生した場合 → 本修正が不足している証拠
- `workflow_run`トリガーがまだ残っている場合は削除が必要

## Why

"Ensure Monnify can create a NUBAN, I can fund it, and VTU works" — these are live-key paths that can only be proven against the real gateways. This adds two browser self-tests (same pattern as `/wema-diagnose`) so each step is verifiable in one URL, with the exact provider error surfaced when something's off.

## What it does

**`GET /monnify-diagnose?token=...`**
1. Config + **OAuth login** (proves `MONNIFY_API_KEY`/`SECRET_KEY`/`BASE_URL` are right)

**`GET /vtu-diagnose?token=...`**

Both accept `DIAG_TOKEN` **or the existing `WEMA_DIAG_TOKEN`** — no new env var needed.

author: rbisecke
body:
## What changed

- `apps/api/app/ai/usage.py` (new): `write_llm_usage()` async helper that inserts one row into `llm_usage` and swallows/logs any write errors so they never surface to the user
- `apps/api/app/ai/rag.py`: `hybrid_retrieve` now returns `(chunks, max_rrf_score)` instead of `chunks` alone; `max_rrf_score` is the top-ranked document's combined RRF score (0.0 when the corpus has no matches); `embed_ms` is logged at DEBUG level
- `apps/api/app/routers/coach.py` (`_do_stream`): Anthropic streaming is now inlined using `raw.messages.stream()` so `get_final_message()` is accessible after the stream closes; system prompt now carries `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` (matching the blocking `/chat` path); TTFT and total duration are measured and passed to `write_llm_usage`; non-Anthropic backends and stub mode keep the existing delegation path
- `apps/api/app/routers/coach.py` (`chat`): updated `hybrid_retrieve` call site to unpack the new tuple
- `apps/api/tests/test_rag.py`: updated two tests to unpack `(results, max_score)` and added an assertion that `max_score` equals `results[0]["score"]`

## Why

Stage 2 of the metrics and admin portal effort. The `llm_usage` table (created in Stage 1) needs data — this wires up the write path for every real streaming interaction.

Inlining the Anthropic stream rather than delegating to `stream_llm_tokens` is necessary because `get_final_message()` must be called inside the `async with raw.messages.stream(...)` context manager; the existing helper function consumes the stream and exits the context before the caller can call it. Non-Anthropic backends don't expose an equivalent, so they keep the existing delegation path.

The `write_llm_usage` call happens after writing `coach_interactions` but before yielding the `done` event, so all three writes are part of the same psycopg transaction and commit together when the FastAPI dependency is cleaned up. Errors in `write_llm_usage` are swallowed to guarantee they never delay or break the SSE response.

Cache prompt caching was already active on the blocking `/chat` path but missing from streaming — this adds it so both paths get the ~10× cheaper cache-read pricing on repeated system prompts.

author: michaeljosiah
body:
## What

Implements **[Spec 051](docs/specifications/051.ingredient-costing-standard-cost.html)** — effective-dated ingredient costing and the product **standard-cost rollup** (food cost / COGS), composing the Spec 050 recipe explosion. Stacked on #165 (base = `feat/spec-050-ingredient-recipe-bom`; this diff shows only 051).

Includes a grounding commit aligning the spec to the landed 050 code (required `EffectiveFrom`, tenant-first index keys, `decimal(19,4)`, landed DTO names, withhold-total-when-incomplete, backdate guard).

## Cost model (the #164 Codex fixes, implemented)

- **Date-aware resolution**: current cost = the row where `EffectiveFrom <= atUtc AND (EffectiveTo IS NULL OR atUtc < EffectiveTo)`. `IsActive` is a soft convenience flag, never the selector.
- **Scheduled (future-dated) costs**: `SetCostAsync` with a future `effectiveFrom` closes the current row **at that boundary** — reads keep returning the old cost until the date arrives (tested via explicit `atUtc` and TestClock advance across the boundary; half-open `[From, To)` semantics).
- **One open row** per (TenantId, IngredientId, Currency), DB-enforced: filtered unique index `WHERE [EffectiveTo] IS NULL` + service invariant test.
- **Backdate guard**: an `effectiveFrom` before the open row's start would rewrite resolvable history → rejected (equal = same-instant correction, zero-widths the prior row).

## Rollup

`RollupStandardCostAsync(variantId, currency, atUtc?)` = Spec 050 `ExplodeAsync(variant, 1 portion)` × date-aware current costs:
- Per-component breakdown (`QuantityPerYieldUnit`, `UnitCost?`, `LineCost?`, `HasCost`).
- Any component without a cost in the requested currency ⇒ `CostComplete=false`, **`UnitCost=null`** — never a partial sum, never a silent zero (the same failure class as 057's P1).
- No active recipe ⇒ `HasActiveRecipe=false` diagnostic. One currency per call; no FX conversion.
- Hand-computed test: jollof (yield 4: 1 kg rice + 0.5 kg tomato), rice ₦1,200/kg + tomato ₦800/kg ⇒ **₦400/portion**.

## Surface

- `PUT/GET /commerce/admin/ingredients/{id}/cost` (+ `/history`), `GET /commerce/admin/variants/{id}/standard-cost`
- Agent tools: `commerce_get_product_cost` (read) + `commerce_update_ingredient_cost` (**medium**, Spec 032-gated)

## Migration

`CommerceIngredientCosts` — EF-CLI-generated: exactly one `CreateTable` (`AnkIngredientCosts`) + the filtered unique open-row index + lookup index. Applied cleanly to the local dev DB.

## Verification

`dotnet build` 0 errors; `dotnet test Aonik.sln` — **1,836 passed / 0 failed** (11 pre-existing skips); 16 new tests across `IngredientCostServiceTests` + `ProductCostingServiceTests`; architecture guard (no Commerce↔Finance reference) still green.

Next in the stack: Spec 052 (raw-material inventory + reorder alerts).

author: evanda
body:
Closes #42. Part of #38 (M1/lane:deep).

## Summary

Folds fuel drain/regen into the shared, framework-free `stepShip` (plan D4, dialectic B1) and sweeps every `ShipState`-construction call site to supply the newly-required `fuel` field.

## Exact new shapes

```ts
// packages/shared/src/physics.ts
export interface ShipState {
  pos: Vec2;
  vel: Vec2;
  angle: number;
  fuel: number; // NEW — required (not optional), per dialectic B1
}

export type ShipPhysicsConfig = Config["ship"] & {
  worldSize: Config["world"]["size"];
  maxFuel: number; // NEW — raw, already-effective number the caller supplies
};
```

`thrustFuelPerSec`/`fuelRegenPerSec` need no new config-slice field — they already flow through via the existing `Config["ship"]` intersection member. Only `maxFuel` is new (it isn't a `CONFIG.ship` key; `CONFIG.ship.baseFuel` is the un-upgraded base, `maxFuel` is the effective/upgrade-folded ceiling the caller computes).

## `stepShip` fuel logic

- `input.thrust && state.fuel > 0` → apply thrust acceleration (unchanged) **and** drain `fuel -= thrustFuelPerSec * dt`.
- `input.thrust && state.fuel <= 0` → **no thrust acceleration** (AC4) — rotation (`left`/`right`) and drag/coast continue exactly as before, so the ship isn't frozen, just can't accelerate.
- `!input.thrust` → regen `fuel += fuelRegenPerSec * dt` (independent of level).
- Clamp to `[0, maxFuel]` in all cases. All fuel math is `* dt` — frame-rate independent, same convention M0 established for drag/thrust.
- `fireFuelCost` stays inert (no combat until M4); left a comment flagging that M4 must reuse this same `fuel > 0` gate + drain rather than invent a parallel mechanic.

## Call-site sweep (confirmed complete)

Grepped the whole repo for `ShipState`/`stepShip` (excluding `dist/`/`dist-ts/` build output, which regenerates):

1. **`packages/client/src/scenes/GameScene.ts`** — the only client construction site:
   - Added `fuel: CONFIG.ship.baseFuel` to the ship's initial `ShipState` literal in `create()`.
   - Added a `maxFuel` getter to `makeLiveShipPhysicsConfig`'s live config-slice object, reading `CONFIG.ship.baseFuel` for now. **Explicitly not T8's job here** — T8 will later swap this getter's body to `effectiveShipStats(owned, CONFIG).maxFuel` once the scene holds real `OwnedUpgrades` state. No economy/upgrade/pickup logic was added to this file — just the minimal fuel field + getter needed to keep the build green.
2. **`packages/client/src/entities/Ship.ts`** — holds/forwards a `ShipState` but never constructs one itself (its constructor takes `initialState` from the caller). No change needed; confirmed by reading the file.
3. **`packages/shared/test/physics.test.ts`** — all 11 pre-existing `ShipState` literal construction sites updated to include `fuel` (mostly `fuel: 100`, i.e. full tank, chosen so unrelated tests aren't confounded by drain/regen side effects). The shared `shipConfig` test fixture gained `maxFuel: CONFIG.ship.baseFuel`. The "sustained thrust never drives speed above maxSpeed" test (30s of continuous thrust) got its own `unlimitedFuelConfig`/`fuel: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` so it isn't confounded by running out of fuel mid-test — that test is about the velocity clamp only, not fuel.
4. No server-package usage of `ShipState` exists yet (M3 territory).

## New tests (`packages/shared/test/physics.test.ts`, new `"fuel"` describe block)

- Thrust drains fuel at `thrustFuelPerSec`, verified frame-rate independent (60×dt=1/60 vs. one dt=1 step converge to the same total drain).
- No-thrust input regenerates fuel at `fuelRegenPerSec`, same frame-rate-independence check.
- **AC4**: at `fuel = 0` with thrust held, velocity does not increase — checked both from rest (stays exactly zero) and from a moving state (matches pure-coast exactly, proving thrust contributes nothing). Also confirms rotation and drag/coast still function at 0 fuel (not frozen).
- Fuel clamps to `[0, maxFuel]`: doesn't go negative under a large forced drain, doesn't exceed max under sustained regen (200s simulated).

## Test evidence

```
npm run typecheck   # clean across client/server/shared
npm run build       # clean across client/server/shared
npm run test        # shared: 68 passed (was 63; +5 new fuel tests, physics.test.ts 10→15)
                     # client: 109 passed, unaffected
npm run lint        # clean, exit 0
```

- `fuel` folded into `stepShip` rather than a separate `stepFuel` (plan D4's chosen option): the out-of-fuel case gates the thrust branch itself, so they couple at exactly one point — threading between two functions would be clumsier than one step.
- `maxFuel` is a raw number in the config slice, never derived from upgrades inside `physics.ts` — consistent with `effectiveShipStats` (T2, `upgrades.ts`) being the sole place that knows about upgrade tiers (plan D6/B2). This repo's ordering constraint (T3 must not depend on T2 types) is satisfied: `physics.ts` has no import from `upgrades.ts`.

## Out of scope (flagging, not doing here)

- Actually deriving `maxFuel` from `effectiveShipStats(owned, CONFIG)` in `GameScene.ts` — explicitly T8's job once real upgrade-ownership state exists in the scene.
- Any HUD/fuel-gauge rendering — T6/T8 territory.

body:
## Changes

- Resolve a dated `newVersion` to its numeric base version before formatting, preserving the current value's format:
- numeric current (`13`) → `13` (equals current → no update)
- codename current (`bookworm`) → `trixie`

## Context

Reported in discussion https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/discussions/42443

<details>

<summary> Explanation </summary>
Debian's Docker images now publish dated tags such as `trixie-20260406`. These sort greater than a plain numeric tag like `13` (same major, plus a date component), so lookup selects the dated tag as `newVersion`.

`getNewValue` then fell through to `getVersionByCodename("trixie-20260406")`, which returns the string unchanged (a dated codename is not a registered codename). 

Resulting in a user pinned to `debian:13` was rewritten to `debian:trixie-20260406`, and one tracking `bookworm` would get `trixie-20260406` instead of `trixie`.

</details>

author: artiz
body:
## Summary
First slice of the HTML browser-render subsystem (MIGRATION §5): **key-value form regions**, detected **statically** — no headless browser. An element classed `form_region` whose descendants carry docling's `keyN` / `keyN_valueM` / `keyN_marker` `id`-convention becomes a `field_region` of `field_item`s (marker/key/value), ordered by key number.

This closes `kvp_data_example`: the Markdown now matches docling's groundtruth **exactly**, apart from the pre-existing, deliberate table-padding divergence (MIGRATION §4) and the trailing-newline convention.

## Key Changes

**Core (`fleischwolf-core`)**
- `Node::FieldRegion { items: Vec<FieldItem> }` + the `FieldItem { marker, key, value }` struct (all `Option`).
- **JSON**: new `field_regions` / `field_items` collections. Emitted **only when a document has form fields**, inserted in docling's slot (just before `pages`), so every non-KVP document's JSON stays byte-identical to before. Field parts serialize as `marker` / `field_key` / `field_value` texts with the correct parent/child refs.
- **Markdown**: the region and each item render as `<!-- missing-text -->` (they carry no text of their own), followed by the item's parts as separate paragraphs — matching docling.

**HTML backend (`fleischwolf`)**
- `detect_field_region` fires from the `div`/`section` default arm: requires the `form_region` class **and** `keyN` descendants, so it anchors on the tight container (never swallows the whole page) and leaves a plain `form_region` (or the items `<table class="form_region">`) as ordinary content.
- `parse_kvp_id` parses the `keyN` / `keyN_marker` / `keyN_valueM` id convention.

## Scope / deferred
- **Not** using a headless browser — kept to the repo's pure-Rust, no-runtime design for declarative formats. The remaining subsystem items (nav/visibility suppression in `wiki_duck`, rendered nested-table cell geometry) genuinely need a rendered page and are left as follow-ups; MIGRATION §5 is updated accordingly.
- The KVP **JSON** matches docling structurally (region/item/labels/children); the one remaining delta is the region's `parent` ref (`#/body` vs docling's `#/texts/1`), which is the pre-existing "HTML doesn't nest content under headings" divergence — orthogonal to KVP and a larger, separate change.

Also bundles a small docs commit: moving the "TableFormer is done" note from MIGRATION's out-of-scope list into the README Status section.

## Testing
- New unit test `form_region_becomes_key_value_fields` (region/item markers + split parts, and that a plain `form_region` stays ordinary text).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`, and the full `cargo test` suite (incl. the all-format regression harness) pass. Regenerated fixtures are limited to the 3 `kvp_data_example` files — no other fixture drifted.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR aligns the SDK's configuration loader with existing documentation and CI workflows by implementing support for the `IMEDNET_STRICT_MODE` and `IMEDNET_TIMEOUT` environment variables.

### Why these changes are necessary
Currently, the SDK references these variables in its documentation, but the configuration loader ignores them. This discrepancy results in:
* **No-op Settings:** Users attempting to tune request behavior via the environment (e.g., increasing timeouts for high-latency staging environments) find the settings have no effect.
* **Misleading CI States:** Integration tests intended to enforce strict data integrity were silently passing because the "Strict Mode" toggle was non-functional.
* **Reduced Trust:** Discrepancies between documentation and behavior create friction for developers integrating the SDK.

### Key Changes

#### 1. Configuration & Environment Parsing
* Updated `packages/core/src/imednet/config.py` to include `timeout` and `strict_mode` in the core `Config` dataclass.
* Enhanced `load_config` to map environment variables using existing parsing utilities. 
    * `IMEDNET_TIMEOUT` is parsed as a numeric value (defaulting to `30.0`).
    * `IMEDNET_STRICT_MODE` uses a `parse_bool` utility to ensure consistent boolean evaluation.
* The finalized `strict_mode` state is exported back to `os.environ` to ensure deep-nested models can access the toggle without architectural bloat.

#### 2. Network Client Integration
* Modified `packages/core/src/imednet/sdk.py` to pass the resolved `config.timeout` to the `ClientFactory`. This ensures the underlying `httpx.Client` correctly respects the timeout configured via either code or environment.

#### 3. Strict Data Validation
* Updated the `_detect_drift` logic in `packages/core/src/imednet/models/json_base.py`.
* **Default behavior:** Extra fields in API responses trigger a logged warning (relaxed validation).
* **Strict behavior:** When `IMEDNET_STRICT_MODE=true`, the SDK now explicitly raises a `ValueError` when unexpected data is encountered, ensuring data integrity during testing and critical production workflows.

### Constraints & Validation
* **Backward Compatibility:** Maintained existing defaults (30s timeout, relaxed validation) if variables are unset.
* **Type Safety:** Used existing validator utilities to handle malformed environment strings gracefully, preventing SDK crashes on invalid input.
* **Testing:** Verified behavior across the existing test suite and manually validated edge cases in REPL environments to ensure proper `TypeError` handling for invalid variable types.

Lessons from dogfooding loopkit to author a curriculum in parallel. `examples/gates/` already had the LLM-judge/mechanical two-oracle kit (with a fully fail-closed `review.sh`) + the bash-3.2 gotchas, so this adds only what that didn't already cover.

**`examples/gates/README.md`**
- **Calibrate a gate before trusting it** — green-on-known-good + red-on-injected-breakage; a matcher that finds *nothing* is a false-green (assert it checked something); keep only universally-true checks as hard failures, demote judgment calls to warnings or the rubric.
- **An offline gate can't see rendered/runtime correctness** — exercise the artifact (render-and-diff, boot-and-hit) or lean on the held-out reviewer + a human.

**`docs/USING-ON-YOUR-REPO.md`**
- A **"parallel on one machine (git worktrees)"** recipe + gotchas: `run` switches the current branch even on `--dry-run`; a fresh worktree/clone lacks *gitignored* files (symlink or track; `protected_paths` is git-diff-based); a gitignore directory pattern ≠ a symlink → trips `require_clean_tree`; gates should grade the **workspace via `cwd`**; shared-file merge conflicts; size the budget for >1 tick.

author: sauersml
body:
### Motivation
- The degeneracy guard treated an exactly-constant Gaussian response (zero variance) as an "effectively constant" numerical failure and rejected it before orchestration could apply the well-posed constant-fit shortcut.
- The intended behavior is that an exact zero-variance response should flow to the constant-fit shortcut (intercept = constant, all smooths shrunk to zero) while only non-zero near-constant numerical dust should be rejected to avoid unstable REML evaluations.

### Description
- Relax `ResponseFamily::validate_response_degeneracy` in `crates/gam-spec/src/lib.rs` so exact-constant responses pass validation by early-returning `Ok(())` when `min_y == max_y` (i.e. all `y` equal). 
- Tighten the near-constant rejection condition to `if sample_sd > 0.0 && sample_sd <= GAUSSIAN_MIN_SAMPLE_SD` so only non-zero tiny sample SDs are refused pre-fit.
- Update accompanying documentation to clarify that `GAUSSIAN_MIN_SAMPLE_SD` targets positive near-constant numeric dust and that exact constant responses are a well-posed degenerate limit handled by orchestration.
- Adjust the unit test to assert that an exactly-constant Gaussian response passes `validate_response_degeneracy` (test renamed to reflect the new contract).

### Testing
- Ran `cargo test -p gam-spec gaussian_degeneracy --lib` and all tests passed (5 passed); the exact-constant and near-constant cases behave as intended.
- Ran `cargo test -p gam --test perf_scale misc::large_scale_accuracy_sweep::edge_all_same_y_yields_constant_prediction` and the targeted perf-scale test passed, verifying the end-to-end constant-fit shortcut.
- A subsequent full workspace build was blocked by a pre-existing repository ban-scanner gate (oversized tracked file) unrelated to this change and did not affect the focused tests above.

author: ajr0703
body:
Adds read_full/write_all helpers (introduced in section 4) to eliminate partial read/write bugs when sending data over TCP sockets, and introduces per-request handling on the server side.

Changes:

- read_full: loops on read() until exactly n bytes are received (or fails on EOF/error), preventing truncated reads on partial TCP delivery.
- write_all: loops on write() until exactly n bytes are sent, preventing partial writes.
- Client (query) : sends messages using a 4-byte length prefix + payload framing, then reads and parses the response using the same framing. Sends three sequential requests (hello1, hello2, hello3) over one connection.
- Server (one_request): reads a single length-prefixed request, logs it, and writes back a length-prefixed "world" reply. The accept loop now calls one_request repeatedly per connection until the client disconnects or an error occurs, instead of handling only one message per connection.

author: hashbender
body:
## Problem
When `dashboard.basic_auth` is the only configured provider, every unauthenticated HTML page load produces an HTTP 500 error. The sequence:
1. User hits `/` while logged out
2. `_auto_sso_response` sees exactly one session provider (BasicAuth) → returns a 302 redirect to `/auth/login`
3. The `/auth/login` handler calls `start_login` on BasicAuthProvider
4. `BasicAuthProvider.start_login` **raises `NotImplementedError`** because password-only providers have no OAuth/SAML redirect flow
5. The unhandled exception surfaces as HTTP 500

## Root Cause
`_auto_sso_response` unconditionally included all session-capable providers as auto-redirect candidates. Password-only providers (`supports_password=True`) — specifically BasicAuth — have no redirect-based login flow, so redirecting to their login endpoint crashes.

## Fix
Filter out password-only providers from the auto-SSO candidate list. When the only session provider is password-based, `_auto_sso_response` returns `None`, allowing the normal `/login` password form to render instead of attempting an impossible redirect.

## Verification
Applied and verified on a live deployment:
- Login page now renders at `/login` instead of crashing
- Password-based login with valid credentials succeeds
- Wrong password returns proper 401
- No regression for OAuth/SAML providers (the filter only removes `supports_password=True` providers)

author: vincentsmedinga
body:
# Describe the pull request

## What

Hardens three CI workflows against shell script injection through the branch name:

- `deploy-acceptance-storybook.yml`
- `remove-acceptance-storybook.yml`
- `check-visual-regressions.yml`

Each one now passes `github.head_ref` / `github.ref_name` through an `env` variable and references it as a quoted shell variable, instead of interpolating the `${{ … }}` expression directly into a `run` block.

## Why

`${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}` is expanded by GitHub into the script text *before* the shell runs it. Because Git allows characters like `$`, `(`, `)` and backticks in branch names, a pull request from a branch named e.g. `$(id)` turned the deploy step into `RAW_BRANCH_NAME=$(id)`, which the runner then executed — arbitrary command execution on a job that carries `contents: write` and `deployments: write` permissions.

This was reported to us as a responsible security disclosure. While the value now flows through the environment, the same branch name arrives as literal data and is never executed.

`check-visual-regressions.yml` had the same pattern in a second spot (`echo "branch=${{ github.head_ref }}"`) that wasn’t in the original report; it’s fixed here too.

## How

- Moved the interpolation into an `env` block (`RAW_BRANCH_NAME` / `HEAD_REF`).
- The `run` blocks now read the quoted shell variable, so command substitution can’t fire.
- In `remove-acceptance-storybook.yml` this also removes a redundant re-derivation that was overwriting the workflow-level env var.
- Quoted `"$GITHUB_ENV"` / `"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` on the touched lines as hygiene.

No behavioural change: the derived branch name is identical for any valid branch.

## Checklist

- [x] Add or update unit tests <!-- n/a: CI workflow change -->
- [x] Add or update documentation <!-- n/a -->
- [x] Add or update stories <!-- n/a -->
- [x] Add or update exports in index.\* files <!-- n/a -->
- [x] Comment `/chromatic test` and verify visual regression tests pass
- [x] Start the PR title with a Conventional Commit prefix, [as explained here](https://github.com/Amsterdam/design-system/blob/main/documentation/publishing.md?plain=1#L11).

## Additional notes

- The same injection pattern exists in sibling repositories flagged in the same disclosure (`design-system-prototypes`, `design-system-community-roadmap`, `ee-ads-rhf`, `amsterdam-schema`); those are tracked separately and are out of scope for this PR.
- Recommend adding `actionlint`/`zizmor` to CI to catch this class of issue automatically in future.
